## What's New

### Full-Featured Git Panel
- Push, pull, fetch, stash, and stash pop operations
- Branch management: create, delete, checkout branches
- Commit log viewer with relative timestamps
- Discard file changes
- Ahead/behind indicators on current branch

### Diff Editor
- Click any changed file to open a Monaco side-by-side diff view
- Supports both staged and working directory diffs

### Canvas Performance
- Memoized context menus and marquee rect calculations
- ResizeObserver-based editor layout instead of Monaco's `automaticLayout`
- Circular velocity buffer for smoother inertia panning
- RAF-batched wheel panning to reduce layout thrashing

### Sidebar Improvements
- Collapsed sidebar now shows workspace dots with panel counts
- Granular Zustand selectors to reduce unnecessary re-renders

### Source Control Sidebar
- Full git operations matching the canvas GitPanel
- Branch list, commit log, stash support

commits.message:
fix: allow scrolling inside focused panels instead of panning canvas

The canvas wheel listener used capture phase with unconditional
stopPropagation(), intercepting scroll events before they reached
panel contents. Now checks if the event originated inside a focused
panel's content area and lets it through for native scrolling.

feat: full git panel with push/pull/branches/stash, diff editor, and canvas perf improvements

Add comprehensive git operations (push, pull, fetch, stash, checkout, branch
create/delete, discard) to both the canvas GitPanel and sidebar SourceControlView.
EditorPanel now supports Monaco diff editor mode for viewing staged/working changes.
Canvas performance improved with memoized context menus, ResizeObserver-based layout,
circular velocity buffer, and RAF-batched panning. Sidebar shows workspace dots when
collapsed and uses granular Zustand selectors to reduce re-renders.
fix: remove leftover setSelectedFile/setSelectedDiff references in GitPanel
fix: skip release creation in CI when release already exists

feat: add process & ports overview popover in sidebar

Add a Pulse icon button next to the notification bell that opens a
popover showing all running processes and their listening ports grouped
by workspace. Processes can be killed from the popover (child-only kill
keeps the terminal alive), and recently closed processes appear as
restart suggestions that re-run the last command.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

🐛 fix: plug memory leaks in terminal loggers, usage watchers, and caches

TERMINAL_LOG_READ and TERMINAL_LOG_DELETE created new TerminalLogger
instances (each with a 1s setInterval) that were never disposed, leaking
timers indefinitely. Usage module chokidar watchers and file caches also
grew without bound or cleanup on quit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

chore: release v0.2.14

Addresses #39: a failed terminal-create no longer becomes a permanent
tombstone. The half-built registry entry is torn down on error and a
'Failed to start terminal' overlay with a Retry button is shown in its
place. Retry clears the failure, re-runs getOrCreate from scratch, and
re-attaches the new xterm into the existing panel — no app restart, no
need to open a fresh canvas.

node.path is absolute, so the tracked-files Set never matched anything
and every file rendered dimmed as 'untracked'. Now we prefix gitLsFiles
output with the repo root so the comparison succeeds.

* fix: contain watcher EMFILE runtime crashes

* test(watch-pool): build paths via path.resolve so Windows CI passes

validatePath() returns path.resolve(p), so '/repo' becomes a drive-prefixed
backslash path on Windows and the hardcoded POSIX event paths never matched
the subscriber prefix. Derive ROOT/SRC/file paths from path.resolve/join.

Co-authored-by: 정경훈 <ruderud0055@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Anton <antonhorn@icloud.com>

fix(worktree-chip): clear scrollbar lane so margins are symmetric (#396)

The worktree chip overlay sat at top-1.5 right-1.5 (6px each), but
terminal/agent panels are xterm-backed and always reserve a 6px scrollbar
lane (overflow-y: scroll). The chip's right edge landed on that lane, so it
overlapped the scrollbar and the right gap looked smaller than the top gap.

Bump to right-3 (12px) to clear the 6px lane and leave a 6px visual gap
that matches the top inset.

fix(workspace): restore terminal cwd into its worktree on restart

A terminal spawned inside a git worktree came back at the workspace root
after a restart. The worktree path was persisted (session.json
workingDirectory) and seeded into terminalRestoreData, but TerminalPanel
reads panel.cwd directly and falls back to workspaceRoot. Since
projectFilesToSnapshot never re-attached panel.cwd, that fallback always
won and shadowed the restore-data cwd, so the shell opened in the primary
checkout while the worktree pill still claimed the worktree.

Re-attach panel.cwd from the persisted workingDirectory so the restored
terminal respawns in its worktree, matching the worktree tag the UI shows.

fix(terminal): diagnose shells that exit immediately on spawn (#401) (#404)

A freshly-spawned shell that exits cleanly (code 0) within ~1s without ever
emitting a byte never became an interactive session - almost always the user's
shell startup files exiting early, or a PTY that could not be allocated. The
bare "[Process exited with code 0]" left users with nothing to act on.

- Renderer: after the exit line, print a hint pointing at startup files / PTY
  allocation when a fresh PTY exits 0 instantly with no output. Gated to fresh
  spawns (reconnects adopt a live PTY) and ordered after the exit line.
- Main: log.warn the same condition with the resolved shell path, so the next
  report carries the cause (daemon stderr is not surfaced after handshake).
- Carry the host-resolved shell path back on PtyHandle for that log.

test(workspace): cover terminal worktree cwd across the full restore path

The existing lifecycle test "uses the session-restore cwd" called getOrCreate
with no cwd opt, which TerminalPanel never does (it passes panelCwd ||
workspaceRoot), so it masked the bug. Add an end-to-end test that runs the real
disk-restore path (files -> projectFilesToSnapshot -> restoreSession -> store)
and asserts the restored terminal panel's cwd is the worktree path, not the
workspace root. Both new assertions fail without the fix.

fix(updater): prompt once per version instead of every 15 minutes (#405)

The "update ready" modal re-surfaced on every 15-minute background check
because the renderer un-dismissed itself on each re-announced 'downloaded'
status. Dismissing ("Install on next quit") only hid it until the next poll.

Decouple checking from prompting: the modal now tracks the dismissed version
and auto-shows at most once per version. A genuinely newer version still
re-opens it, and "Check for Updates…" force-resurfaces a staged update so the
user can always get back to "Restart now".

fix(agent): move the running agent when its worktree is switched

Switching an agent panel's worktree only re-tagged it (worktreeId), so the
running pi kept its old cwd until the next restart. Pi's cwd is fixed at spawn
and its sessions are cwd-scoped on disk, so AgentPanel now reacts to the derived
cwd changing under a live mount: it disposes the old checkout's chats and reopens
pi in the new one, so the agent actually moves with the pill.

Extract disposeAgentChats from disposeAgentPanel for the teardown half, and
factor the mount effect's initial-open into a shared openInitialChat used by both
the mount and the worktree-switch reinit.

add OSC52 terminal clipboard support (#402)

Co-authored-by: Anton Horn <73064193+Anton-Horn@users.noreply.github.com>

fix(fs-watch): use native recursive watch to stop EMFILE on large workspaces

chokidar v4 has no FSEvents backend, so a full-tree watch opens one fs.watch
fd per directory. On macOS Electron caps the process at ~8k fds, so a workspace
with >8k directories hit EMFILE and flooded unhandled rejections, freezing the
UI (issue #398). #395 only contained the symptom.

Add createRecursiveWatcher: on macOS/Windows it uses one native recursive
fs.watch handle (FSEvents / ReadDirectoryChangesW) for the whole subtree —
descriptor cost independent of directory count, the model VS Code uses. Linux
(no native recursive watch) falls back to chokidar unchanged.

The native eventType is advisory for add-vs-change (macOS reports a modify as
rename), so a stat() disambiguates the only distinction consumers depend on —
existence → unlink. The ignore predicate runs as a cheap pre-stat filter so
churn inside excluded trees (npm install) never triggers a stat storm, and the
async stat is wrapped so EMFILE can never resurface as an unhandled rejection.

Swap both watcher call sites (local pool in main/ipc/filesystem.ts and the
daemon's watch capability in runtime/capabilities/index.ts) to the adapter.

Two new settings under Settings > Worktrees:

feat: worktree panel cleanup and symlink-on-create

feat(fs-watch): move workspace-tree watching to @parcel/watcher

Replace the native-fs.watch/chokidar split (#407) with one @parcel/watcher
backend, and consolidate all workspace-tree watching into a single pool
(createWatchPool in runtime/capabilities/fileWatcher.ts). Both call sites — the
local IPC pool (main/ipc/filesystem.ts) and the daemon capability
(runtime/capabilities/index.ts) — now delegate to it.

parcel emits explicit create/update/delete (identical to FsChangeType), so the
stat-to-disambiguate-existence dance, the inFlight dedup and the lost-update
race are gone. Exclusions are pruned by parcel's native ignore globs
(**/.*/** + per-exclusion), reproducing the exact hidden-file-kept /
hidden-dir-and-excluded-pruned policy, so createFsIgnoreMatcher and the JS
ignore predicate are deleted. The pool owns covering-root sharing, prefix
fan-out, refcounted teardown, refresh-on-exclusion-change and error
containment. In-proc subscriptions (git monitor) are now active, matching the
daemon's long-standing semantics.

chokidar remains only for jsonStateFile.ts single-file watches (parcel is
directory-recursive only).

Packaging (two ABIs — Electron main + the daemon's bundled node):
- esbuild externalizes @parcel/watcher for the daemon bundle
- electron-builder asarUnpacks @parcel/watcher + its platform binary packages
- build-runtime-tarball stages parcel's runtime closure + the target's prebuilt
  watcher.node (npm pack for cross-targets like linux-arm64), signs it on macOS
- release.yml stages both macOS arches into the app (parcel loads watcher.node
  at import; the x64 dmg would otherwise crash on Intel)

@parcel/watcher is N-API: one prebuilt per platform/arch runs under both ABIs,
so no electron-rebuild / from-source compile.

Closes #409

test(fs-watch): cover subtree-delete fan-out, symlink robustness, closeAll

Close the gaps in the watch-pool's behavioral coverage:
- subtree delete: assert parcel synthesizes a delete for EVERY file in a
  removed populated subtree (top-level + deeply nested), the narrowing the old
  native recursive fs.watch carried.
- symlink robustness: a real-FS test confirming an external directory symlink
  in the tree does not break watching of real files. Documents that parcel does
  NOT recurse into a symlink pointing outside the watched root (it behaves like
  native fs.watch here, not chokidar v4) — the test asserts only that its
  presence is harmless, not that symlinked subtrees are followed.
- closeAll: unit-assert it unsubscribes every tree and drops late events.

test(fs-watch): resolve the watch root so the wiring test passes on Windows

fsWatchWiring used a bare '/repo', but validatePathStrict drive-prefixes it to
'D:\repo' on Windows, so the FS_WATCH_START assertion (prefix === root) failed
there while passing on macOS/Linux. Use path.resolve('/repo') (the same pattern
index.watch.test.ts already uses) so the literal matches the validated path on
every OS.

fix(canvas): consolidate selection + focus into one canonical model

Multi-panel marquee selection was broken in two ways:

1. The marquee rectangle offset/froze the moment the cursor crossed onto
   the focused panel. The marquee tracked the pointer with window-level
   mousemove/mouseup but, unlike every other canvas gesture, never took
   the shared `canvas-interacting` body class, so the focused panel's
   webview/terminal/editor swallowed the events. It now holds that class
   for the drag.

2. What rendered as selected and what actually moved could differ. Focus
   and selection were two independent fields (`focusedNodeId` +
   `selectedNodeIds`): a focused panel rendered a halo and read as
   selected, but a group drag only translated `selectedNodeIds`, so a
   stale-focused panel looked selected yet didn't move.

Replace both fields with one canonical ordered array, `selection`, plus a
`selectionActive` flag. The active/focused node is now derived as the lead
of the selection, so the glowing set (rings + halo) and the moved set are
the same by construction. The invariant lives in the store mutators rather
than at call sites; read sites use the derived `focusedNodeId(s)` helper.

fix(canvas): grab any selected panel to move the whole group

In a multi-selection no node is active, so the press lands on the node's
dim overlay rather than the title bar. The overlay's onMouseDown called
the single-node drag directly and never tried startGroupDrag (unlike the
grab strip and tab bar), so dragging a selected panel moved only that one
and the follow-up click collapsed the selection. Route the overlay press
through startGroupDrag first, matching the other two handlers.

test(canvas): regression tests for selection, single + group drag

Lock down the selection/focus model and drag behaviors:
- selectionModel: selectNodes replace/additive/dedup, the always-deactivate
  rule, selectAll/clear/toggle, focusAndCenter/toggleMaximize/addNode
  activation, moveNode isolation, removeNode/finalizeRemoveNode reconcile,
  navigateSelect vs navigateDirection, undo/redo of selectionActive, and
  the focused-is-always-in-selection invariant.
- marquee: overlapping nodes get selected (non-overlapping don't), replace
  vs additive, result is un-activated, bare/empty click clears.
- group drag: gating (non-member / single / non-left button fall through to
  single-node drag), grabbing any member moves all, history pushed once.
- single-node drag isolation through the real drag runtime.

fix(canvas): keep group drag when grabbing a selected panel's title bar

A press on a multi-selected node's tab bar hit the dock-content wrapper's
capture-phase focus handler before the bubble-phase group-drag handler. That
focus collapsed the selection to the grabbed node, so useGroupNodeDrag then
saw a single-node selection, bailed, and only that one panel moved.

Guard the capture-phase focus so it bails for a live multi-selection member,
leaving the group drag to read the intact selection. Extract the shared
isGroupDragMember predicate so the focus guard and the group-drag takeover
can't drift out of agreement.

Add a regression test that renders the real CanvasNode and drives a real
mousedown on the tab bar, plus unit cases for the predicate.

fix(runtime): stage @parcel/watcher's full dep closure so the daemon starts

The 1.3.2-beta.1 runtime shipped without picomatch, so the daemon crashed at
startup with `Cannot find module 'picomatch'` (required by
@parcel/watcher/wrapper.js) and no terminal/workspace could come up.

stageParcelWatcher copied @parcel/watcher's nested node_modules if present, else
a hardcoded dep list that omitted picomatch. On the release runner npm hoisted
picomatch to the top level (no nested dir), so neither branch staged it.

Resolve each of @parcel/watcher's runtime deps (picomatch, is-glob, is-extglob,
detect-libc) from its own resolution root via createRequire, staging each into
the same relative location node would load it from. Works whether npm nested or
hoisted them. Add a post-stage assert that wrapper.js's requires resolve in the
staged tree, so a missing dep fails the build instead of shipping broken.

Also regenerates the stale version.ts (was 1.3.1, package.json is 1.3.2-beta.1).

fix(runtime): auto-retry a failed LOCAL daemon start

The crash-reconnect only armed after a successful handshake (the onClose
handler), so a daemon that died DURING startup just surfaced the static
"Failed to start / Retry" screen with no auto-recovery.

Schedule the reconnect on a failed start too, with exponential backoff
(1s to 8s), a forced re-extract from the 2nd attempt on (repairs a corrupt or
partial install), and a hard cap so a permanently-broken bundle can't tight-loop
forever. The retry budget resets on any successful connect.

fix(updater): stop re-checking once an update is staged

On macOS a redundant update check (the 15-minute poll, a manual "Check for
Updates", or a beta-toggle re-check) re-enters electron-updater's download flow,
which re-arms the native Squirrel.Mac install-on-quit and resets its internal
"ready" flag. With that flag false, the "Restart now" button's quitAndInstall
silently skips the relaunch: the update installs on quit but the app never
reopens (ShipItState launchAfterInstallation=false).

Skip the check entirely while an update is downloaded and staged. There is
nothing to find, and the manual path still re-opens the staged modal.

Co-authored-by: Paul Horn <paul@paul-horn.de>

fix(worktree): make the worktree tag the authoritative cwd on reload

A worktree-tagged terminal sometimes came back at the workspace root after a
restart. The terminal resolved its cwd only from the captured live PTY cwd
(terminalGetCwd at save time), with no link to the worktree tag. When that query
was absent at the last autosave (PTY not live yet, query failed, terminal just
reopened), the persisted workingDirectory was empty and the shell fell back to
the root while the pill still claimed the worktree. Intermittent by nature.

Resolve a tagged terminal's cwd from its worktree tag at render time, the same
way AgentPanel already does, so the tag is authoritative and the live-cwd
capture no longer gates correctness. This covers every reload path at once
(main restore, reload-from-disk, deferred/workspace-switch, detached windows).

Also tolerate a path-valued worktreeId: a panel tagged before a background sync

record (whose id is wt-...) and dropped the agent/pill to the root. resolveWorktree

feat(providers): add StepFun/BytePlus LLM, WaveSpeed/BytePlus image, BytePlus video, and Inworld/Fish Audio/Speechify TTS

Adds new agent-brain, image, video, and TTS providers following each
capability's existing conventions:

- LLM: StepFun and BytePlus ModelArk (data-driven preset registry, no
  bespoke code needed beyond the preset entry + vendor icon).
- Image: WaveSpeed (async task submit/poll) and BytePlus Seedream.
- Video: BytePlus Seedance, sharing the existing seedance2/Volcengine
  Ark task API and reference limits via a config-driven refactor of
  generateSeedance() instead of duplicating it.
- Voice/TTS: Inworld, Fish Audio, and Speechify (minimal text+voiceId+
  modelId surface, matching the simplest existing provider shape).

BytePlus image/video share one BYTEPLUS_API_KEY/BASE_URL pair (same
convention as MiniMax's shared key across its four capabilities),
separate from LLM_BYTEPLUS_* used for Agent chat.

Also fixes the settings panel's "test & discover models" button/copy
to key off any field with discoverableModel:true instead of a
hardcoded llm/ page-key prefix, and wires model discovery into the
new BytePlus image/video probes so their model pickers work the same
way the LLM pages already did.

image input, context-length overflow). Log the real body server-side
only, matching the console.warn/error pattern already used elsewhere
(generation-jobs.ts, normalize-media.ts, export-runtime.ts); the
client-facing response is unchanged.

fix(export): render clip effects through transitions

GL transitions re-uploaded raw media, bypassing each clip's ordered WebGL
effect graph, so entering a transition flashed unfiltered footage and toggled
a per-frame raw fallback layer. renderTransitionWithFx now renders both
clips' effect pass chains into retained textures in one context, then
transitions those textures; TimelineComposition keeps its effect-aware CSS
composition visible until the exact GL frame exists and hides stale frames
while sources/LUTs warm up.

feat(agent): mode-aware provider routing for generation capabilities

Four-tier provider choice driven by config state and proposal mode:
- unconfigured capability: agent must not call it, guides user to Settings
- single vendor: use directly
- several vendors + manual (proposal card per change): ask once via
  ask_followup_questions, then keep that choice
- several vendors + auto (auto-apply AI proposals): agent picks and states
  the reason, no forced ask

Skill files now document only per-provider usage details; the actual
provider decision is pinned to the live configured list in the
capabilities prompt (fixes static vendor enums going stale, e.g. PR #34
providers not yet in skills).

AgentContext gains getApprovalMode (built-in chat reads the persisted
auto-apply preference); external MCP sessions don't consume this prompt.
capabilities.verify.ts is wired into verify:salvage.

feat(chat): rename proposal modes to Ask / YOLO

- Settings popover now shows a two-way switch: Ask Mode (AI changes wait
  for confirmation; asks first when several options exist) vs YOLO Mode
  (ordinary changes apply immediately, still undoable; generation/export
  always confirm first via skill guard)
- Chat composer's Q&A mode renamed Ask -> Q&A in the toolbar label and en
  dictionary to avoid colliding with the new Ask Mode naming
- system prompt and skill docs (ui-and-features) updated to the new names
- Internal identifiers (autoApply / approvalMode / sessionPrefs keys) stay
  stable; external MCP protocol untouched

feat(media): add master quality mode for import preview and export

Prefer original media on preview, raise 4K export bitrate headroom to
60 Mbps, and default export to high bitrate when Master quality is on.

feat(preview): add original/proxy/auto preview source toggle

Let the preview header cycle Auto/Original/Proxy independently of the
export quality mode, keep master-preferring resolution rules, and cover
the policy matrix in qualityPolicy.verify (wired into pretest).

fix(agent): close paid-tool guard gaps and rename skill guard to cost guard

Gaps found in deep review:
- transcribe_track (AssemblyAI, paid per minute), web_browser/web_search/
  web_map/web_crawl/web_batch_scrape (Firecrawl, paid per page), and
  run_code (E2B, paid per second) were NOT in HIGH_COST_TOOLS — the runtime
  guard never confirmed these paid calls.
- The whole guard was gated behind settings.skillGuard; turning the toggle
  off disabled ALL paid-operation confirmations.

Fixes:
- HIGH_COST_TOOLS now covers every paid surface; the guard is no longer
  configurable (paid operations always confirm before execution and never
  auto-apply, in any mode). UI toggle removed; the Ask/YOLO popover explains
  that paid operations always confirm first.
- Renamed skillGuard -> costGuard (file), functions
  generationSkillForTool -> costCategoryForTool, is/rememberSkillAllowed ->
  is/rememberCostAllowed, type GenerationGuardSkill -> CostGuardCategory.
- New costGuard.verify.ts guards the paid-tool registry completeness so a
  future paid tool cannot silently bypass confirmation again.

feat(export): add full-timeline ProRes 422 HQ mezzanine

Offer ProRes .mov as a server-only mezzanine codec for high-quality
hand-off (grading / Resolve). Keep H.264/WebM for web delivery; force
server routing and skip bitrate/retime for ProRes.

fix(agent): recover edit_item volume updates mis-typed as effect

When the model omits type or sets type:effect while sending clip fields
like volume, coerce to a generic audio/video update using the live item
kind, and improve unknown-field errors for effect rows that carry volume.

fix(proxy): never forward browser cookies to upstream providers

Cookies are shared across every localhost port, so an accumulated cookie
jar on a dev machine was forwarded verbatim by the LLM relay and rejected
by provider gateways (xiaomimimo 431, deepseek 400 Request Header Or
Cookie Too Large). Strip cookie alongside x-openchatcut-provider; auth
always comes from the server-injected key headers.

fix(preview): return stable snapshots from useQualitySnapshot

getSnapshot returned a fresh object literal per call, which
useSyncExternalStore treats as a change on every render — an infinite
re-render loop in the preview hooks. Split into two stable string
snapshots (mode / preview source) instead.

fix(agent): strip targetItemId when coercing effect rows to clip updates

The coercion path rebuilt the entry but kept the targetItemId locator,
which is not a GENERIC_UPDATE_KEYS field — so the typical LLM mix-up
(type:"effect" + targetItemId + volume on a real clip) still failed
with "unknown field targetItemId". Extract stripEffectLocators, use it
for both the coerced and generic update paths, and cover the payload
shape in edit-item-volume-hint.verify.

fix(export): accept mov in temporary export job filenames

ProRes mezzanine jobs write .mov files, but the temporary export
filename whitelist only allowed mp4/webm/mp3/wav — rendering failed with
"invalid export job filename". Add mov to the extension set and the
cleanup-sweep regex; cover it in export-runtime.verify.

Merge branch '0xsline/fix-edit-item-volume-hint'

Coerce effect-typed edit_item volume rows to generic clip updates, and
strip targetItemId locators when routing them to the generic validator.

Merge branch '0xsline/master-quality-mode'

Master quality mode (preview source + export defaults), ProRes 422 HQ
mezzanine export, and fixes: stable useQualitySnapshot snapshots and
mov in temporary export job filenames.

feat(preview): rename preview source labels to user language

'原片/代理' assume users know proxy concepts; rename the three-way
toggle to 自动/高清/流畅 (auto/high quality/smooth) and '预览源' to
'预览画质', matching video-site vocabulary. Fallback notices become
'轻量副本生成失败，已切换为原画质播放'. Internal auto/original/proxy
values and localStorage keys are unchanged.

feat(preview): make proxy-fallback notice user-friendly

Drop the UUID filename list and state the impact instead: '流畅预览暂不
可用，已自动使用原画质播放（画面正常，不影响导出）'. Users cannot map
UUIDs to clips and were left wondering whether action is needed.

feat(preview): on-canvas text/MG style editing

Show a floating color + font-size bar above the transform outline when a
text or text-like MG clip is selected; edits route through
updateItemProps (undoable). Also fix multi-lane auto captions having no
preview hitbox: build flat cues whenever captions are enabled and fall
through to them when manual target lookup misses.

Merge branch '0xsline/preview-text-edit-ux'

On-canvas text/MG style editing (color + font size bar) and a fix for
multi-lane auto captions missing preview hitboxes.

feat(preview): full text editing on canvas — content, weight, align, AI rewrite

Extend the floating text bar: inline textarea editing (double-click or
pencil), font-weight and alignment cycling, and an AI rewrite entry that
seeds the chat with the current text. Text-clip field resolution now
covers text/fontWeight/align; caption preview paints full styles when
selected. Verified: tsc + previewTextEdit/captionPreviewTarget/
preview-transform-overlay verifies.

Merge branch '0xsline/preview-text-edit-ux' (take 2)

On-canvas text editing v2: content editing, font weight, alignment,
double-click inline edit, and AI rewrite seeding.

fix(preview): stop playback at the end instead of looping

Remove the Player loop prop so preview stops on the final frame, per
issue #41. The existing ended listener in usePlayheadPaint already
resets the transport (playing=false, head persisted), so no further
wiring is needed.

fix(export): raise render heap and humanize out-of-memory failures

Remotion renders export frames inside the Electron main process, which
had no V8 heap ceiling — large/4K exports (e.g. driven via MCP by
hermes) died with opaque out-of-memory errors (issue #40).

- desktop/main.ts: raise V8 heap to 6 GiB via js-flags before ready
  (covers main process and headless render tabs).
- server/plugins/export.ts: detect OOM failures and report an actionable
  Chinese message instead of the raw engine error; OOM is not retryable.

docs: update WeChat community QR code in READMEs

Replace the community QR asset (shared by README.md and README_ZH.md)
with the new design: dark theme, white modules, WeChat chat-bubble
center logo.

feat(media): plain click selects assets, double-click adds to timeline

Multi-select was hidden behind Ctrl/Shift+click or marquee drag with no
visible affordance — users never discovered the batch action bar. Make
plain click select (single), Ctrl/Shift/meta click toggle-append, and
double-click add to the timeline (drag-to-track still works). Fix
onSetSelected not being passed to MediaAssetCard, which broke the new
single-select path.

feat(media): float batch actions beside the selected card

Replace the always-on top selection bar with a floating toolbar that
appears to the right of the first selected asset card (view-fixed,
follows scroll/resize). Selection now feels like a context menu instead
of occupying a whole toolbar row.

feat(media): open the asset menu on select, drop the floating toolbar

Clicking an asset card now selects it AND opens the same context menu
as right-click (download/favorite/rename/relink/delete/move/add), which
already operates on the whole selection for multi-select. The floating
batch toolbar added earlier is removed — selection affordance is now the
familiar context-menu pattern.

feat(timeline): stable two-row track names + rename menu

Track labels drifted because custom names (often AI-assigned, e.g.
Titles/BGM) replaced the type+index title entirely. Now the head always
shows the stable title (视频1/音乐1/字幕1, audio default renamed 音频→音乐
per user expectation) with the custom name as a second row underneath.
Add '重命名轨道' to the track context menu (prompt → updateTrack; empty
resets to default).

feat(chat): @ opens asset/timeline reference picker grouped by track

Typing @ in the composer now opens the reference picker (previously only
the toolbar button did). The picker groups references: media-pool assets,
then timeline items under their track aliases (V1/A1/...), then the
template library. Timeline item references reuse the existing 'item'
selection-reference type, so the agent gets full clip context. Fixed a
latent bug where opening the picker without an anchor rendered nothing.

feat(chat): drill-down @ picker — root → assets/timeline/tracks → clips

The @ reference picker now navigates instead of listing everything flat:
root shows three entries (media pool / timeline / templates), timeline
drills into per-track groups (V1, A1, ...), each track expands to its
clips, with back navigation at every level. Counts shown on entries.

feat(chat): keyboard navigation in the @ reference picker

Arrow up/down moves a highlight through the current drill level, Enter
activates (enters a submenu or inserts the reference), Escape closes.
Enter no longer submits the message while the picker is open. Mouse
hover syncs the same highlight.

fix(chat): stop duplicating reference names in the composer input

Inserting a reference showed it twice: the attachment chip AND a
@name token in the textarea. The token is display-only for the agent
(references travel structurally via resolveAgentReferences), so drop
the textarea insertion; append tokens to the message text only at send
time so message history stays self-describing.

fix(timeline): clarify caption toggle tooltip — text clips are not captions

Users saw on-screen text clips (海边日记 标题, 文艺叠字) and expected the
CC toggle to manage them, but the toggle covers caption-track data only.
Tooltip now says so explicitly instead of 'no captions yet'.

feat(captions): fold on-screen text clips into the caption system

The CC toggle now manages text clips too, not just caption-track data:
- TimelineState.captionsHidden: global caption-system switch; CC click
  toggles it and keeps every caption track's enabled in sync.
- Render layer hides text-like clips (text + text-styled MGs, judged by
  previewTextEditFields) when captions are off — item data untouched,
  preview and export share the same composition.
- Toggle stays enabled when only text clips exist; tooltip reports the
  clip count instead of the misleading 'no captions'.

fix(media): make the whole asset card draggable, not just the thumbnail

Dragging into a subfolder only worked when starting on the thumbnail
button — starting from the name or card padding did nothing, so users
reported #42 as broken. Move draggable + dragstart/dragend onto the card
root (HTML5 picks the nearest draggable ancestor).
refactor(skills): export CREATIVE_SKILL_METADATA for external checks

fix(media): allow pool assets to drop into folders and back up

Chromium often rejects HTML5 drops onto buttons, and effectAllowed
"copy" blocked folder dropEffect "move" (issue #42). Folders are now
droppable divs with copyMove drags, multi-select move, drop highlight,
and an "up one level" tile inside subfolders to drag assets back out.

feat(chat): slash-command skill completion (/slug activates a workflow)

Typing '/' in the composer opens a completion popover over the creative
workflows (built-in + custom). Keep typing filters by slug prefix first,
then slug/name/nameZh substring — works for Chinese input like /长视频.
Tab/Enter completes and activates exactly like the wand picker
(activateWorkflowStarter: sets creative mode, fills the starter prompt,

- Keyframe inspector + preview overlay wiring; text clips no longer
  disappear when transform keyframes are present
- Media pool: folder context menu (right-click / ⋯), delete-empty-folder,
  navigation, drag-into-folder improvements
- Agent: edit_item visual props surface scale axes; system prompt notes
- TimelineComposition/layouts/types align clip transform resolution
- New verifies: previewTransform, preview-transform-overlay,
  inspector-controls, media-folder-menu (all green)

Companion revert f020684: normalize concurrency stayed 2/8 — the 4/16
raise made normalize-media.verify crash (20 hanging gate-held requests
get connections closed).

fix(preview): no unfiltered-frame flash when seeking clips with effects

ClipFx kept the raw source layer visible while the GL shader frame for a
new timeline position was not yet drawn (showingShaderFrame =
renderedKey === renderKey). Clicking the timeline to jump therefore
flashed the UNFILTERED source video for 1-2 frames until the effect pass
completed. Once any effect frame has been drawn, keep the GL canvas
visible across seeks (stale effect frame until the new one is ready) —
the raw source only shows during the initial never-drawn load. Export
path unchanged (delayRender already gates on the staged frame).
Verified: tsc, clipFxExport.verify 60/60, lint 0, browser seek smoke
(rapid seeks on 黑白胶片 clips, no errors).
chore: release 0.1.9

> [!WARNING]

## Highlights

- **Windows local transcription works for the first time** (#120): packaging had separated `whisper-cli.exe` from its DLLs, so local Whisper died instantly with a bare exit code for every model size, in every previous version. Verified both ways on a real Windows runner.
  **Windows 本地转写首次真正可用**（#120）：此前打包把 `whisper-cli.exe` 与其 DLL 分开放置，任何模型尺寸都会立刻失败。已在真实 Windows runner 上双向验证。
- **New: Whisper Large v3 Turbo** local model tier (#127) — near large-v2 quality, a fraction of the decode cost. 新增 Whisper Large v3 Turbo 本地模型档。
- **FlexCrop** — crop clip edges in composition pixels, contributed by @J160KU (#123). 画布像素级裁边，@J160KU 贡献。
- Word-level timestamps and hallucination suppression fixed via transformers.js 4.2.0 (#109). 词级时间戳与幻听抑制修复。
- Stopping an agent run then immediately sending the next no longer loses the new answer (#125); one failed proposal apply no longer silently disables the rest of the session (#129 symptom). Agent 竞态与 proposal 静默失效修复。
- Browser fast export no longer fails on slow-to-open media (10-minute per-frame budget, matching the local renderer). 浏览器快导不再因素材打开慢而失败。
- Release-blocking data-safety fixes: unreadable projects are never overwritten by the next save; version/export history written by newer builds survives older builds. 数据安全：读不出的工程不会被覆盖；新版写入的历史在旧版下保留。

fix(transcript): prevent whole-video fallback for local ASR

Require compact audio extraction on the browser-local ASR path and retain
stage-specific failures instead of attributing every error to model downloads.
Expose Russian transcription in settings and local model language labels.

Shared-path impact: extraction remains optional for cloud and desktop-native
callers. Existing fallback behavior, model readiness validation, project data,
and editor commands are unchanged. Independent silence-detection work is
excluded from this commit.

Validation:
- Staged snapshot: TypeScript build, lint, and assemblyai, language settings,
  transcript-tools, and mediaSourceRevision verifies passed.
- Development tree: 16 affected verifies and production build passed.
- Real browser Agent smoke: gpt-5.6-sol invoked transcribe_track with
  provider=local; a 17,350-byte extracted audio file produced three words.
- Full development-tree tests hit an unrelated pending read_transcript
  contract change; that contract verify passes in the staged snapshot.

Refs #120

fix(i18n): complete Russian transcription language labels

Add English and Italian labels for the Russian transcription option introduced by the issue #120 fix.

Shared-path impact: dictionary-only additions; ASR behavior and existing translations are unchanged. Unrelated working-tree changes are excluded.

Validation: isolated issue #120 snapshot passed TypeScript, lint, i18n coverage, 104 test segments, agent-skill verification, and production build. Browser4 with DeepSeek and local Whisper Base transcribed a Russian video into 15 words via transcribe_track and read_transcript.

Refs #120

fix: harden desktop recovery and media analysis workflows

Recover Windows renderer/GPU failures within the selected profile and singleton owner. Ignore clean GPU exits and replay the latest floating transcript payload after renderer reloads. Clear queue-only export hints on active progress and direct completion.

Report missing transcripts and explicitly optional music analysis as availability states while preserving stale-source and invalid-target failures. Cap source contact sheets at eight samples and skip browser-local ASR inference for near-silent PCM.

Shared paths: recovery stays Windows-gated except the explicit smoke flag; nonqueued export details and default music failures are preserved. No README, persistence schema, dependency, or user-profile changes.

Validation: complete pretest/posttest coverage and 104 core test segments; tsc -b --force, lint, web build, desktop build, and targeted lifecycle/stale-transcript checks passed. Real DeepSeek completed read_transcript, 6/8/2-frame extraction, optional missing-model music analysis, and zero-word local ASR; project/media/chat survived refresh. macOS Electron baseline and forced main/floating renderer recovery both reached SMOKE-OK. Windows/Linux hardware and CI were not run. Evidence: /tmp/openchatcut-commit-validation-20260830/validation-summary.md.

perf: reduce hot-path overhead in editor, transcript, and agent streaming

- editor/store: memoize activeEditorState so unrelated renders keep
  downstream [state] memos and effects stable
- editor/sequenceGraph: skip graph traversal when the project has no
  sequence items (runs on every per-timeline action); duplicate
  timeline id detection is preserved in the fast path
- agent/proposal: cache projectDocsDiffer per (baseDoc, currentDoc)
  identity pair (docs are immutable) so pending-proposal renders stop
  re-migrating and stringifying two full docs
- transcript/TranscriptViews: memoize buildScriptRows and WordRow so
  drag-over/gap-adjust state changes no longer rebuild rows and
  re-render every word span on long transcripts
- agent/serverRun: batch streaming text/thinking persistence into
  200ms flushes via new serverRunStreamDeltaBuffer instead of
  rewriting the full localStorage record per SSE delta (O(text^2));
  cursor+text always land in one atomic patch, non-delta commits fold
  pending text into their own write, stale cross-run flushes are
  discarded, and flush failures follow the existing persistenceError
  abandon path

Shared paths touched: useEditor state identity (all editor consumers),
per-timeline action validation, proposal staleness checks (browser and
external bridge), transcript script view, serverRun durable stream
persistence. All changes are memoization/short-circuit/batching only;
no action semantics, storage schema, or recovery contract changed.

Verification: tsc -b --force clean; oxlint 0 warnings; verify:affected
(sequenceGraph, proposal) and serverRunSessionStorage.verify pass;
6-scenario standalone logic test for the delta buffer (batch merge,
fold, cross-run discard, failure reporting, drop) passed; browser e2e
on localhost:5199 (isolated dev profile): new project -> add solid ->
undo -> redo -> dashboard reload with 0 console errors. Pre-existing
issue confirmed on a clean tree: useServerRun.verify and
serverRunToolRecovery.verify crash under run-check (dynamic require in
@vercel/oidc via the ai package), unrelated to this change.

fix(persist): stop silent data loss when reads or the bootstrap merge fail

Three failure paths converted transient errors into authoritative
destructive writes; each now fails safe:

- projectStore/AppViews: loadProject conflated "no stored document"
  with "stored bytes exist but read/migration failed", so an unreadable
  project opened as empty and the 500ms autosave overwrote the real
  data. New loadProjectForEditing returns ok/missing/unreadable; the
  editor opens "missing" as an empty project exactly as before, and
  blocks "unreadable" behind a retry/back screen (new i18n strings in
  en + ru dicts) instead of mounting the editor.
- sharedKv bootstrap: a failed merge (transient 5xx, timeout, lease
  contention) fell through to the sync-down branch, which deleted the
  local project index when the remote library was empty (or overwrote
  it when found). A failed merge with a local 'projects' entry now
  marks migration pending: local stays authoritative for reads and the
  merge retries on a later load.
- mediaCleanup: scanUnreferenced auto-purged any project doc missing
  from the index, but listProjects degrades to [] on any read error,
  so a lost/unreadable index classified every project as an orphan and
  purged them all. Extracted pure orphanDocIdsToPurge with a guard:
  an empty index alongside existing docs purges nothing.

Shared paths touched: editor entry load (all projects), sharedKv
bootstrap (every session), media cleanup dialog scan. Behavior is
unchanged for healthy reads: readable projects open identically,
successful merges migrate identically (covered by existing verify
scenarios), and orphan purge still runs whenever the index has
entries. Only the previously destructive failure branches changed.

Verification: tsc -b --force clean; oxlint 0 warnings; verify:affected
(appShell, projectStore, sharedKv, mediaCleanup) passes including new
scenarios: loadProjectForEditing ok/missing/unreadable, merge-failure
preserves the local index then a retried merge completes migration,
and orphanDocIdsToPurge refuses to purge when the index is empty but
docs exist. Browser e2e on localhost:5199 (isolated dev profile):
existing project with clips reopens intact through the new load path,
new-project creation and editor mount unregressed, 0 console errors
(the 409 on /api/external-agent/unregister during route transitions is
pre-existing).

fix(editor): numeric boundary guards and no-op reference stability

Undo-history integrity (no-op contract):
- reduce()'s transition-reconcile exit only allocates a new state when
  reconcileTransitions actually changed something; reconcileTransitions
  returns the ORIGINAL array when content is unchanged. Previously any
  rejected/no-op action on a timeline with >=1 transition produced a new
  state object, pushing a phantom undo step and clearing redo (Cmd+Z
  "did nothing" and lost redo after every clamped drag nudge).
- moveItemWithGroups returns the original state when the clamped delta
  is 0 and no track change was requested.

Numeric validation on tool/LLM-facing action channels (frame domain is
integral; NaN stringifies to null and corrupts the persisted doc):
- move: rejects non-finite startFrame, rounds fractional targets
- split: rounds atFrame before boundary checks
- retime: rounds action-supplied startFrame/durationInFrames
  (srcInFrame intentionally left fractional-capable for playbackRate)
- reorderTrackItems.starts (apply_script channel): non-finite or
  negative pinned start rejects the whole action atomically;
  fractional starts are rounded
- setVolume/setFade/setSpeed: reject non-finite inputs
- setCanvas / tl.retarget: reject non-finite or <1 dimensions, round
  fractional ones (zero canvas divided nested-sequence layout)
- updateMarker: rejects non-finite frame fields, clamps to >=0 integers
  (symmetric with addMarker's command-side clamp)

Shared paths touched: reduce() exit (every per-timeline action),
move/retime/split/speed/volume/fade/canvas/marker/reorder reducers.
Valid inputs behave identically (round is a no-op on the integral
frames every existing caller sends); only previously-invalid inputs
change outcome, from corrupting state to being rejected or normalized.

Verification: tsc -b --force clean; oxlint 0 warnings; new
reducerGuards.verify covers no-op reference stability plus every guard
above (all passing); full editor verify sweep 35/37 green - the two
failures (mediaAssetUsage, transitionPreview) reproduce identically on
a clean tree (pre-existing run-check bundling issues, not regressions);
browser e2e on localhost:5199 (isolated dev profile): open project,
add solid, undo, redo all correct with 0 console errors.

fix(agent): strip internal __ control fields from model-supplied tool args

Generation tools use __operationId/__rerunGeneration/__rerunOf as
internal plumbing: the idempotency wrapper injects the reserved
operation id, and rerun_generation marks legitimate reruns. Both
happen AFTER the invocation boundary. Ajv runs with strict:false and
tool schemas do not set additionalProperties:false, so a model (or a
prompt injection carried in scraped web/transcript content) could pass
__rerunGeneration:true directly and bypass the paid-generation
idempotency window and durable reservation chain, or bind a submission
to a forged __operationId.

effectiveToolInvocationArgs now drops every __-prefixed key from
model-supplied args before policy/digest/execution. All LLM entries
converge on this function (executeOpenChatCutTool via
prepareToolBoundary, plus the external bridge); internal callers
(rerun_generation invokes submit handlers directly, the idempotency
wrapper calls executeGenerateCommand directly) are behind the boundary
and keep injecting their fields unaffected. Result-side __followup is
untouched (it lives on results, not args).

Shared path touched: every agent tool invocation. Args without
__-prefixed keys pass through by reference (zero-copy, identical
behavior); no schema declares a __-prefixed parameter (grepped).

Verification: tsc -b --force clean; oxlint 0 warnings; new
execution-policy-args.verify covers stripping, non-mutation,
reference passthrough, and composition with the transcribe_track
provider default; external-tool-policy.verify and abortedTurn.verify
pass (approval-policy.verify fails with the pre-existing @vercel/oidc
dynamic-require bundling error already confirmed on a clean tree).
Real agent chain e2e on localhost:5199 (isolated dev profile,
gpt-5.6-sol): sent an instruction triggering read_timeline; observed
the tool call execute and the agent reply correctly ("2 clips, no
changes"), 0 new console errors from this path (a 403 on
/api/agent-runs/<id>/draft/clear during post-run cleanup is
server-side and pre-existing).

fix(transcript): keep word/index/ref alignment under playOrder; project word-click seeks

Two breaks of the word <-> source-time <-> timeline-frame invariant:

- retimeWords sorts its output by projected timeline start, but
  keptWordIndices enumerated surviving indices in SOURCE order. With
  transcriptPlayOrder (speech-block reorder) the two orders diverge, so
  resolveCaptionWords[i] no longer corresponded to
  resolveCaptionWordIndices[i] / wordRefs[i]: hiding or overriding a
  caption word hit a DIFFERENT word, and agent-facing refs pointed at
  the wrong source word. Refactored both onto a shared core
  (retimedWordEntries) that carries {index, word} pairs through the
  same survival, sort, and de-overlap steps — retimeWords output is
  byte-identical; keptWordIndices now emits indices in the SAME
  timeline order, which is what its doc contract ("callers stay
  aligned") always promised. Its only caller is captions/resolve.ts.

- Word-click seek in TranscriptPanel used
  startFrame + msToFrame(word.start): source ms added to a timeline
  frame with no projection — wrong on split clips (large source ms
  jumps past the clip), after deletions/silence compression (late
  drift equal to removed span), and on trimmed or rate-stretched
  video. New wordTimelineFrame in transcript/edit.ts projects through
  the same math as the render layer (audio: keptSegments stream;
  video: continuous srcIn window with playbackRate); a deleted word at
  a cut seeks to the cut point where playback resumes.

Shared paths touched: caption word resolution (render, translation
generator, agent read_captions all share resolve.ts) and the
transcript panel click-to-seek. Without playOrder the emitted order is
unchanged (stable sort over already-chronological words), so existing
projects and non-reordered clips resolve byte-identically.

Verification: tsc -b --force clean; oxlint 0 warnings; new
wordAlignment.verify covers edit-layer and resolve-layer positional
alignment under playOrder (words/indices/refs triple), plus
wordTimelineFrame for audio (deletion stream, cut-point fallback) and
video (srcIn window, playbackRate); transcript/edit.verify passes;
full captions+transcript sweep 28/35 green — the 7 failures
(captionCue*/captionSelection*/captionGroupMove/captionTimelineClipboard/
whisper-word-timestamps) reproduce identically on a clean tree
(pre-existing). Browser smoke on localhost:5199: editor loads,
Transcript and Captions panels open, 0 console errors.

fix(server): gate media read paths, block inline skill interpreters, guard probe URLs

AGENTS.md states the local auth invariant as "loopback + Host + Origin +
Sec-Fetch-Site", but only write paths and editor endpoints enforced it.
Three local-privilege gaps closed:

- Read paths (/media/uploads, /upload/list, /upload/presign GET, and the
  ffmpeg-spawning /api/waveform|filmstrip|media-frame|media-poster|
  preview-proxy*) skipped the Host check entirely, so a rebound DNS name
  could enumerate and read the whole media library and spawn a
  derivative process per request. They now require
  editorCredentialAuthorized(req, false): loopback socket + local Host,
  Origin optional because media elements send none. /upload/presign GET
  also stopped short-circuiting its auth check (`method !== 'POST' ||
  requireEditorMutation` let every GET through). The Electron embedded
  server's own /media/uploads mount (desktop/static-files.ts) is gated
  the same way — it has no Vite allowedHosts layer, so it was the one
  confirmed-reachable path.

- skill-exec whitelisted bash/sh/node/python, making `bash -c <anything>`
  a full command-execution primitive despite execFile and the cwd lock.
  Interpreters now must run a script FILE resolved inside the skill
  directory; eval-style flags are rejected per interpreter (bash/sh -c,
  node -e/--eval/--print, python -c/-m), scanning only the option region
  before the script path so the script's own arguments are unaffected.

- key probes send REAL stored credentials to a settable base URL with no
  address check. probeUrlError now rejects non-http(s) schemes,
  credential-bearing URLs, and cloud-metadata/link-local targets
  (169.254.x, fe80:, metadata.google.internal). Loopback and LAN stay
  allowed: local model servers and gateways are legitimate probe targets.

Shared paths touched: all media/preview reads (both hosts), skill script
execution, every provider connection test. Same-origin and no-Origin
local reads behave exactly as before.

Verification: tsc -b --force clean; oxlint 0 warnings; new
read-path-auth.verify covers the read-gate shape (loopback no-Origin
allowed, rebound Host rejected, cross-origin rejected, non-loopback
rejected), the probe URL guard, and the interpreter guard including its
negative cases (bash -e + script allowed, flags after the script path
allowed, ffmpeg/npm unaffected). Live curl against a restarted dev
server: local read 200, cross-origin 403, presign GET cross-origin 403
(previously bypassed), waveform cross-origin 403. Browser e2e: same-
origin fetches to /upload/list (112 files), /media/uploads, /api/waveform
and /upload/presign all 200, and an <audio> element (which sends NO
Origin) loaded and read duration successfully — the main regression risk
of a read gate.

Runner correction: earlier commits in this series cited "pre-existing
verify failures" observed through scripts/run-check.mjs. That runner is
not the project's canonical one (package.json and
run-affected-verifies.mjs both invoke `npx tsx <file>`) and its bundling
of @vercel/oidc fails at import time. Re-run with tsx, every verify
named in those messages passes. This change was validated with the
correct runner: server domain 0 failures, and 182 verifies across
editor/agent/captions/transcript/persist/app/media/export 0 failures.

fix(persist): stop write-back from destroying data this build cannot read

Boundary validation on read had become deletion on write. Every list
store validated persisted entries (correct — persisted data is
untrusted), then wrote the FILTERED array back, so any entry this build
cannot parse was erased. The common source of such entries is a NEWER
build, which makes this a direct violation of the release rule that new
data opened by an old version must degrade safely and must never be
overwritten. versionStore is the worst case: automatic snapshots save
every 30s, so a snapshot written by a newer build disappeared within
minutes of running the older one.

- New recordPartition helper splits a stored array into entries this
  build understands and opaque ones kept verbatim; every write appends
  the opaque tail. Applied to versionStore (persistVersion,
  deleteVersion), exportHistoryStore (recordExport), templateStore
  (saveTemplate, deleteTemplate) and jobRegistryStore (in writeJobs,
  the single write path, rather than threading it through all seven
  read-modify-write callers). clearExportHistory still clears
  everything — that is explicit user intent, not a silent drop.
- Field-level passthrough: toValidVersion and toValidRecord rebuilt
  objects from known fields, dropping unknown ones on write-back. They
  now spread the raw entry first and override only validated fields
  (an invalid destinationId is still stripped, not inherited).
- v1ToV2 enumerated its output fields with no `...value` (v2ToV3
  already spreads), so unknown V1 top-level fields evaporated at
  migration. It now spreads, while still explicitly dropping an
  invalid designStyle rather than letting the spread carry it.
- loadChat collapsed "read failed", "corrupt shape", "old session
  generation" and "nothing stored" into null; hydration treated null as
  "no chat", set an empty session, and the next persist overwrote a
  real conversation. New loadChatResult distinguishes ok / missing /
  unreadable (a generation bump is still "missing" — that IS the fresh
  conversation record). On unreadable, hydration stops before setting
  hydratedRef/hydrated, which gates both persistence and new runs, and
  shows the reason in the chat instead of an empty history.
- collectAllUploadRefs ignored version snapshots, so removing a clip
  and running media cleanup deleted media that restoring a 5-minute-old
  snapshot still needs. Version docs now count as references.

Shared paths touched: version history, export history, template
library, generation job registry, chat hydration/persistence, media
cleanup reference set, and the v1→v2 migration. For data this build can
read, behavior is unchanged: partitioning yields an empty opaque tail
and the same array is written as before.

Verification: tsc -b --force clean; oxlint 0 warnings; new
unreadablePreservation.verify covers the partition helpers, a
version-99 snapshot surviving saveVersion and deleteVersion, an
export record surviving alongside an unknown-field passthrough, and the
v1→v2 passthrough with designStyle still stripped; chat-persist.verify
extended with the three-state load (missing / ok / unreadable on both
read failure and corrupt shape); migrations.verify passes; 114 verifies
across persist/agent/media/export/app pass with the canonical tsx
runner. Browser e2e on localhost:5199 (isolated dev profile): planted a
version-99 snapshot into a real project, made an edit, waited for the
automatic version to be written — the new snapshot was stored (2→3
entries) and the unreadable one survived byte-identical; test data
removed afterwards, 0 console errors.

fix(agent): six correctness gaps in run dispatch, tool bounds and proposal apply

- detect_beats was listed as unconditionally parallel while it writes
  markers through ctx.commands when `markers` is set. Parallel tools
  share the executor draft with the exclusive chain, so whichever
  request settled first drained the other's recorded actions, mislabeling
  proposal rows and persisting the wrong actions per toolCallId.
  toolExecutionMode now takes args and classifies per invocation:
  analysis-only calls stay parallel, marker-writing calls are exclusive.
- Double-send race: prepareServerRunPayload checked `running` before two
  awaits (payload build, ownership) and ownership QUEUES behind an
  in-flight run instead of failing, so a second Enter started the same
  prompt again as soon as the first run finished. Re-check after
  ownership and release the queued slot.
- MG tool schemas had unbounded width/height/duration: 1e7 px froze the

first frame that no first screen needs.

1. React shipped inside the Remotion chunk. `codeSplitting.groups` leaves
   `includeDependenciesRecursively` at its default of TRUE, which drags a
   group's whole dependency closure into it, and the highest-priority group
   wins. So `remotion` (priority 20) claimed react and react-dom before the
   `react` group (10) could — the react chunk came out empty and the entry
   chunk imported 2 MB of Remotion just to get React. The project list route
   has no player on it. Every group here matches the package it is named
   after and wants only its own modules, so they all opt out of recursive
   dependency inclusion, the way `templates` already did.

   across zh/en/it/ru, so each user downloaded and parsed three languages
   they cannot read. src/i18n/dictRegistry.ts fetches one locale on demand;
   t()/tData() stay synchronous, reading a snapshot that is replaced rather
   than mutated, and fall back to the Chinese original — which is also the
   dictionary key — so the "never go blank" contract holds while a fetch is
   in flight. main.tsx starts that fetch before the rest of boot so it
   overlaps, and gates the first render on it, so no frame renders
   untranslated copy. The remaining languages warm on idle after first
   paint, keeping the switcher instant.

perf(timeline): coalesce hover-preview updates to one per frame

Moving the pointer across the timeline re-rendered the timeline, the ruler
timecode and the preview panel once per pointer report. The browser delivers
each report in its own task, so React had no chance to batch them, and a
pointer reports faster than the display refreshes — every commit but the
last in a frame was thrown away before anything was painted.

Measured in the editor, 60 pointer moves delivered one per task:

  before   890 DOM mutations   292 ms
  after    250 DOM mutations   125 ms

Hover positions now go through createFrameCoalescer, which keeps only the
newest value and applies it on the next animation frame — the pattern the
drag path in useTimelinePointer already used. Clearing stays synchronous:
when a drag or playback starts, a stale hover marker has to go immediately,
and dropping it a frame late is visible.

The scheduler is injected rather than calling requestAnimationFrame
directly, so frameCoalescer.verify.ts drives it with a hand-cranked frame
and can assert what actually matters: many values in one frame collapse to
one application of the last value, the newest apply callback wins (React
closures go stale every render), cancel() disarms the frame so an unmount
cannot apply into dead state, and a throwing apply does not wedge the
coalescer for later values.

Note for anyone re-measuring: dispatching a burst of pointermove events
synchronously shows almost no difference, because React batches a
synchronous burst into one render. That measurement is misleading — a real
pointer arrives one event per task. Deliver the events through separate
tasks (MessageChannel) to see the real behaviour.

fix(export): give the browser engine the same per-frame budget as the local one

Reported: an export dying with

  A delayRender() "Extracting frame at time 0.2 from /media/uploads/….mp4"
  was called but not cleared after 28000ms … Retries left: 1

Reproduced on current main: load a project whose timeline holds a real
video, stall that media's requests, and call renderTimelineInBrowser. It
fails at 28068ms with that exact message.

Cause: src/export/browserExport.ts never passed
delayRenderTimeoutInMilliseconds to renderMediaOnWeb, so
@remotion/web-renderer used Remotion's 30s default, and delayRender reports
that minus its own 2s buffer — hence 28000. The local renderer has always
set its own budget, so the same project could fail on the browser engine and
render fine on the local one. Both now read DEFAULT_RENDER_TIMEOUT_MS from
remotion/render-timeout.mjs. Passing the option through was confirmed
end-to-end: the reported figure moved from 28000ms to 118000ms when the
budget was 120s.

The budget itself is now ten minutes a frame, up from two. It bounds ONE
frame's async work, never the export — a 76k-frame render still runs as long
as it needs. Its job is to catch a hang: a delayRender() that will never
clear (a decoder that fails silently, a media read that never settles, a
lost WebGL context) would otherwise freeze the export at N% with no error,
and this timeout is also what triggers Remotion's one-shot frame retry, so
dropping it entirely would drop the retry that rescues transient decode
failures. Two minutes was tight enough to fail exports that would have
finished; a frame with no data after ten minutes is hung, not slow.
CC_RENDER_TIMEOUT_MS still overrides, and its ceiling moved to an hour so
the default is no longer also the maximum.

remotion/render-timeout.d.mts lets browser code import the constant:
render-timeout.mjs stays plain ESM because bare node runs it, and
tsconfig.app.json only includes src/.

browserExport.verify.ts asserts the option is passed and equals what the
local renderer resolves, so the two engines cannot drift apart again.

Validation: npm run build (tsc -b), npm run lint (0 warnings), npm test
(162 segments). In the browser the constant resolves to 600000 through the
