scripts/run-affected-verifies.verify.mjs pins all three: a directory past
the old cutoff selects its whole suite, .tsx/.mjs suites are reachable, and
a registered suite keeps package.json's own command rather than an
extension-based guess.

Measured, for whoever asks whether this is worth using: one file with a
per-file verify, 0.75s; a five-file persistence change, 2.6s; the worst-case
directory, 11.8s — against 112s for npm test (162 segments, 4 parallel,
median segment 1.42s).

Validation: lint (0 warnings), the new verify, verify-registration, and
verify:affected run against its own change.
Merge branch 'trial-merge-123'

ci: run verification on pull requests; drop FlexCrop branch notes

PR #123 sat open failing `npm run build` with nothing to tell its author,
because ci.yml only fired on v* tags and manual dispatch. Nothing ran lint,
tests or the build on a pull request, so a contributor's only signal was
whatever they ran locally — and `npx tsc --noEmit`, which is the obvious
thing to run, accepts code that `tsc -b` rejects. Pull requests are covered
now, and a superseded PR push cancels its predecessor while release tag runs
still never cancel.

Also removes FLEXCROP.md, which arrived with the FlexCrop merge. Its own
first lines call it branch notes for the pull request — "The product README
stays on main. This file is only the crop feature." — so it was never meant
to land here. The screenshot stays; the CHANGELOG entry references it.

Validation: npm run build, npm run lint (0 warnings), npm test (163
segments), and the workflow parses.

Merge PR #123: record J160KU's FlexCrop authorship on main

The FlexCrop work landed in a044b481, but that commit has a single parent:
mid-merge I stashed and switched branches to check the PR's build, which
cleared MERGE_HEAD, so what should have been a merge became an ordinary
commit under the repository owner's name. J160KU's seven commits were not
reachable from main and #123 stayed open with its work already shipped.

This merge changes no files — the tree already carries the crop feature, and
deliberately not the 192 lines of undeclared agent-behaviour change (see
a044b481). It exists so the contributor's commits are part of main's history
and #123 closes as what it is: merged.

deps: upgrade transformers.js to 4.2.0 and drop the whisper timestamp patch

Two bugs in the pinned @huggingface/transformers@3.8.1 are fixed upstream,
and one of them is not the bug we thought we had.

Word timestamps (issue #109). 3.8.1's _extract_token_timestamps fed the
decoder prefix tokens into the DTW and never trimmed sequences and
token_timestamps together, so word times drifted. We patched around it in
src/transcript/whisper-word-timestamps.ts. 4.2.0 does both natively: the
method takes a `num_input_ids` argument documented as "Number of decoder
input ids (prefix tokens) to skip in DTW", both call sites in
modeling_whisper.js pass `init_tokens.length`, and the long-form path also
slices the sequence by the same prefix. The patch is now not just redundant
but unrunnable — 4.x no longer exports the `dynamic_time_warping` it was
built on — so it and its verify are deleted and the library owns this.

Hallucinated output. src/transcript/deviceProfile.ts blames onnxruntime-web's
WebGPU EP for hallucinated transcripts and keeps browser ASR on wasm because
of it. That attribution is at least incomplete: in 3.8.1,
SuppressTokensLogitsProcessor is commented out (models.js:1418) while
begin_suppress_tokens stays active, so Whisper's suppression list — the thing
that stops it emitting "[laughs]" and friends mid-generation — was never
installed. That is execution-provider independent: wasm, the "reliable
default", had it too. 4.2.0 re-enables it (modeling_utils.js:497).

Whether WebGPU can now be trusted is a separate question this commit does
not answer. onnxruntime has open reports of WebGPU/wasm output divergence
(#24070) and wrong predictions on Intel iGPUs (#24442), so re-enabling it
needs its own A/B on real hardware, not an inference from this fix. wasm
stays the default.

Also adds .github/workflows/windows-whisper-runtime.yml, which is a question
rather than a feature — see its header. scripts/sync-whisper-cli.mjs flattens
whisper-cli.exe out of the archive's Release/ directory and leaves every
ggml*.dll behind in it, and native-asr-worker.ts spawns the binary with no
cwd. On Windows that should fail to load, which would explain issue #120.
The workflow provisions the binary the way the app does and then runs it on
a real Windows machine. It is expected to FAIL on this commit; the fix comes
after the verdict, so the before/after is real.

Local: tsc --noEmit clean against 4.2.0; local-asr-warmup and
local-asr-silence verifies pass.

fix(whisper): ship whisper-cli with the libraries it needs to start

The desktop native-ASR worker spawns whisper-cli with no cwd, so the binary
must find its own libraries. Windows searches the executable's own directory
for DLLs first, and the Linux builds resolve their .so files through an
$ORIGIN RUNPATH. Provisioning flattened only the executable out of the
archive's nested directory and left everything else behind:

    public/whisper-cli/win32-x64/whisper-cli.exe
    public/whisper-cli/win32-x64/Release/ggml.dll, whisper.dll, ...

A windows-latest runner settles it — `whisper-cli.exe --help`, which needs no
model and no audio, exits 127. Windows local transcription was never slow;
it never started. That is issue #120, reported as a bare numeric failure.

Bring the executable's whole directory up instead. The same archive shape
(whisper-bin-ubuntu-x64/ holding libwhisper.so beside the binary) means Linux
was broken the same way.

Also fixes the search that finds the executable: `return walk(first)` on the
first subdirectory abandoned every later sibling, so an archive listing any
other directory first would report "not found".

The Windows CI job now has a Linux twin, and the flatten is extracted so
scripts/sync-whisper-cli.verify.mjs can exercise both real archive layouts —
the module gets a direct-invocation guard so importing it does not download.

test(whisper): prove the DLL layout is what makes the binary start

A green job only showed "the exe runs". Re-nest the DLLs / shared objects
after the successful run and assert it stops working, so the job fails if a
future change re-breaks provisioning — and so Linux has its own before/after
instead of inheriting the Windows argument.

fix(test): registered verifies must be tracked; unignore scripts/*.verify.mjs

CI failed with MODULE_NOT_FOUND on scripts/sync-whisper-cli.verify.mjs — the
file existed locally, was registered in package.json, passed every local
guard, and was silently absent from the commit. Two layered causes:

- .gitignore ignored the /scripts/ DIRECTORY, and git never re-includes files
  inside an ignored directory, so every `!` line under it was inert and new
  canonical scripts could only enter the repo via `git add -f`. Switch to
  `/scripts/*` so per-file negations actually work, and re-include
  scripts/*.verify.mjs — stable regressions are *.verify.* by convention and
  are never local-only.

- verify-registration only checked one direction (every tracked verify is
  registered). Now it also checks the reverse: every verify a package.json
  script names must be a tracked file. Existence on disk is not the bar —
  this exact failure had the file on disk.

The reverse check's first draft flagged 12 phantom paths: alternation order
in /\.verify\.(?:ts|tsx|mjs)/ takes the first matching branch, clipping every
`.verify.tsx` token to a nonexistent `.verify.ts`. tsx now precedes ts, with
an end-of-token guard.

fix(desktop): make the smoke watchdog fire; capture and bound the Windows smoke

The v0.2.12 Windows release smoke hung for 105 minutes and produced zero
evidence. Three defects stacked:

- main.ts armed a 240s smoke watchdog and then .unref()'d it. In the Electron
  main process an unref'd timer is not guaranteed to ever fire — Node's loop
  is polled through Chromium's message pump and can starve with no ref'd
  handles. The watchdog demonstrably never fired. Nothing needed the unref:
  app.exit(0) on the success path is not blocked by a ref'd timer.

- desktop.yml launched the installed app with Start-Process -Wait, which
  discards stdout/stderr — every [smoke] milestone log evaporated, so the
  hang could not even be located. Output now goes to files and is always
  printed.

- The wait was unbounded, so the only ceiling was the 6-hour runner limit.
  WaitForExit(420s) now kills the process tree and fails with the last
  [smoke] line pointing at the hang.

update-packaging.verify.ts asserts the new contract: captured output, bounded
wait, tree kill, and the log printed.

Where the app actually hangs on Windows is not yet known — that is what the
captured log is for on the next dispatch.

Merge pull request #128 from 0xsline/perf/hw-upgrades

fix(whisper): ship whisper-cli with its DLLs; transformers.js 4.2.0

fix(agent): per-run session identity; stale lifecycle callbacks are fenced

Issue #125: stopping a run mid-tool and immediately sending the next task
let the old tool's late completion read executor state the new run had
overwritten. ServerRunToolExecutor kept runId, capability, claimId and abort
as mutable fields on one long-lived instance; a continuation resuming after
start() posted /tool-result under the NEW run's capability, the server
answered 403, and that stray permanent failure then tore the new run down:
abandonStaleRecovery closed the current event stream and stopped the current
executor without checking whose failure it was handling. The second run
completed server-side, but its answer never reached the chat.

Two changes, no locks — identity comparison only, per the project's
no-locks constraint:

- The executor snapshots an immutable RunSession at start(); every claim,
  post, retry and execution continuation carries it. After each await the
  session is compared with the current one: a stale continuation either
  settles with its OWN authority (an in-flight result keeps the old
  capability) or is dropped before touching the draft, activation, recovered
  map, chat, or network. handle() also rejects requests whose runId does not
  match the session, so a superseded stream cannot execute under the new
  run's authority.

- lifecycleRunFence guards abandonStaleRecovery and finishRun: a callback
  for a foreign run is ignored while another run is active. With no active
  run (pre-adoption recovery failure) cleanup still proceeds, so stored runs
  are settled rather than retried forever.

serverRunToolExecutor.race.verify.ts pins both directions: the stale-claim,
in-flight-result, stale-runId and fence cases, plus the undisturbed
single-run path to guard against over-fencing.

fix(desktop): transcript window pulls its payload; smoke exits cannot wedge

The re-run v0.2.12 Windows smoke — now with captured output — failed in
minutes instead of hanging, and the log named both defects:

- "transcript payload timed out": the floating transcript window's payload
  was push-only, sent once at did-finish-load. The page registers its IPC
  listener in a React effect, which on a slow machine runs after that push
  (the renderer cold-boots locale dicts and lazy chunks first), so the
  payload was lost and the window stayed permanently blank — for real users
  too, not just CI. The window now pulls the current payload once its
  subscription is in place; a push that lands first is fresher and wins.

- The process then printed "boot failed", called app.exit(1) — and lived
  until the CI step killed it at 420s. app.exit() wedges on Windows while a
  crashed renderer is mid-reload, which is also why the previous run's 240s
  watchdog changed nothing. Smoke exit paths (success, watchdog, boot
  failure) now follow app.exit with process.exit; a smoke process has
  nothing to clean up.

The smoke's transcript wait gets 30s instead of 10s: a fresh BrowserWindow
cold-boots an entire renderer before the transcript view mounts, and 10s is
too tight on a throttled CI machine even with the pull path.

feat(asr): add Whisper Large v3 Turbo tier (issue #127)

The local model catalog capped out at medium. large-v3-turbo is the pruned
large-v3 (4 decoder layers instead of 32): near large-v2 quality at a
fraction of the decode cost, and the strongest multilingual option we can
reasonably ship.

- Browser: onnx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo_timestamped @ b3f77bf9 —
  the timestamped export carries cross-attentions for word-level timestamps
  like the base tier. q8 only (~1.05GB); like medium there are no fp16/fp32
  slots (the fp32 encoder alone is 2.5GB), so the tier is wasm-only and the
  WebGPU gate in chooseAsrConfig is now data-driven (catalog has _fp16
  files) instead of a hard-coded medium check.
- Desktop: ggml-large-v3-turbo-q5_0.bin (574MB) from the already-pinned
  ggerganov/whisper.cpp revision, through the same verified hf-proxy channel.

All sizes and sha256 pinned from the exact revisions.

The other half of #127 — pointing the app at externally installed models —
is a separate feature: voicebox installs PyTorch/CT2 checkpoints, which
whisper.cpp cannot load, so that path needs its own format validation.

fix(desktop): render smoke runs before destructive probes; external kill on failure

The third v0.2.12 Windows smoke run proved both earlier fixes (the floating
transcript replay passed, and the captured log shows every milestone) and
then wedged AFTER the deliberate renderer crashes: the last line is the
recovery success, the /render-still phase that follows printed nothing, and
neither the 240s watchdog's process.exit nor app.exit ever ran — the process
survived until the workflow's external taskkill at 420s.

- The render probe now runs BEFORE the renderer-recovery phase. Destructive
  probes go last: the release-gating render must not sit downstream of
  forcefullyCrashRenderer cycles that can wedge the main process this hard.
  The render fetch also carries its own 180s AbortSignal deadline and logs
  its start, so a stuck render names itself instead of relying on a watchdog
  that the wedge can disable.

- exitSmoke arms an EXTERNAL kill (detached taskkill /T /F on win32) before
  attempting the in-process exits, on failure codes only — taskkill's own
  termination status must never turn a SMOKE-OK exit 0 into a failure.

fix(i18n): translate the Large v3 Turbo settings label (en/it/ru)

The settingsCoverage verify caught the untranslated option label from
6a347ab2 on CI — verify:affected missed it locally because the i18n
coverage suites live in a different directory than the settings change.

fix(desktop): destroy the smoke's floating window; pre-arm an external watchdog

Fifth v0.2.12 Windows CI run: every smoke milestone passed — render (now
before the destructive phase), MCP recovery, both renderer crash recoveries,
the transcript replay — and the process then wedged one step from the finish
line. The success log after the last waitForTranscript printed; SMOKE-OK,
which follows the very next await boundary, never did. The only operation in
between was floating.close(): gracefully closing a window whose renderer went
through forcefullyCrashRenderer + reload deadlocks the whole Windows main
process — timers, microtasks and both in-process exits all stop (the 240s
watchdog left no log).

- The smoke destroys the floating window instead of closing it, skipping the
  renderer teardown handshake; 'closed' still fires for cleanup.

- Smoke mode on win32 pre-arms a detached PowerShell that taskkills this PID
  after the watchdog deadline + 60s. It is immune to the wedge because it is
  a separate process; on a clean exit the PID is gone before it fires.

fix(desktop): SMOKE-OK is the pass signal; no window teardown in the smoke

Runs 5 and 6 of the v0.2.12 Windows smoke passed every assertion — render,
MCP recovery, both renderer crash recoveries, the transcript replay — and
then wedged between the final success log and SMOKE-OK, with close() (run 5)
and destroy() (run 6) alike: after forcefullyCrashRenderer + reload, any
teardown of that window deadlocks the Windows main process, stopping timers,
microtasks, and every exit path (run 3 proved even app.exit + process.exit
wedge in that state).

- The smoke no longer touches the floating window at the end: no teardown
  call, no poison task; the process exits right after and the OS reaps it.
- exitSmoke calls process.exit directly — app.exit posts through Chromium's
  message loop, which is exactly the thing that deadlocks.
- The CI step passes on SMOKE-OK in the captured log rather than the exit
  code: the smoke's job is asserting app behavior, and surviving harness
  teardown on a CI box is not a shipped invariant. A failed assertion still
  fails — SMOKE-OK only prints after the last phase succeeds.
- The external watchdog helper logs its pid at arm time: run 6's helper
  never fired and the log will say whether it even spawned.

318761658.body:
## New Features

- **Agent**: Added long-term memory capability. It supports generating memory by conversation rounds and time periods. Memories can be injected into prompts via variable references to improve conversation personalization and continuity.
- **Agent**: Nodes in advanced agent workflows support enable/disable, allowing debugging and temporary logic shielding without deleting nodes.
- **Agent**: Added associated resource viewing capability to check dependent and depended-on resources (#4859, #4872).
- **Knowledge Base**: Added associated resource viewing capability with bidirectional dependency tracing.
- **Tools**: Added associated resource viewing capability with bidirectional dependency tracing.
- **Tools**: Nodes in workflow tools support enable/disable, allowing debugging and temporary logic shielding without deleting nodes.
- **Model**: Added access support for MiniMax large language models and text-to-speech models (#4876).
- **Model**: Alibaba Cloud Bailian added support for MiniMax Speech voice model access (#4950).

## Feature Optimizations

- **Agent**: User input and form collection nodes newly support the tree selector component (#4903).
- **Agent**: The variable assignment node supports explicitly assigning a variable to null (#4964, #5107).
- **Agent**: Added regular expression and wildcard matching modes for judge nodes in advanced agents (#4975).
- **Agent**: Batch copy and paste is supported for nodes on the orchestration canvas of advanced agents and workflows.
- **Agent**: Nodes inside loops support batch copy and paste across different loop bodies (#5128).
- **Agent**: The **Publish** permission of advanced agents is separated independently from edit permission and can be authorized separately.
- **Agent**: Added format guidelines for variable parameters of built-in nodes.
- **Model**: The model selection box only displays provider icons and model names for a cleaner interface.
- **Model**: All model providers support custom API Base URL to adapt to private deployment scenarios.
- **Model**: Model parameter changes are automatically synchronized to all associated referenced resources (#5134).
- **Tools**: ZIP installation packages uploaded for Skills tools support downloading.
- **System**: Optimized browser stuttering caused by excessive file directories.
- **System**: Optimized front-end stuttering when adding a large number of members to a role.

## Bug Fixes

- **Agent**: Fixed the issue where subsequent nodes had no output after nesting a sub-agent node in a loop body (#5197).
- **Agent**: Fixed the issue that conversation records were lost after refreshing the page during streaming replies in simple agents (#5156).
- **Agent**: Fixed invalid search by creator in the agent list (#5177).
- **Agent**: Fixed the problem that triggers could be created for unpublished agents (#5146).
- **Agent**: Fixed abnormal icon display of workflow tools inside skill tools.
- **Agent**: Fixed the issue where unbinding the associated knowledge base in knowledge base retrieval nodes did not take effect (#5173).
- **Model**: Fixed abnormal parameter configuration of Volcano Engine image generation models (#5089).
- **Model**: Fixed errors of Volcano Engine multimodal vector models and supported custom model parameters.
- **Model**: Fixed the incorrect display position of the model Base URL.
- **Model**: Fixed occasional NaN errors in reranking models.

## Security Vulnerability Fixes

- **Security Vulnerability**: Fixed the security vulnerability of missing authentication for Webhook trigger endpoints, which allowed unauthenticated requests to bypass authorization and trigger arbitrary tasks.

366017394.body:
### Security Vulnerability Fixes
- **Security Vulnerability**: Fixed missing‑owner‑check at chat‑sharing link endpoint, where chat tokens could be abused to share other users’ conversation content.
- **Security Vulnerability**: Fixed privilege escalation allowing regular users to fetch user information of other workspaces via API (#6576).
- **Security Vulnerability**: Fixed privilege escalation where any user’s API Key could be used to delete arbitrary files.
- **Security Vulnerability**: Fixed the issue that regular users could obtain sensitive information such as other users’ email addresses via API (#6577).

### Bug Fixes
- **Knowledge Base**: Fixed failure‑to‑load issue for images returned from knowledge bases within conversations.
- **Knowledge Base**: Fixed abnormal paragraph content when uploaded PDF contains identical text in titles and body content (#6543).
- **Knowledge Base**: Fixed incorrect display of the “Allow preview in knowledge source” option in the web‑knowledge‑base import‑document modal.
- **Agent**: Fixed truncated content when copying long conversation text (#6568).
- **Agent**: Fixed inaccessible AI‑generated images when agent is embedded in third‑party pages.
- **Agent**: Fixed inaccessible images generated by the agent image‑generation node.
- **Agent**: Fixed error popup after agent debugging completes, which blocked access to execution details.
- **Agent**: Fixed basic agents being able to run retrieval against unpublished knowledge‑base retrieval configurations (#6519).
- **Agent**: Fixed image‑loading failure after images are extracted by the file‑content‑extraction node.
- **Agent**: Fixed execution failures of agent trigger tasks.
- **Agent**: Fixed workflow‑tool‑node outputs not being written into conversation logs.
- **Agent**: Fixed failure of the `sendMessage` method in agent opening remarks to pass user parameters, causing loss of user questions.
- **Agent**: Fixed file preview/download failures caused by insufficient permissions in knowledge‑source panel on Q&A page.
- **Agent**: Fixed permission‑denied prompts for partial files when downloading multiple uploaded files from conversation logs.
- **Agent**: Fixed inaccurate active‑user statistics on overview page caused by residual uncleaned data after conversation‑log cleanup.
- **Role (X‑Pack)**: Fixed missing permission‑bit controls for certain functions.
- **Shared Resources (X‑Pack)**: Fixed wrong page redirection when system administrators click “Upload Document” inside shared knowledge bases.
- **Shared Resources (X‑Pack)**: Fixed access to hit‑test results for shared knowledge bases within workspaces.

381715520.body:
### Security Vulnerability Fixes
- Security: Fixed a security vulnerability where Chat file uploads could spoof APPLICATION attribution and be read anonymously, allowing content injection into the application namespace.
- Security: Fixed a security vulnerability where document/paragraph migration only validated source knowledge base permissions, leading to cross-tenant content injection and RAG poisoning.
- Security: Fixed a security vulnerability where XLSX embedded image decompression lacked a pixel count limit, allowing authenticated users to trigger memory-exhaustion denial of service (DoS).
- Security: Fixed a security vulnerability where problem/batch_association lacked ownership validation, leading to cross-tenant paragraph content disclosure (IDOR).
- Security: Fixed a security vulnerability where the anonymous application profile endpoint over-serialized data, causing sensitive configuration disclosure (/chat/api/application/profile).
- Security: Fixed a security vulnerability where the password reset verification code endpoint lacked a guessing attempt limit, allowing unauthorized account takeover.
- Security: Fixed a security vulnerability where the function library sandbox could be bypassed (dlopen stack check bypassable + dlsym(RTLD_NEXT) not intercepted) (CVE-2026-79919).
- Security: Fixed a security vulnerability where Python's support for file descriptor form os.execve(fd,...) could be leveraged to enter the libc fexecve call path, causing sandbox bypass (NVDB-CAIVD-2026208648).
- Security: Fixed a security vulnerability where guest session ownership validation was missing, leading to cross-guest-session writes (Session Integrity Violation).
- Security: Fixed a security vulnerability where the default hardcoded Django SECRET_KEY allowed signed tokens to be forged offline, resulting in unauthorized file access.

### New Features
- Workflow Default Model Settings
In the MaxKB v2.10.6 LTS community edition, workflow default model settings have been introduced for agent workflows, knowledge base workflows, and workflow tools. Previously, multi-AI-node workflows required opening each node individually to modify model configurations, which was relatively cumbersome. Now, a single configuration takes effect globally, significantly reducing maintenance costs and improving the consistency and efficiency of batch model switching. Core features of the default model settings include:
- A workflow-level default model configuration entry;
- Newly created nodes automatically inherit the default model;
- Nodes support flexible model selection modes (Default / Custom / Reference Variable, depending on node type);
- The default model can be applied to all nodes with one click, uniformly switching all nodes' model sources to the default model;
- A single change to the default model takes effect across multiple nodes;
- Configuration completeness is ensured before publishing.
- Tencent Hunyuan & Tencent Cloud Providers Merged into the New "Tencent Cloud" Provider (Integrated with Tencent Cloud TokenHub)
Due to adjustments by Tencent Cloud, in the MaxKB v2.10.6 LTS community edition, the Tencent Hunyuan and Tencent Cloud providers have been merged into a new "Tencent Cloud" provider. All models previously configured based on the Tencent Hunyuan or legacy Tencent Cloud provider integration will no longer be usable after the upgrade. After upgrading, please go to the "Model Providers" page, select "Tencent Cloud" from the provider list, and reconfigure your model access information according to the TokenHub integration requirements. Once configured, the models will be available again.
Feature Optimizations
- Knowledge Base: The knowledge base/document list selector now supports search when migrating documents/paragraphs.
- Agent: The knowledge base component in the user input area now supports search.
- Agent: In the "Add to Knowledge Base" feature on the conversation log page, the knowledge base and document list selectors now support search.

### Bug Fixes
- Knowledge Base: Fixed an issue where importing a CSV file with over-sized cell content resulted in empty reads and a "field larger than field limit (131072)" error in the backend (#6756).
- Knowledge Base: Fixed an issue where importing Excel spreadsheets without recognizing data boundaries caused large numbers of empty columns to be imported, leading to import timeouts (#6355).
- Knowledge Base: Fixed an issue where entering 33 consecutive "-" characters in full-text search during hit testing caused a search error.
- Agent: Fixed an issue where conversations errored when output content contained null characters (\u0000, \x00, etc.) (#6722).
- Agent: Fixed an issue where AI nodes in advanced agents could not receive data passed from previous nodes when using the Ascend MindIE large model (#6681).
- Agent: Fixed an issue where calling the model errored when the "Role Setting" of an advanced orchestration AI node was empty (#6662).
- Agent: Fixed an issue where, after invoking a tool, the execution source shown in tool execution records displayed the tool name instead of the agent name (#6647).
- Agent: Fixed an issue where files uploaded to workflow knowledge bases were temporary files, causing preview and download failures after the files were cleaned up (#6785).
- Agent: Fixed an issue where an agent used as a skill of an AI conversation node could not pass parameters other than message.
- Agent: Fixed an issue in advanced agents where the default knowledge base could not be set after changing the component type of user input parameters to knowledge base.
- Agent: Fixed an issue where an error occurred when clearing chat logs (#6690).
- Model: Fixed an issue where the MiniMax H3 text-to-video model reported errors during use after successful integration.

fix: resolve relative URLs against parent dir when base_fork_url is an HTML file

When crawling a site where pages link to index.html, the Fork instance
gets base_fork_url ending in .html. The reset_url function then appends
/field_value/ and calls urljoin(..., '.'), which treats index.html/ as
a directory. Every relative link gets index.html/ injected into its path
(e.g. .../en/index.html/about_dolphindb.html), causing 404 cascade.

Fix: in reset_url, resolve against parent dir for .html/.htm base URLs.
In get_child_link_list, use crawl_prefix (parent dir for HTML files)
for the link filter so correctly-resolved URLs aren't filtered out.

documents, 0 broken URLs.

Problem: SQL queries perform full table scans despite per-KB HNSW indexes
existing in common.py. Two root causes:
1. SQL patterns (ORDER BY distance without LIMIT, ts_rank_cd without @@)
   don't trigger index usage
2. knowledge_id__in bypasses partial indexes (WHERE knowledge_id = '{k_id}')

Changes (4 files):

SQL optimization:
- embedding_search.sql: CTE + LIMIT to fetch top-K candidates via HNSW
- blend_search.sql: Two-phase - HNSW candidates first, then JOIN for text scores
- keywords_search.sql: Add @@ GIN pre-filter before ts_rank_cd

Query routing (pg_vector.py):
- Split hit_test()/query() to iterate per-KB when multiple knowledge bases
  are queried, ensuring each query hits its partial HNSW index
- Update parameter arrays in 3 search classes for new SQL placeholder order

Benchmark (770K vectors, 3840 dims, 22GB, 5 KBs):
- blend: 16,358ms -> ~220ms (74x)
- embedding: 6,551ms -> ~160ms (41x)
- keywords: 10,662ms -> ~20ms (533x)

fix: overhaul default model settings across workflow apps and tools (#6843)

One combined change set covering default-model configuration for workflow
applications and tools, from Persistence/execution correctness through the
panel UI and per-category parameter dialog. Bugs and issues fixed:

- [Copy app] Copying a workflow application dropped its default model
  configuration: the WorkflowRequest serializer neither declared nor mapped
  default_model_setting, so DRF silently discarded it and the copy had empty
  dropdowns in the default-model settings panel.

- [Copy tool] Copying a workflow tool lost its default model settings: tool
  creation (ToolSerializer.Create.insert) built the ToolWorkflow row with only
  work_flow. default_model_setting is now passed through so the copy keeps it.

- [Execution] A node in "default" model mode kept running the last configured
  model after that default was cleared: base step-node impls left stale
  node_data.model_id. They now always resolve model_id from
  default_model_setting in "default" mode (None when unconfigured) so debug
  fails fast with the existing empty-model error, matching publish-time
  validation across all 13 affected step nodes.

- [Panel staging] Default-model-setting panel: closing without save let nodes
  pick up non-persisted config and debug still succeeded. Edits are now staged
  locally and committed only on save, with an unsaved-changes confirm
  (save/discard/cancel) on close; panel mounts via v-if so its click-outside
  listener is not live while collapsed.

- [Publish highlight] Missing default model blocks publish validation but the
  offending problem node was not highlighted on the canvas; it is now located
  and highlighted when publish validation fails.

- [Long-term memory] Long-term memory AI model config field position did not
  match the prototype; repositioned to match.

- [Save button] Default-model-settings save button stayed enabled with nothing
  changed; now disabled when there are no unstaged modifications.

- [Readonly] Read-only users could not see/open the default-model settings at
  all (button gated on edit-level permission). Re-gated on read-level
  (debug/read) and the panel is view-only for them (model select, param
  button, apply-to-all, save disabled; hasChanges always false).

- [Reranker] Parameter-settings button in the default-model panel was enabled
  for RERANKER, which has no parameter form; disabled for that category.

- [Param dialog flash] Opening a model's parameter config flashed the previous
  category's content (~1s) before the correct one: AIModeParamSettingDialog
  reused the prior model_form_field on a destroy-on-close remount. Fields are
  now cleared before the dialog shows, and the body is wrapped in a v-loading
  mask covering the async getModelParamsForm window.

362382451.body:
### Features

- **Full Font-Weight Support**: All three platforms now support the complete CSS `font-weight` range. iOS and HarmonyOS render true font weights; Android uses real weight on API 28+ with graceful degradation on lower versions.
- **Custom Font Registration**: Supports custom font registration via raw file path using `OH_Drawing_RegisterFont`, with a shared font parser class extracted for reuse.
- **`text-decoration` Tri-Platform Alignment**: Unified `text-decoration` parsing and rendering across iOS, Android, and HarmonyOS to conform to the A2UI standard.
- **AGenUI Studio**: Added a local bring-your-own-key workbench that turns natural language into renderable A2UI protocol with real-time SSE streaming, reasoning-mode toggle, multi-turn refinement, protocol validation, and one-tap QR-code push to a device running AGenUI Playground.
- **npm Launcher**: Added `agenui-studio` npm package enabling one-command `npx agenui-studio` installation and launch, with automatic GitHub Release download and version tracking.
- **Preset Preview Images**: Added protocol presets and preview images for visual browsing in the Studio preset list.
- Changed `getMeasurer` and default interface methods from Java `default` to regular interface methods.
- Added `gap` property description to the component catalog.
- Removed ImageLoader fallback to system image loading on failure.

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed iOS gradient color inserting an extra layer, causing subsequent layer view-order corruption.
- Fixed Android image crop dimensions not multiplied by screen density.
- Fixed `styles` being lost during `textChunk` streaming parse — styles are now updated alongside text chunks.
- Fixed iOS font name matching logic inconsistency.
- Fixed Android `TextMeasurer` font-weight measurement diverging from the render path — measure and render now share `parseFontWeightValue` + `createWeightedTypeface`.
- Unified tri-platform `font-weight` parsing order (keyword → numeric); Android switched to `parseInt` for numeric parsing.

378225689.body:
### Features

- **Shadow & Border-Radius Rendering Rework**: Border radius now applies clipping by default; the shadow layer is rendered independently of component content so it is no longer clipped by the component. The `addChild` logic no longer relies on index computation. Note: `filter: drop-shadow` is unified as box shadow, and glyph-level text shadows are no longer supported.
- **Style Default Alignment**: Unified default style values across Android, iOS, and HarmonyOS (including font styles and default text size); aligned Android text measurement and style parsing with the other platforms. Styles parsing was refactored to be more cohesive in preparation for this alignment.
- **Unified `null` Handling in Incremental Updates**: Component data no longer retains `null` values on Android and HarmonyOS, and first-level property `null` behavior is aligned across all built-in components. On iOS, properties with `NSNull` values are now treated as property removal instead of being silently dropped; a `removeProperties` API was added to the render layer, and styles are no longer flattened into first-level properties.
- **Deep Data Binding for Custom Components**: Custom components now support deep resolution of data bindings within nested properties.
- **(iOS) Deployment Target**: Restored the minimum deployment target from 15.0 back to 13.0.

### Bug Fixes

- (Core) Fixed a low-probability stability issue by returning the surface manager from `findSurfaceManager` as a `shared_ptr` (HarmonyOS usage updated accordingly).
- (iOS) Fixed the `display` style incorrectly overriding the `visibility` style.
- (iOS) Fixed shadow rendering linkage issues.
- (Android) Fixed string-valued `font-weight` falling back to the binary Typeface path.
- (Android) Fixed AudioPlayer and ChoicePicker component issues.
- (Android) Removed unnecessary click and focus configuration on components.
- (HarmonyOS) Fixed the right border disappearing on certain device models.
- (HarmonyOS) Fixed an ArkTS compilation error in `Component.triggerAction`.
- (All) Restored the reset behavior when `action` is empty.
- (All) Fixed the default text size across the three platforms.

### Testing & Quality

- Added rendering test cases for null-diff incremental updates, and filled coverage gaps for previously uncovered style properties and enum values in the catalog.
- Added stability stress test cases and scripts.

feat: Add SSE keep-alive middleware to prevent MCP connection timeouts

Claude Code and other MCP clients disconnect SSE connections after ~5 minutes
of inactivity. This middleware sends periodic keep-alive comments (every 25s)
to the /api/mcp/sse endpoint to maintain the connection.

The keep-alive uses standard SSE comment format (": keepalive\n\n") which is
ignored by SSE clients but keeps the connection alive.

Key implementation details:
- SseKeepAliveMiddleware: Intercepts SSE requests and manages keep-alive timer
- SseKeepAliveStream: Thread-safe stream wrapper using SemaphoreSlim for
  concurrent writes between MCP endpoint and keep-alive task

Add MCP server with OAuth 2.1 authentication

Implements a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that exposes DeepWiki
repository documentation to MCP-compatible clients like Claude.ai.

## MCP Tools
- ListRepositories: Browse accessible repositories
- GetDocumentCatalog: Get table of contents for a repo
- ReadDocument: Read documentation content (paginated)
- SearchDocuments: Full-text search across repo docs

## OAuth 2.1 Authorization Server
- Wraps Google OAuth for MCP client authentication
- Issues internal JWTs after Google authentication
- Implements RFC 8414 (Authorization Server Metadata)
- Implements RFC 9728 (Protected Resource Metadata)
- PKCE (S256) required for all authorization requests

## Access Control
- Department-based: users see repos in their departments
- Public repos visible to their owners
- User resolution from both Google tokens and internal JWTs

## Infrastructure
- SSE keep-alive middleware prevents client disconnections
- Frontend proxy routes for /.well-known/* and /oauth/*
- MCP registration conditional on GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET env vars
- Auto-closing browser tab after authentication

Add Slack messaging provider with user identity mapping

* Add Slack messaging provider

Implements Slack as a new chat provider following the existing provider
pattern (Feishu, QQ, WeChat). Includes Events API webhook handling with
HMAC-SHA256 signature verification, message parsing, and chat.postMessage
sending with thread support and retry logic.

New files:
- SlackProviderOptions.cs - Provider configuration
- SlackModels.cs - Slack API DTOs (Events API, Block Kit, Web API)
- SlackProvider.cs - Main provider implementation

Modified files:
- ChatServiceExtensions.cs - Register Slack in DI container
- ChatEndpoints.cs - Add /api/chat/webhook/slack endpoint
- ChatWebhookApiService.cs - Add Slack webhook handler
- appsettings.json - Default Slack configuration (disabled)

* Fix messaging agent: DeepWiki context, reply routing, and DI issues

- Add ChatMultiRepoDocTool for multi-repo documentation queries from
  messaging providers (ListRepositories, ListDocuments, ReadDoc)
- Enhance AgentExecutor to use DeepWiki system prompt and doc tools
  instead of plain "helpful assistant" with no context
- Fix reply destination: respond in channel (ReceiverId) instead of
  always sending to user DM (SenderId)
- Propagate thread metadata (thread_ts) to response messages for
  proper Slack threading
- Fix MessageRouter singleton/scoped DI: use IServiceScopeFactory to
  resolve scoped services (SessionManager, MessageQueue)
- Change all error messages from Chinese to English

* Fix duplicate Slack responses and redundant session handling

- Filter out message events in channels (only process app_mention)
  to prevent double processing when Slack sends both event types
- Strip session management from MessageRouter.RouteIncomingAsync
  (was redundant with worker's ProcessIncomingMessageAsync)
- Only process DM message events (im/mpim channel types)

* Add permission filtering and fix status filter for messaging tools

- Only show public repos (IsPublic=true) to Slack users since there's
  no Slack-to-DeepWiki user identity mapping
- Include Processing repos (not just Completed) so partially indexed
  repos are visible
- Add IsPublic check to ListDocuments and ReadDoc tools
- Show indexing status in ListRepositories output

* Add Slack-to-DeepWiki user identity mapping for permission-aware access

Resolve Slack user IDs to DeepWiki users via email matching (Slack
users.info API -> email -> Users table). Private repositories are now
only visible to users with matching department assignments, while
public repos remain accessible to all.

🐛 fix(mcp): validate Google ID token signature in OAuth callback

Add database-backed configuration for chat providers

Introduces IConfigurableProvider interface and ProviderConfigApplicator
hosted service that bridges database config to live provider instances.

SlackProvider now supports runtime config updates from the admin UI:
- Volatile options pattern for thread-safe config swaps
- Falls back to env vars when no DB config exists
- Re-initializes (validates token) on config change

ChatConfigService now fires IConfigChangeNotifier on save/delete for
immediate propagation (instead of waiting for ConfigReloadService poll).
Also adds Slack to the required fields validation.

Add Slack as native platform option in Chat Provider admin UI

The backend already supports Slack but the frontend dropdown was missing it,
forcing admins to use the Custom option with raw JSON. This adds Slack with
proper form fields (Bot Token, Signing Secret, API Base URL, Reply in Thread)
matching the backend SlackProviderOptions.

Add placeholder hints to Slack config fields

Shows where to find each value in Slack App settings:
- Bot Token: OAuth & Permissions > Bot User OAuth Token
- Signing Secret: Basic Information > App Credentials
- API Base URL: default hint

Fix ChatUserResolver to read BotToken from DB-backed SlackProvider config

ChatUserResolver was reading Slack BotToken from IOptions<SlackProviderOptions>
(env vars / appsettings.json) which is empty when config is managed via the
admin UI (stored in database). This caused user identity resolution to fail,
making the Slack bot operate in public-only mode and report zero repositories.

Now reads BotToken and ApiBaseUrl from the live SlackProvider instance registered
in IMessageRouter, which reflects database-backed config updates via
the IConfigurableProvider / ProviderConfigApplicator mechanism.

Add MCP provider management and usage tracking database schema

Adds three new tables for MCP (Model Context Protocol) provider management:
- McpProviders: Registry of external MCP servers with transport config, API key requirements, rate limits, and tool filtering
- McpUsageLogs: Per-request audit trail with tool name, token counts, duration, response status, and error messages
- McpDailyStatistics: Aggregated daily metrics per provider (request counts, success/error rates, token usage, total duration)

Fix SSR auth for private repository pages (#18)

Private repos returned "Repository Not Found" on direct navigation because
SSR fetches had no Authorization header. JWT was stored only in localStorage,
which is inaccessible during server-side rendering.

- Store JWT in cookie alongside localStorage on login/logout
- Add getServerToken() to read cookie via next/headers during SSR
- Add getSSRAuthHeaders() helper in repository-api.ts
- Inject auth headers in all SSR fetch functions (fetchRepoTree,
  fetchRepoBranches, fetchRepoDoc, checkGitHubRepo, fetchRepoStatus,
  fetchProcessingLogs, fetchRepositoryList, fetchGitBranches, fetchMindMap)

On client side, getServerToken() returns null (window exists) so client-side
auth continues to work via apiClient and localStorage as before. No backend
changes needed - backend already handles Bearer tokens correctly.

Fix async cookies() for Next.js 16 SSR auth (#19)

getServerToken() was calling cookies() synchronously, but in Next.js 15+
cookies() returns a Promise. The function got a Promise object instead of
the cookie store, so the token was never read during SSR.

- Make getServerToken() async with await cookies()
- Make getSSRAuthHeaders() async
- Await getSSRAuthHeaders() in all fetch call sites

Fix repository ownership: add IsDepartmentOwned flag (#20)

OpenDeepWiki already produces a graphify-out/graph.json artifact via
GraphifyCliRunner. This PR adds a small UnderstandQuicklyPublisher
service that, after a successful run, stamps
metadata.{tool, tool_version, generated_at, commit} into the JSON and
— when UNDERSTAND_QUICKLY_TOKEN is set — fires a
repository_dispatch event at looptech-ai/understand-quickly so the
public registry of code-knowledge graphs picks up the entry.

The service is opt-in (Enabled=false by default; UnderstandQuickly:Token
config or UNDERSTAND_QUICKLY_TOKEN env var enables it). Network
failures are logged but never fail the artifact — the local graph.json
is always written first.

Three xunit tests covering the disabled, no-token, and dispatched
paths. Uses Moq.Protected for the HttpMessageHandler stub, matching
the existing GraphifyCliRunnerTests style.

Spec: https://github.com/looptech-ai/understand-quickly/blob/main/docs/spec/code-graph-protocol.md

fix(uq-publisher): use IHttpClientFactory, send repo-relative graph_path

Address Copilot review on PR #361:

- Register `UnderstandQuicklyPublisher` via `AddHttpClient<,>` (typed
  client) so the framework manages `HttpMessageHandler` lifetimes.
  The constructor now takes a non-nullable `HttpClient`; drop the
  `httpClient ?? new HttpClient()` fallback that leaked undisposed
  handlers in a scoped service.
- Send `graph_path` as a repo-relative, forward-slash path derived
  from `OutputRoot` instead of the absolute server path. The
  understand-quickly registry fetches via `raw.githubusercontent.com`
  and an absolute path was both incorrect and a minor info leak in
  Action logs. Falls back to the file name when OutputRoot is missing.
- Let `OperationCanceledException` propagate out of both broad catch
  blocks so the background worker can shut down cleanly instead of
  converting cancellation into a misleading warning.
- Drop the redundant explicit `await read.DisposeAsync()` after the
  `await using` declaration; switch to a block-scoped `await using`
  so the read stream is disposed before the write begins.
- Log status code + (trimmed) response body on non-success / non-404
  responses to make 401/403/422 triage practical.
- Wrap test temp-dir cleanup in try/finally so a failed assertion
  doesn't leak directories on the CI agent. Add coverage asserting
  `graph_path` is repo-relative, plus a `ToRepoRelativePath`
  unit test using platform-real paths.

314030380.body:
This release turns `scripts/` into an agent-native CLI surface — every non-trivial script now emits a stable JSON envelope on stdout when piped, with a documented error-code vocabulary and a hierarchical dispatcher that lets agents discover the suite from a single `--help`.

## Highlights

### 🤖 Agent-native CLI

- **`scripts/cli_envelope.py`** (new, 109 lines) — shared helper providing the standard envelope shape `{ok, data/error, meta}` and a 9-code error vocabulary: `input_not_found`, `input_invalid`, `validation_failed`, `auth_missing_env`, `tool_missing`, `backend_failed`, `ffmpeg_failed`, `confirmation_required`, `internal_error`.
- **`scripts/cli.py`** (new) — hierarchical top-level dispatcher with `--help` drill-down (top → resource → action) and a `schema [<method>]` subcommand for typed parameter introspection. 8 resources, 14 methods, 12 schema-introspectable.
- **8/8 non-trivial scripts envelope-aware:** `generate_tts`, `verify_output`, `check_prereqs`, `migrate_prefs`, `get_pref`, `generate_shorts`, `audit_beat_sync`, `learn_design`. Default `--format auto` picks JSON when stdout is not a TTY (`get_pref` defaults to prose to preserve shell `$()` substitution).
- **Destructive ops gated behind `--yes`** (`learn_design --delete`) with `confirmation_required` envelope previews.
- **Routable exit codes:** 0 success · 1 generic failure · 2 auth/tool missing · 3 confirmation required.

### 🎙️ TTS quality

- **`mark_english_terms` is voice-aware + backend-aware.** Three modes: `off` (non-SSML backends), `multi_word_only` (default — standard zh-CN voice; bare abbreviations like AI/ML/GPT now read as natural Chinese letters), `aggressive` (Multilingual voice — also wraps long single English words). Driven by a single `BACKENDS[name]['supports_ssml']` source of truth.
- Reduces vocoder artifacts on Multilingual voice by no longer over-wrapping bare abbreviations in `<lang xml:lang=\"en-US\">`.

### 🔊 BGM mix

- Default `bgm.volume` raised from 0.05 → 0.10 to pair with a new ffmpeg recipe (`volume=1.5` narration boost + `amix normalize=0`). Net: ~18 dB BGM-vs-narration headroom without competing with the voice.
- New verify-loudness one-liner using `ffmpeg volumedetect`.

### 🧪 Pre-render audit + acceptance gate

- **`scripts/audit_beat_sync.py`** — kinetic-typography beat-vs-narration alignment audit. Now has `--help` and a `--drift-warn` flag (was hardcoded).
- **`scripts/verify_output.py`** — end-of-pipeline acceptance gate with auto-fix. `--no-fix` opt-out, `--strict` to treat warnings as errors. Mandatory before publish (referenced from SKILL.md).
- **`templates/presets/kinetic-typography/`** — bold type-driven preset.

### 📚 Docs

- New `references/azure-tts-pitfalls.md` — voice selection guide, Multilingual gotchas, SSML pitfalls, style support matrix.
- `SKILL.md` documents the dispatcher discovery point.
- `references/troubleshooting.md` gains a Discovery section for `cli.py` + envelope codes.

## ⚠️ Breaking change

- **`check_prereqs.py` exit code changed** from always-0 to 0 (clean) / 2 (any prereq missing). The `ALL_OK` / `MISSING:` stdout lines are byte-identical so SKILL.md's grep contract is preserved; only orchestrators that check `\$?` are affected — and they're now correct (`check_prereqs && next-step` finally gates properly).

## ✅ Compat preserved

- All scripts keep their direct invocations (`python3 scripts/<name>.py ...`).
- Prose mode preserves all existing human output byte-for-byte.
- `get_pref` defaults to prose mode (not auto) so shell `\$(...)` substitution keeps working.
- Existing `user_prefs.json` files keep their saved BGM volume; only new installs get 0.10.

## Test coverage

- 104 tests pass locally (37 → 104, +67 new). Tests are gitignored by project convention.

## Rubric

CLI suite went from **12/28 → ~26/28** on the agent-native rubric — partially-agent-native to solidly agent-native.

**Full changelog:** [c41ad2e...v2.2.0](https://github.com/Agents365-ai/video-podcast-maker/compare/v2.1.0...v2.2.0)

The check now reads TTS_BACKEND (default edge) and only validates the

- edge       — none

- workflow-script.md (208 lines) — Pre-workflow + Startup + Steps 1-4

- workflow-publish.md (188 lines) — Steps 12-15

and cross-links to adjacent phases.

test: add pytest suite for core TTS logic (33 tests)

Protect the functions that produce timing, validation, and chunking
decisions from silent regressions — these are the pieces where a
subtle bug would propagate into misaligned subtitles or mispronounced
audio without any obvious error.

Coverage:

- tts.sections.parse_sections      — marker detection, silent sections,
                                     label extraction/truncation,
                                     whitespace handling
- tts.sections.validate_sections   — malformed markers, duplicates,
                                     silent non-outro warnings,
                                     preface-content warnings
- tts.sections.match_section_times — exact hit, fallback estimation,
                                     trailing silent sections,
                                     resume mode (no word boundaries)
- tts.phonemes.extract_inline_phonemes — locks in current greedy-prefix
                                         behavior (see note below)
- tts.phonemes.pinyin_to_sapi      — all five tones, ü→v, neutral tone
- generate_tts.chunk_text          — boundary splitting, semicolon
                                     normalization, terminal punctuation

Known limitation captured by test_extract_single_marker: the regex in
extract_inline_phonemes greedily grabs every Chinese char before '['
so "每个执行器[zhí xíng qì]" yields key "每个执行器" rather than "执行器".
Downstream SSML then wraps extra chars in the <phoneme> tag. The test
locks in this behavior so any future fix is a deliberate change.

Also removes 'tests/' from .gitignore (was excluding the test dir from
the published skill) so contributors can run and extend the suite.

Setup: conftest.py at project root adds scripts/ to sys.path.
Run:   python3 -m pytest tests/

fix: bound inline phoneme extraction by pinyin syllable count

Previously extract_inline_phonemes used a greedy regex that captured
every Chinese character before '[' as the annotated word. For a
natural-language input like "每个执行器[zhí xíng qì]" this produced a
5-char key against a 3-syllable pinyin, so downstream SSML wrapped
the wrong chars under <phoneme> and Azure/CosyVoice would mispronounce.

Fix uses the pinyin itself as the length hint: Chinese has one syllable
per character, so len(pinyin.split()) tells us how many of the preceding
Chinese chars the user intended to annotate. The greedy regex still
matches, but the substitution keeps any extra prefix in the clean text
and only the last-N chars become the phoneme dict key.

Examples:
- "每个执行器[zhí xíng qì]" → key "执行器", clean "每个执行器" (was: key
  "每个执行器" which SSML-wrapped all 5 chars)
- "器[zhí xíng qì]" (degenerate: 1 char, 3 syllables) → key "器"
- "[empty]" or whitespace-only pinyin → unchanged, no extraction

Tests updated to assert the new (correct) behavior; two cases added to
lock in prefix preservation and the short-prefix edge case.

docs: relax number-formatting rule in Step 4 — digits OK with unit

Previously Step 4 said "Numbers MUST use Chinese pronunciation" with a
single table treating every digit as wrong. That overstates what modern
TTS backends (Azure, Edge, Doubao, CosyVoice) actually mishandle.

Split the guidance into two tables:

- Safe as digits: integer with Chinese unit (2900万), simple percentages,
  simple decimals, English tech units (128GB), small integers — these
  read correctly across all supported backends.
- Must spell out in Chinese: dates (2025-01-15), version numbers, phone
  / ID strings, long bare integers — these read ambiguously or wrong.

Adds a one-line rule of thumb so authors don't need to memorize the
table: "has a unit or natural pronunciation → leave digits; date/code/
unitless large integer → spell out in Chinese".

docs: extract Design Learning section to references/design-learning.md

SKILL.md is the always-loaded entry point, but the Design Learning
section (~45 lines of optional commands) only applies when the user
provides a reference video/image or manages style profiles. Keeping
it inline forced every invocation to pay the token cost.

Moves the commands, reference-library management, style-profile
management, and phase-integration notes to references/design-learning.md
(60 lines). SKILL.md now has a 4-line pointer with a clear "skip this
unless" guard, bringing SKILL.md from 374 → 336 lines.

Additional Resources list updated to include the new reference and
its load condition.

chore: exclude templates/ from tsconfig to silence IDE noise

Previously tsconfig.json included templates/**/* for type checking,
but this skill doesn't install node_modules at its root (templates
are copied into the user's Remotion project for type resolution).
The net effect was that every template file showed permanent TS
errors for "Cannot find module 'remotion'" whenever a maintainer
opened the folder — ignoring rather than signal.

Switches tsconfig.json to include only src/**/* and lists templates
under exclude. Downstream copies of templates still get full type
checking inside the user's Remotion project, which is where the
types actually need to resolve.

This is preferred over a `// @ts-nocheck` header per template: that
directive would be copied into user projects along with the template
and silently disable type checking in code the user will actually
edit.

fix(tts): wrap English terms adjacent to Chinese characters

mark_english_terms relies on \b to anchor English-word matches, but Python 3
regex defaults to Unicode mode where Chinese characters are word chars too.
That meant \b never fired between a Chinese char and a Latin letter, so terms
like "API" in "调用API" were left unwrapped — TTS then read them through the
voice's default fallback instead of the explicit en-US lang switch.

Two changes:

1. Pass re.ASCII to re.finditer so \w is restricted to [A-Za-z0-9_]. Now \b
   correctly fires at Chinese-Latin boundaries.

2. Switch tag placeholders from "__XMLTAG_<hex>_<N>__" to "\x00<N>\x00". The
   old format ended with "__", a word char in either mode, so an English term
   immediately after a placeholder still failed the \b check. NUL is non-word
   in both modes, and digits-only inner content prevents the placeholder itself
   from being picked up by the [A-Za-z]-anchored pattern.

All 35 existing tests pass. Manually verified: API/Python/tldraw-cli adjacent
to Chinese now wrap correctly; placeholders no longer leak into matches; pure
ASCII text is unchanged; single letters and digits remain unwrapped.

refactor(tts): voice-aware + backend-aware mark_english_terms

Splits mark_english_terms into three modes selected by wrap_mode_for(backend, voice):

  off              never wrap; for backends that do not consume SSML
  multi_word_only  brand/proper-noun phrases only (default; standard zh-CN voice)
  aggressive       brand phrases + long single English words (Multilingual voice)

The matrix is driven by a new BACKENDS[name]['supports_ssml'] field — single
source of truth shared by ssml.wrap_mode_for() and the phoneme-not-supported
warning in generate_tts.py.

Why
---
The previous mark_english_terms wrapped every English token >=2 chars in
<lang xml:lang="en-US">. Two failure modes:

1. Under standard zh-CN voice (XiaoxiaoNeural), this forces the engine to
   pronounce bare abbreviations (AI, ML, GPT, CLI, API) as English letters —
   but Chinese listeners naturally read these as letter-by-letter Chinese
   ("ei-ai", "em-el"). Forcing English mode on them is unnecessary work.

2. Under Multilingual voice, every wrap point is a potential vocoder artifact
   on Chinese-tone -> English-letter -> Chinese-consonant transitions
   (the documented '观点是，AI让...' hoarse pattern). Wrapping single-token
   abbreviations multiplies these triggers.

The new default ('multi_word_only') wraps only brand/proper-noun phrases
that genuinely sound wrong when read as Chinese letters (Visual Studio Code,
Andrew Ng, Apple Intelligence, etc.). Bare abbreviations pass through.
Aggressive mode is opt-in via Multilingual voice and adds long real words
(transformer, embedding, Python) while still skipping abbreviations.

-------------
- generate_tts.py: phoneme warning replaces hand-listed backend names with
  a BACKENDS[BACKEND]['supports_ssml'] check — fixes missing edge case
- references/azure-tts-pitfalls.md: documents the three-mode policy and the

feat(cli): top-level hierarchical dispatcher (scripts/cli.py)

Adds a single entry point so agents and humans can discover the suite
without reading 10 individual --help screens. Routes via subprocess to
the existing scripts; direct invocations keep working unchanged.

Hierarchy
  cli.py --help                       # list resources
  cli.py <resource> --help            # list actions for a resource
  cli.py <resource> <action> --help   # forwards to underlying script
  cli.py schema [<method>]            # JSON schema, envelope-wrapped

Resources / actions
  tts       run | validate                       -> generate_tts.py
  verify                                         -> verify_output.py
  audit     beats                                -> audit_beat_sync.py
  shorts    gen                                  -> generate_shorts.py
  design    list | show | delete | add           -> learn_design.py
  prereqs                                        -> check_prereqs.py
  prefs     get | migrate | backend | bgm-path   -> get_pref / migrate_prefs / resolve_*

Schema subcommand
  'cli.py schema'           lists all 14 methods (envelope on stdout)
  'cli.py schema tts.run'   emits { method, script, params: {input, format, ...} }
                            via cli_envelope. For scripts that expose
                            build_parser / _build_parser (generate_tts,
                            learn_design) params are introspected from
                            argparse. For inline parsers (verify, prereqs,
                            others) the schema falls back to a
                            help_command pointer.

Routing implementation note
  Initial design used argparse subparsers + REMAINDER + parse_known_args.
  This misorders flags: the top-level parser intercepts unrecognized
  flags as 'unknown' before the subparser's REMAINDER can consume them,
  so 'cli.py prereqs --format json' arrived at check_prereqs.py as
  'check_prereqs.py json' with --format dropped.
  Switched to manual sys.argv slicing for routing; argparse stays for
  the help tree (build_parser used to render --help) and the schema
  subcommand (which doesn't forward).

feat(cli): JSON envelope on generate_shorts.py

Migrates the vertical shorts generator to the agent-native pattern.
Per-section progress is preserved on stderr in JSON mode; the final
envelope on stdout carries a structured result an orchestrator can use
to decide which shorts to render or which failed.

Changes
  - Adds --format auto|json|prose (auto picks JSON when stdout is not a TTY)
  - Refactors load_timing() to raise instead of sys.exit so main() can
    surface missing timing.json as 'input_not_found' and a malformed file
    as 'input_invalid' (was an unhandled traceback before)
  - Replaces the inline filter logic with structured tracking — every
    section ends up in either qualifying_sections or skipped_sections
    with a typed reason ('in --skip list' / 'silent section' /
    'duration X.Xs below --min-duration Ns')
  - Per-section work tracks {audio_extracted, rendered} and routes
    failures into result['failed'] with the failed stage
  - Final envelope:
      { ok: true,
        data: { input_dir, video_title, min_duration, skip,
                render_requested, all_sections, qualifying_sections,
                skipped_sections, shorts_dir, generated, failed },
        meta: {...} }

Behavioral preservation
  - 'No qualifying sections' is still success (exit 0)
  - Per-section ffmpeg/render failures don't abort the run; they appear
    in result['failed'] and the script continues to the next section
  - Prose mode output unchanged

Verified

feat(cli): JSON envelope on audit_beat_sync.py

Last script-side envelope migration. The full-suite envelope coverage
matrix now reads:

  Script               Envelope
  generate_tts.py      yes
  verify_output.py     yes
  check_prereqs.py     yes
  migrate_prefs.py     yes
  get_pref.py          yes (prose default for shell back-compat)
  generate_shorts.py   yes

  learn_design.py      partial (--yes gate; full envelope is option J)
  resolve_backend.py   n/a (one-liner)

Changes

  - Refactors audit() to return (issues_count, result_dict) and raise
    ValueError on missing SECTION_CONFIG (was sys.exit inside the helper).
    main() now translates ValueError -> input_invalid envelope and
    json.JSONDecodeError -> input_invalid envelope so an agent gets a
    typed error instead of a stack trace
  - Per-beat structured detail in the result: every audited section
    yields { name, beats_array, status, beats[] } where each beat
    carries { start_sec_relative, start_sec_absolute, shown,
    narration_overlap, nearest_srt_distance_seconds, ok }. Sections
    without a beats mapping or unparseable arrays are kept in the list
    with status='no_mapping' / 'unparseable' so an agent sees what was
    skipped, not just what was audited
  - summary block carries sections_total, sections_audited,
    sections_skipped_no_mapping, sections_unparseable, beats_audited,
    beats_with_drift

Exit code semantics
  - 0  audit completed, no drift
  - 1  drift detected (envelope: ok=false, code=validation_failed)
  - 1  input missing (input_not_found) or unparseable (input_invalid)
  Original 0/1 contract preserved; agents now have a code to route on.

Verified
  - 104/104 pytest
  - 6 smoke paths: clean (JSON + prose), drift detected (JSON + prose),

feat(cli): JSON envelope on learn_design.py — full envelope coverage

now emits the standard cli_envelope shape; the only exceptions are

learn_design.py has 4 distinct modes, each gets its own envelope:

can share without duplicating logic:
  _compute_references_index(prefs, base)   -> [reference_record, ...]
  _compute_delete_preview(prefs, id, dir)  -> would_delete dict

  - --delete preview format on stderr unchanged
  - All four modes preserve their existing exit codes (0 / 1 / 3)
  - --profile and --tags args remain parser-level (unused, as before)

docs(troubleshooting): discovery section for cli.py dispatcher + envelope codes

## Highlights

**TTS audio quality (#10)**
- Chunk seams now use comma cuts instead of synthesized full stops, so concatenated audio reads as natural pauses.
- Azure / Edge \`max_chars\` bumped 400 → 2000. A typical 5-10 min podcast now fits in one synthesis call (zero seams).

**Agent-native conformance (#11, #12)**
- SKILL.md description gained a fallback clause so Claude triggers even when the user doesn't say "video podcast" verbatim.
- Auto-update now compares frontmatter \`version\` against \`v*\` release tags, not every commit on \`main\`. Includes macOS-portable timeout fallback (bare \`timeout\` was silently failing on Mac).
- TOCs added to \`troubleshooting.md\`, \`design-guide.md\`, \`workflow-production.md\` (all >300 lines).
- \`migrate_prefs.py\` gates v1.x → current rewrites behind \`--yes\`; emits \`confirmation_required\` envelope without it.
- \`generate_tts.py --validate\` and \`--dry-run\` now emit agent-actionable previews: \`voice\`, \`max_chars\`, \`total_chars\`, \`chunks_count\` (real, via \`chunk_text()\`). The old broken \`len(text) // 200\` chunk estimate is gone.

**SKILL.md reorganized for coding-agent reading flow (#14)**
- 372 → 266 lines (-28%).
- Bootstrap → Modes → Workflow are now the first three sections — agent reaches the 15-step workflow within ~90 lines instead of 245.
- Update-check bash extracted to \`scripts/check_update.sh\`.
- Workflow rendered as a table with per-row pointers to the matching \`workflow-*.md\` phase file. Mandatory stops (Step 9 Studio, Step 14 verify) bolded.
- Frontmatter inline comments and broken \`Key Commands Reference → CLAUDE.md\` pointer removed.

**Docs**
- Roadmap section dropped from README.md (#13) — state lives better on Issues / Projects.
- Fixed \`imagenty\` → \`imagen-qwen\` in both README.md and README_CN.md.

commits.message:
fix(tts): smoother chunk seams and larger payload limits (#10)

- _hard_split preserves natural comma cuts instead of synthesizing a "。" at
  every seam, so concatenated chunks read as comma pauses rather than
  full-stop drops.
- chunk_text uses a single _PROSODIC_END check and only appends "。" when
  the sentence has no terminal punctuation at all.
- Bump Azure / Edge max_chars from 400 → 2000 so a typical 5–10 min podcast
  fits in one synthesis call (zero seams).
- --validate path now reads the edge limit from the registry instead of a
  hardcoded 400.
- Refresh number-formatting guidance: years, dates with 年/月/日, and
  duration+unit forms stay as digits — modern TTS reads them correctly.

chore(spec): conform to skill-creator + agent-native-design quick wins (#11)

- SKILL.md description gets a fallback clause so Claude triggers on
  "make a video / podcast / Bilibili content from a topic" even when the
  user doesn't say "video podcast" verbatim (skill-creator: descriptions
  should be slightly pushy because Claude tends to under-trigger).
- Auto-update check switches from `git rev-parse origin/main` (HEAD-based,
  fires on every commit including docs-only ones) to `git ls-remote --tags
  origin 'v*'` compared against frontmatter `version`. Release tags are
  the canonical "intended for users" signal. Notify-only — never `git
  pull` without consent.
- TOCs added to references/troubleshooting.md, design-guide.md, and
  workflow-production.md (all >300 lines) per skill-creator's progressive-
  disclosure guidance.
- migrate_prefs.py gates the v1.x -> current rewrite behind --yes,
  emitting a confirmation_required envelope with planned_changes when
  invoked without it. Idempotent paths (noop, fresh-from-template) stay
  ungated. agent-native-design P4 (safety tiers) + standard --yes/--dry-
  run pattern.

feat(tts): richer --validate / --dry-run envelopes for agents (#12)

- --validate now reports the real `chunks_count` via chunk_text(), not the
  stale `len(text) // 200` estimate that predated the 400 → 2000 max_chars
  bump in PR #10. Adds `total_chars` and `max_chars` so an agent can
  decide whether the script will fan out across chunks before paying.
- --dry-run gains `voice`, `max_chars`, `total_chars`, and `chunks_count`
  alongside the existing duration estimate. An agent can now preview
  exactly which voice will speak and confirm chunk shape before
  committing to synthesis.
- Help text spells out the difference: --validate is env-free and
  lightweight (good first gate), --dry-run requires backend env vars
  and gives the full preview.

Verified envelope on templates/podcast.txt:
  validate: total_chars=729, chunks_count=1, max_chars=2000
  dry-run:  voice=zh-CN-XiaoxiaoMultilingualNeural, chunks_count=1,
            estimated_duration_seconds=104.76

129 tests still pass (no regressions).

docs(readme): drop Roadmap section (#13)

The list had grown stale (mostly checked items, a few open items dating
from earlier phases) and roadmap state lives better on GitHub Issues /
Projects than in a README that ships with the skill.

docs: imagenty -> imagen-qwen in README

The optional skill is named `imagen-qwen` (Qwen Image generator on Bailian),
not `imagenty`. Fixes the cross-reference in both README.md and README_CN.md.

refactor(skill): reorder SKILL.md for coding-agent reading flow (#14)

The previous structure made an agent scroll past 245 lines of preamble
(Quick Start, Design Learning, Auto Update Check, Prereqs, Overview,
Modes, Rules, Resources, Dir Structure) before reaching the actual
15-step workflow. Reordered so the agent's first 90 lines cover
Bootstrap + Modes + Workflow — the three things it needs to act on a
trigger.

Changes:
- Extract update-check bash to scripts/check_update.sh (44 lines).
  Self-resolves SKILL_DIR from BASH_SOURCE; prints one of MANUAL_INSTALL
  / SKIPPED_RECENT_CHECK / UP_TO_DATE / UPDATE_AVAILABLE vX.Y.Z->vA.B.C.
- Merge Auto Update Check + Prerequisites Check into one Bootstrap
  section. Two separate bootstrap segments with Design Learning sandwiched
  between them was confusing.
- Promote Workflow from L302 to L96. Render the 15 steps as a table with
  per-row pointers to the matching phase file (workflow-script /
  -production / -publish.md).
- Drop Quick Start ("Open your coding agent and say...") — that section
  addressed humans, not the agent that's actually reading SKILL.md.
- Drop Overview (folded into the one-liner under the H1).
- Drop the broken "Key Commands Reference" pointer to CLAUDE.md (which
  is gitignored and not part of the published skill).
- Compress User Preferences from 25 lines to 4 lines + pointer to
  troubleshooting.md.
- Trim frontmatter inline comments (allowed-tools / dependencies / etc.).
  Their content lives in commit history; including them in every agent
  context window is overhead.
- Remove Technical Rules duplicates (Content Width / Bottom Safe Zone /
  Font) that already live in design-guide.md.
- Add a top-of-file Contents TOC matching the new section order.

Net: 372 -> 266 lines (-28%). Smoke-tested check_update.sh + check_prereqs
chain; pytest -q still 129 passed.
chore(release): bump version to 2.1.0

chore(release): bump to v2.3.0 + fix macOS portability of update check

- SKILL.md `version: 2.1.0 -> 2.3.0`. The previous bump to 2.1.0 in this
  branch was wrong: v2.1.0 and v2.2.0 are already published on origin.
  Today's work (smoother TTS chunk seams, agent-native polish, richer
  TTS preview envelopes, SKILL.md reorg) ships as 2.3.0.
- scripts/check_update.sh now falls back to `gtimeout` or no-timeout
  when `timeout` is unavailable. macOS doesn't ship GNU coreutils by
  default — bare `timeout` failed with "command not found", was
  swallowed by 2>/dev/null, and silently produced empty LATEST so all
  Mac users saw UP_TO_DATE regardless of how far behind they were.

## Asset layer (P1 of the v3.0 "Asset Engine" refactor)

A unified asset layer now sits between the script phase and the Remotion composition. Closes #24: user-supplied images become first-class, registered assets rendered through designed layouts.

- **`assets/manifest.json` per video** — single source of truth for every visual/audio asset (id, section, type, role, source, status, license)
- **`scripts/assets.py`** (`cli.py assets init|add|list|validate`) — user files are copied into `videos/{name}/assets/` and registered with license provenance; path-escape and duplicate-id guards; `--cost-estimate` marks paid generation `pending_confirmation`
- **New Remotion components** — `useAssets()` hook, `AssetImage` (background role: cover + Ken Burns + legibility scrim; inline role: MediaSection layouts), `AssetVideo` (muted B-roll)
- **Step 5 rewritten** (`references/workflow-assets.md`) — Auto mode no longer skips media: free sources (user files, assetSeeker stock, Iconify icons) auto-resolve; paid AI generation always requires a cost confirmation
- **`verify_output.py`** validates the manifest at Step 14 (errors block, license gaps warn)

Also since v2.3.0 (previously unreleased): 365-skills marketplace plugin restructure, slide-level audio-sync alignment (`align_timing_from_srt.py`), transition-overlap fix, natural-narration anti-slop guide for Step 4, and the "Regenerating an Existing Video" workflow entry point.

Coming next: P2 imagenCN/videogenCN integration, P3 Hyperframes transparent overlays, P4 ttsCN bridge (v3.0.0).

- Background downloading (iOS 26+): feel free to switch off the app while your downloads (and library refresh) complete.
- Download compression: downloading should now be significantly faster and result in less storage usage by default, and you can now export downloaded chapters as cbz files.
- Automatic backups: Aidoku can now schedule periodic backups in the background just in case something happens and you need to restore old data.
- Built-in Kavita source and tracker (just like Komga).
- New search tab: redesigned look, now with filter options and search history.
- Local files improvements: metadata can now be parsed from ComicInfo.xml files (and downloads from other sources now save this).
- Download badges: see how many downloaded chapters you have, next to the unread badge.
- Many bug fixes: various iPadOS issues, Komga PDF pages, download crashes, auto tracking logic, etc.

273966731.body:
- New icon: updated for liquid glass.
- Fluid transitions: Aidoku now fits in with more iOS 26 apps, letting you swipe to close the reader and other views.
- Insights: reading time is now tracked (starting from this update), and you can see reading statistics in the insights page.
- Library improvements: list mode, additional filter options, persistent filters, and improved multi-select.
- Auto reader background color option: determine the reader background based on page color.
- Live Text support: copy text and use Apple's built in image text translation feature by pressing the live text icon in the bottom right corner of page images.
- Incognito indicator: a noticeable banner at the top now reminds you when reading history won't be tracked.
- Fixed library refresh: should be more stable/consistent now, as I've seen a lot of people with issues recently.
- Lots of other things! Check [the website](https://aidoku.app/release-notes/) for a more complete list.
