Explicitly launch OpenID Connect authentication with ?autoLaunch=1

This change extends OIDC authentication by enabling explicit redirection
to the OAuth provider when navigating to the login page with the manual
override parameter (/login?autoLaunch=1).

Use case: directly launch audiobookshelf from within e.g. Nextcloud using the
external sites app (use something like https://abs.example.org/login?autoLaunch=1
as URL) while keeping the possibility to launch audiobookshelf using its built-in
authentication mechanism. Assuming the username or mail address used in Nextcloud
and audiobookshelf are identical the user will be logged in to his or her account
no matter which method is used.

### Added

### Fixed

- Listening sessions from Android app showing device name as `Abs iOS`
- RSS feeds serving m4b files with incorrect Content-Type #5041 by @brandonfhall in #5221

### Changed

- Book & podcast descriptions from audio files are sanitized
- `cancel_scan` and `set_log_listener` socket events validate account type and log level
- More strings translated

commits.message: Add: 10 second grace period to access token cycle
Revert default token expiry
Fix: race condition in rotation
Allow rotation without grace period for invalidating all user sessions
Fix JS Doc deletion
Fix: grace period enable statement
Merge branch 'master' into token_refresh_race_condition
Rename migration to v2.35.0 & merge master
Cleanup rotateTokensForSession

fix: set correct Content-Type for RSS feed audio files

commits.message:
Add useIsMobile hook for responsive breakpoint

SSR-safe matchMedia hook keyed to the 640px mobile breakpoint shared with
globals.css. Components branch inline styles on it for mobile layout, since
the codebase styles almost everything inline (CSS media queries alone cannot
override inline styles).

Auto-hide sidebar on mobile and close it on selection

On the mobile breakpoint the sidebar is an overlay drawer. Default it to
hidden on load, and collapse it after the user picks a session, starts a new
session, or opens a file, so the chat/file content is revealed without an
extra tap. Desktop behavior is unchanged.

Fit chat top bar and its popovers to mobile width

On the mobile breakpoint the top bar would overflow: Export/Branches/System
become icon-only and the session-stats button collapses to a single info
icon, keeping every action reachable in one row. The shared top-panel
dropdown is now height-bounded and scrollable, and the session-info panel
stacks into a single column so it no longer overflows horizontally.

Wrap chat input controls and clamp model dropdown on mobile

The bottom controls row now wraps on the mobile breakpoint instead of
overflowing horizontally, and the model selector dropdown is pinned to the
viewport with a capped width so long model names can't push it off-screen.

Make Models and Skills modals fit mobile screens

Both modals had a fixed 860px width and a fixed-width inner side list, which
overflowed narrow screens. On the mobile breakpoint they now fill the
viewport (minus a small margin) and stack the side list above the detail
pane, each with its own scroll area, so every section stays reachable.

Close top panel and sidebar mutually on mobile

On narrow viewports the system/branches/session dropdown (z-index 500)
rendered above the sidebar overlay (z-index 200). Opening the sidebar
while a top panel was open left the panel stacked on top of the expanded
sidebar. Make the two mutually exclusive on mobile: opening the sidebar
closes any active top panel, and opening a top panel closes the sidebar.

Hide chat minimap on mobile

The 36px scroll minimap on the right edge is hover/drag oriented and only
adds clutter on touch-sized screens. Skip rendering it on mobile and
reclaim the space it reserved: the floating notice overlay, the
below-editor widgets, and the chat input no longer pad for the minimap
when it is absent.

fix: prevent SSE event loss in connectEvents onerror handler

The old onerror handler unconditionally called settle() + es.close() on
every error, then manually reconnected after 1s. This created a race:

1. A recoverable network glitch triggers onerror
2. settle() resolves the Promise immediately -> handleSend proceeds to
   send the prompt
3. es.close() kills the SSE connection -> all events emitted during the
   1s reconnect window (agent_start, message_*, prompt_done, agent_end)
   are lost
4. The UI stays stuck in 'waiting for model' until reconcileAgentState
   (15s polling) recovers

The fix distinguishes between fatal errors (readyState === CLOSED, e.g.
404/500) where manual reconnect is needed, and recoverable errors
(CONNECTING) where EventSource auto-reconnects on its own. For
recoverable errors we no longer settle() or close() - the 1.5s timeout
in the Promise constructor still ensures handleSend won't hang.

## 中文

基于 `v0.8.7..v0.8.8` 的提交整理。本次版本重点如下：

### 重点更新

- **实时会话更可靠**：升级至 Pi `v0.84.1` 并适配新的流式增量协议，增强 SSE 重连、跨标签页恢复和失败提交恢复，减少断流、重复消息与卡住状态（`05db5b2`、`e4fded0`、`6ac87ec`、`6a76151`）。
- **跨工作区任务更清晰**：工作区选择器显示运行中/未读状态，切换时恢复上次会话；后台完成、需要人工处理时可通过声音和浏览器通知及时提醒（`776fcb1`、`c8692e4`、`044af0e`、`3d9acf6`、`598c3c6`）。
- **文件产物更易查看**：回复下方直接列出本轮写入的文件，HTML 默认打开预览；文件标签保留滚动与查看状态，聊天图片支持点击放大，Markdown frontmatter 以元数据卡片展示（`51e0510`、`2e9e0d6`、`e851d30`、`5ae7152`）。
- **移动端体验重做**：采用更紧凑的移动工具栏，支持 Enter 换行与 Ctrl/Cmd+Enter 发送，并修复 iOS PWA 键盘收起后的视口和旋转行为（`0475e14`、`fcfac31`、`5eb71d8`、`99d4ea1`）。

### 更多改进

- 自定义模型支持 provider/model 级请求头和 developer-role 兼容设置；模型价格、思考级别、切换反馈和加载错误展示更清晰，并新增只读工具预设（`d5dff1c`、`c3b741e`、`81767f4`、`4fc2995`、`d60c547`）。
- 分支导航使用分叉消息作为标签；会话统计新增活跃时间、缓存命中率；System 面板可在发送首条消息前加载系统提示词（`c87a9a4`、`360667c`、`8640559`、`c0a6083`）。
- 改善长消息与代码流式渲染性能、滚动跟随、CJK token/TPS 估算和单波浪号显示；修复 Windows 目录浏览、worktree 路径识别与打包兼容问题（`9ebe18a`、`5d6342a`、`3095198`、`a8ba47e`、`f355928`、`b3e1eed`、`6960b2a`）。

## English

Prepared from commits in `v0.8.7..v0.8.8`. Highlights of this release:

### Highlights

- **More reliable live sessions**: upgraded to Pi `v0.84.1` and its new streaming delta protocol, with stronger SSE reconnects, cross-tab recovery, and rejected-submission recovery to prevent dropped streams, duplicate messages, and stuck states (`05db5b2`, `e4fded0`, `6ac87ec`, `6a76151`).
- **Clearer task activity across workspaces**: the workspace selector now shows running and unread activity and restores the last session; sounds and browser notifications cover background completion and requests for attention (`776fcb1`, `c8692e4`, `044af0e`, `3d9acf6`, `598c3c6`).
- **Faster access to generated files**: files written during a turn appear below the reply, HTML opens in preview by default, file tabs preserve viewer state, chat images open in a larger preview, and Markdown frontmatter renders as a metadata card (`51e0510`, `2e9e0d6`, `e851d30`, `5ae7152`).
- **Reworked mobile experience**: a more compact toolbar, Enter for newlines with Ctrl/Cmd+Enter to send, and fixes for the iOS PWA viewport after keyboard dismissal and device rotation (`0475e14`, `fcfac31`, `5eb71d8`, `99d4ea1`).

### More Improvements

- Custom models now support provider/model request headers and developer-role compatibility; pricing, thinking controls, model-switch feedback, load errors, and the new read-only tool preset are clearer (`d5dff1c`, `c3b741e`, `81767f4`, `4fc2995`, `d60c547`).
- Branches are labeled by their diverging messages; session statistics add active time and average cache hit rate; the System panel can load the system prompt before the first message (`c87a9a4`, `360667c`, `8640559`, `c0a6083`).
- Improved performance for long and streaming messages, scroll following, CJK token/TPS estimates, and single-tilde text; fixed Windows directory browsing, worktree path identity, and packaging compatibility (`9ebe18a`, `5d6342a`, `3095198`, `a8ba47e`, `f355928`, `b3e1eed`, `6960b2a`).

The base html.dark .catppuccin-file-icon rule re-applies the colorful Mocha SVG as background-image on top of the monochrome gray set by the @supports background shorthand (higher specificity), so dark mode bled the language colors back through the semi-transparent mask. fix: don't treat a single tilde as strikethrough (CJK ranges) (#392)

`~` is the standard CJK notation for numeric ranges (e.g. "5~7U",
"100~200倍"). GFM strikethrough accepts a single tilde as a delimiter, so
any assistant message with two `~` in one paragraph had the tildes
dropped and an arbitrary span struck through - silently corrupting the
content (a "5~7U" range renders as "57U"). This is common in LLM output
for CJK users.

Pass singleTilde:false to remark-gfm (its supported option) so
strikethrough requires ~~double~~ tildes, leaving single-tilde ranges
literal. Applied via the shared markdown plugin config, so chat, file
preview, and the minimap all honor it.

Fixes #385

fix: don't misparse in-hunk diff lines as file headers (#394)

parseUnifiedPatch checked every line for a "--- "/"+++ " file header,
including lines inside a hunk body. A removed line whose content starts
with "-- " (raw line "--- ...") or an added line whose content starts
with "++ " (raw line "+++ ...") was therefore misread as a new file
header: flushChanges() ran mid-hunk and a bogus extra SplitDiffFile was
started, corrupting the split-diff view. This happens for ordinary
content — Markdown/reStructuredText bullets, and especially diffs that
themselves contain diff text.

Track the remaining line counts from the @@ hunk header (defaulting an
omitted count to 1) and only look for file headers when outside a hunk
body. Inside a hunk, "--- ..."/"+++ ..." lines fall through to the normal
-/+ content handling.

Adds regression tests for header-like in-hunk content and for resuming
header detection across multiple files.

feat: add system appearance theme mode (#408)

Cycle the top-bar control through light, dark, and auto. Auto follows
prefers-color-scheme, updates when the OS theme changes, and is the
default for first-time visitors. Existing light/dark localStorage values
are preserved.

Closes #407

Co-authored-by: lei.zhang003224 <lei.zhang003224@tongdun.net>

fix: render YAML frontmatter as a metadata card in markdown preview (#391)

react-markdown has no frontmatter support, so a leading `---` block was
parsed as CommonMark instead: the opening `---` became an <hr> and the
closing `---` turned the YAML lines into a setext heading, leaking raw
metadata like `title: My Doc` into the rendered preview between two
horizontal rules (and letting remark-math mangle any $ inside it).

- Add remark-frontmatter (yaml only) to both render pipelines so the
  block parses as a `yaml` node and disappears from the rendered output.
- Add parseFrontmatter() (lib/markdown.ts) backed by js-yaml, and a
  FrontmatterCard that renders the metadata above the preview body:
  `title` as a heading, `tags`/`categories`/`keywords` as chips, remaining
  keys as a key/value table with http(s)/mailto values as links.
- Malformed YAML shows no card but is still hidden by the remark plugin;
  documents without frontmatter render exactly as before.

Verified with tsc --noEmit and eslint; the parse pipeline was also
checked with unified directly (frontmatter yields no output, and the
setext-trap / mid-document `---` cases still parse as CommonMark).

Co-authored-by: Alex Yang <agegcn@gmail.com>

fix: compare git-emitted paths correctly on Windows (#388)

* fix: compare git-emitted paths correctly on Windows

`git rev-parse --path-format=absolute` prints POSIX-style absolute paths
even on Windows (`D:/repo`), while `realpathSync()` and the session cwds
recorded by pi are native (`D:\repo`). `resolveProject()` compared the two
with `===`, so on Windows:

- `isTopLevel` was permanently false, which hid the worktree switcher
  entirely and left only the disabled "Open repo root" hint;
- `isWorktreeTopLevel` was therefore also always false, so linked
  worktrees never collapsed into the main repo's `projectRoot` and each
  showed up as a separate phantom project instead of being grouped;
- `listWorktrees()` returned slash-style paths that never matched
  `selectedCwd`, breaking the current-worktree highlight in the sidebar.

Route every path read out of git through `toNativePath()` and compare with
`samePath()`, which also tolerates drive-letter case since Windows paths
are case-insensitive. Branch names deliberately skip normalization so
`feature/x` does not become `feature\x`.

Both helpers live in a new `lib/paths.ts` alongside `isWindowsAbsolutePath()`,
which had been duplicated in `lib/file-access.ts` and `lib/path-security.ts`.
`isFilePathAllowed()` was a byte-for-byte copy of `isPathWithinRoots()` and
now delegates to it, leaving one implementation of the access-control check.
The allowed-roots set keeps its slash-normalized form: it is an internal Set
key that is never displayed, and containment checks re-normalize both sides
anyway, so both path forms authorize identically.

Verified on Windows against real repositories: repo roots now resolve as
top-level, subdirectories still do not, linked worktrees collapse to the
main repo, and `feature/x` keeps its slash. Adds `lib/paths.test.mjs`
covering separator style, drive-letter case and UNC paths.

fix: cap the user message bubble height with a scrollbar (#419)

* feat: restore the last-open session when switching workspaces

Switching to a workspace previously landed on a blank new-session page and
the session open there last had to be re-picked by hand. Record the
selected session per workspace (resolved project root, sharing one slot
across worktrees) in localStorage, and on a cross-project cwd change
look it up against the live session list to restore it.

A deleted or drifted session clears the memory and keeps the welcome
page; a failed list fetch keeps the memory for a later retry. A token
guard drops stale async restores after a rapid switch sequence.

fix: guard oversized message rendering (100KB+) against browser freeze (#418)

Multi-hundred-KB messages (pasted HAR/log dumps) freeze the browser
because react-markdown + KaTeX + syntax highlighting run on the entire
payload. SafeMarkdownBody renders such messages as a click-to-reveal
plain-text <pre> instead; applies to user messages and assistant text
blocks. i18n: en/zh-CN.

feat: play completion sound for tasks finishing in other workspaces (#417)

The completion tone previously lived in ChatWindow, so only the active
session could ring. Audio ownership moves up to AppShell so a task that
finishes in a non-active workspace (whose ChatWindow is not mounted) can
still notify. SessionSidebar already detects completedInBackground while
polling running sessions; it now reports those via a new onBackgroundTaskDone

owning its own AudioContext.

perf: skip syntax highlighting while a message is streaming (#433)

* perf: cut streamed-render CPU — skip Prism while streaming, memoize CodeBlock and toolResults map

Streaming updates re-rendered the live message on every SSE message_update,
re-tokenizing the whole growing code block with Prism each time. Render code
fences as plain monospace text while the message is streaming and highlight
once on completion.

Also memoize CodeBlock (unchanged code must not re-run tokenization when the
parent markdown re-renders) and hoist ChatWindow's toolResults Map into a
useMemo keyed on messages so its identity stays stable across streaming
updates.

fix: custom headers and compat for custom models (#456)

* feat: add headers and compat for custom models

Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints often need per-request headers
(such as User-Agent for gateway bot detection) and a compat flag to
fall back to the system role when the server rejects the developer
role. These previously required hand-editing models.json.

* headers editor at both provider and model level, with model-level
  values overriding the provider for that model

  compat value and writes an explicit per-model override

Co-authored-by: Alex Yang <agegcn@gmail.com>

Strip skill XML from session auto-naming (#457)

A new session whose first message is a /skill: invocation stores the
SDK-expanded <skill> block as the message, so the no-name fallback
(firstMessage.slice(0, 50)) leaked that XML into the sidebar title and
the rename input. Collapse such blocks to the compact /skill:name args
command via the existing skillExpansionToCommand helper before slicing,
mirroring MessageView's rendering.

The rename input seeds from the same collapsed form, so an untouched
rename of a skill-invoked session stays a no-op instead of persisting
the raw XML as the session name.

fix: resolve hydration mismatch from browser extensions and responsive aria-valuemax (#463)

Two sources of hydration mismatch on initial page load:

1. Browser extensions (Grammarly, translation, password managers) mutate
   the <body> element's attributes before React hydrates. <html> already
   had suppressHydrationWarning but <body> did not.

2. The sidebar resize separator's aria-valuemax was computed via
   effectiveMaxWidth() during render, which calls getMaxWidth(). On the
   server this returns the constant maxWidth, but on the client it
   returns a viewport-dependent value, causing a mismatch for viewports
   between 641px and 799px wide. Gate the responsive computation behind
   a mounted flag so the initial render uses the constant maxWidth.

fix(streaming): count CJK as ~1 token for accurate TPS estimate (#467)

* fix(streaming): count CJK as ~1 token for accurate TPS estimate

chars/4 under-counts CJK by ~4-5x (1 CJK char = 0.25 token vs ~1 token
in GLM/DeepSeek/GPT-o200k). Add an inline estimateTokens() that counts
CJK chars as ~1 token each and keeps ~4 chars/token for the rest; use it
for the streaming TPS badge and estimated-token count.

* perf(streaming): cache token estimate updates

Co-authored-by: lyhue1991 <lyhue1991@126.com>
Co-authored-by: Alex Yang <agegcn@gmail.com>

fix: suppress DEP0190 deprecation when auto-opening browser (#468)

* fix: suppress DEP0190 deprecation when auto-opening browser

Starting pi-web on Windows prints a Node.js DEP0190 deprecation warning:

  (node:XXXXX) [DEP0190] DeprecationWarning: Passing args to a child
  process with shell option true can lead to security vulnerabilities,
  as the arguments are not escaped, only concatenated.

This is emitted by the browser auto-open call, which used
`spawn(openCmd, [url], { shell: isWindows })`. DEP0190 triggers
whenever args are passed together with `shell: true`.

Refactor the call to avoid `shell: true` entirely while preserving
the same auto-open behavior:
- Windows: invoke `cmd.exe /c start "" <url>` directly so the URL
  is passed as a structured argv (the empty title is required by the
  `start` built-in).
- macOS / Linux: spawn `open` / `xdg-open` without `shell`.

* fix: validate browser launch port

The right panel previously rendered only the active file tab, so every

position, zoom, and viewer state. Now all open tabs stay mounted and
inactive ones are hidden with display:none; closing a tab (removing it
from fileTabs) still unmounts and frees it.

## English

Prepared from commits in `v0.9.0..v0.9.1`.

### Added

- Added provider usage quota visibility (`6d53fd5`).
- Expanded the built-in subagent workflow with concurrent queues, persisted recovery, worktree isolation, profiles, and extension tool selectors (`f106531`, `b77a25f`, `a31d5c5`, `bbe2f7d`, `2661247`, `e3fbbf6`).

* fix: default terminal shells to a UTF-8 locale

On Windows the spawned shell inherited the system ANSI codepage
(GBK on zh-CN hosts). Non-ASCII filenames were emitted in GBK and
only some bytes happened to decode as valid UTF-8, so a subset of
CJK characters rendered while the rest showed as tofu or

fix(push): make iOS background delivery actually work (#728)

* fix(push): make iOS background delivery actually work

Delivery investigation on a real iOS home-screen web app showed that
background pushes never arrived while the same subscriptions worked once
the VAPID subject was corrected. Three independent causes, all fixed here:

1. Invalid VAPID subject: Apple's push service rejects
   `mailto:pi-web@localhost` with 403 BadJwtToken, so every send failed
   before leaving the server. The subject now defaults to the project
   homepage (a valid https URL) and can be overridden with
   PI_WEB_PUSH_SUBJECT.

2. Subscription poisoning via suppressed notifications: the service
   worker skipped showNotification whenever an app window was visible.
   iOS revokes the push subscription when a push is handled without a
   notification, so every foreground-observed completion silently
   poisoned the subscription until background delivery stopped entirely
   (servers keep getting 201 from APNs, so nothing visible in logs).
   The SW now always shows the notification; same-tag notifications
   replace each other, so a visible window just sees it re-appear.

3. Deferred delivery: sends had no Urgency/TTL, so iOS may defer them to
   an arbitrary later wake-up window. Sends now use urgency=high with a
   4-week TTL.

Also adds a "register push" control to Settings → General. On iOS the
permission prompt must run inside a user gesture and cannot be
re-triggered after a home-screen re-install, and the previous code only
subscribed automatically after a task completion, which could leave a
freshly installed home-screen app without any subscription path. The
button reuses setupPushSubscription() and lives next to the language
section.

Verified: node --test (push/sw suites 15/15), eslint, tsc --noEmit.

* fix(push): allow permission prompts and retries

seeding with whitelist preservation, alias-based flag fallback). npm test

## 中文

`v0.9.2` 重点改善了模型管理、长会话性能、多标签页体验，以及子代理运行的可靠性。同时补齐了一批文件查看、上传、插件管理和跨平台兼容问题。

> [!IMPORTANT]
> 如果 Pi Web 可从公网访问，建议尽快升级。旧版使用的 Next.js 版本存在无需登录即可在服务器上执行代码的安全漏洞；本版已升级到 Next.js 16.3.5 并关闭不必要的图片处理入口。

### 升级

直接运行最新版：

```bash
npx @agegr/pi-web@latest
```

或更新全局安装：

```bash
npm install -g @agegr/pi-web@latest
```

### 模型管理更直观

- 现在可以直接在 **设置 → 模型** 中启用或停用单个模型，也可以按模型服务商批量操作，不再需要手动编辑配置文件。已有选择、思考级别设置和暂时不可用的条目会被尽量保留；项目级配置存在时，界面会明确提示当前设置只读。([#930](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/930))
- 新增 **刷新模型列表** 按钮。模型服务商发布新模型后，可以立即获取最新列表，无需等待 Pi Web 更新，也无需先运行 Pi 命令行工具；离线模式下会给出明确提示。([#938](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/938))
- 由扩展添加的模型服务商现在也会出现在模型设置和登录页面中，可以正常管理其 API Key。([#833](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/833))
- 新增 OpenCode Go 用量与额度展示；较早的用量数据会显示“多久前更新”，避免把旧数据误认为当天数据。([#844](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/844), [8b084d3](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/commit/8b084d338))

### 长会话更快、更完整

- 会话列表会先显示已有信息，再在后台补充尚未读取的详情；会话搜索不会因为后台活动而反复刷新和重新排序。切回最近打开的会话时，会立即恢复已经加载的内容，也不会丢掉用户手动加载过的更早记录。([#940](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/940))
- 自动生成会话名称时，不再把整段历史和所有工具输出发送给模型。在 120 轮会话的基准中，模型输入量从约 74,000 token 降到约 1,700，耗时从约 3.8 秒降到约 1.3 秒。([#807](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/807))
- 加载长会话时，现在按用户实际能看到的消息计算分页，不会再让大量隐藏的工具记录挤占首屏。一个包含 15 条用户消息、562 条内部记录的真实会话，旧版首屏只显示 1 条用户消息；本版不再出现这种情况。([#810](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/810))
- 每个浏览器标签页会分别记住自己打开的会话。刷新一个标签页时，不会再被另一个标签页最近打开的会话带走。([#887](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/887))
- 从 Pi 命令行或另一个 Pi 进程写入同一会话的内容，在重新打开或刷新会话后可以正确显示。([#796](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/796))

### 对话与文件操作更顺手

- 侧栏中的会话列表与文件列表可以拖动分隔线调整高度。文件查看器也可以临时展开到全宽，退出后会恢复原来的布局和预览状态。([#825](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/825), [#790](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/790))
- 离开对话底部后，会出现“滚动到最新”按钮。聊天滚动条也更清晰、更容易拖动；把鼠标放到右侧会话导航条上时，可以看到每轮调用了多少次工具。([#845](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/845), [#932](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/932), [#939](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/939))
- 发送前可以预览图片附件。工具返回的截图或生成图片即使在工具卡片折叠时也会保持可见，点击 Markdown 图片还可以打开大图预览。([#735](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/735), [#826](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/826))
- GPT 通过 `apply_patch` 修改文件时，会显示文件名和左右对照的代码差异，不再只显示原始数据；用户手动展开的工具卡片在回复继续生成时也不会自动收起。([#744](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/744), [#743](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/743))
- 当回复因为模型输出上限而被截断时，消息下方会显示明确提示，不再像正常结束一样静默停止。运行过程中也会继续显示本轮实际使用的思考级别。([#830](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/830), [#777](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/777))
- 新增 `/auto-compact` 命令，可直接在聊天中开启或关闭当前会话的自动压缩。([#828](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/828))
- PDF 链接中的页码现在会被保留，例如 `report.pdf#page=12` 会直接打开第 12 页。超过 10 MB 的上传也不再被中间层提前截断，可使用 Pi Web 原有的单次 100 MB 上传额度。([#841](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/841), [#846](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/846))
- “已修改文件”列表新增快捷引用按钮，可一键把文件路径插入输入框；较长路径会保留完整文件名，便于区分。([#853](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/853))

### 子代理更可控

这里的“子代理”指主对话派出去独立处理一项工作的任务。

- 可以单独停用 `general-purpose`、`explore` 或 `plan` 等内置子代理，无需复制和维护一份内置配置。([#934](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/934))
- 后台子代理的结果只会交付一次：如果主代理已经主动取得结果，完成通知不会再触发一次重复处理。([#937](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/937))
- 后台子代理的报告不会再被误当作用户的新指令，因此压缩长会话时不会污染用户目标；完成通知也不会再让前面的回复从当前视图中消失。([#935](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/935), [#891](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/891))
- 模型服务报错时，子代理会正确显示失败原因，不再误报为成功但没有输出。前台子代理完成后也会返回会话 ID，方便继续或恢复该任务。([#886](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/886), [#847](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/847))

### 稳定性、兼容性与安全

- 新会话现在会遵循 Pi 配置中的默认工具，不再静默替换成 Pi Web 内置的四项工具；只有用户明确选择工具预设时才会覆盖配置。([#936](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/936))
- 修复回复生成时首段文字、思考内容或工具参数短暂重复的问题，以及开发模式下切回正在运行的会话时，实时内容偶尔要等刷新后才出现的问题。([#835](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/835), [#933](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/933))
- 安装为网页应用后，如果服务器端口仍可连接但服务没有响应，页面最多等待 8 秒便会显示离线页，不再无限白屏。([#879](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/879))
- Windows 上的 npm 插件更新检查和路径处理已修复，并支持通过 Windows 网络共享路径打开文件；RISC-V 设备的启动兼容性也得到改善。([#837](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/837), [#827](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/827), [c04bab7](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/commit/c04bab75e), [#823](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/823))
- 创建 Git 工作树（并行检出目录）时，大型仓库有更充足的处理时间；本地没有目标分支时，会优先从已有的远程跟踪分支创建。([#732](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/732))
- 升级 Next.js 至 16.3.5，修复两个无需登录即可利用的远程代码执行漏洞。Web 登录连续失败时会从 1 秒开始逐步延长等待时间，最长 60 秒；从外部页面返回 Pi Web 时也不会再轻易丢失登录状态。([e5a2434](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/commit/e5a2434d5), [20ad98b](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/commit/20ad98bc9), [#818](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/818))
- 服务重启时会主动关闭仍在等待实时消息的连接，避免旧进程卡住并造成 502。([#809](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/809))

## English

`v0.9.2` focuses on easier model management, faster large sessions, better multi-tab behavior, and more reliable subagents. It also includes file-viewing, upload, plugin, platform, and security fixes.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Upgrade promptly if Pi Web is reachable from the public internet. The Next.js versions used by earlier releases contained vulnerabilities that allowed code execution on the server without authentication. This release upgrades to Next.js 16.3.5 and disables an unnecessary image-processing endpoint.

### Upgrade

Run the latest version directly:

```bash
npx @agegr/pi-web@latest
```

Or update a global installation:

```bash
npm install -g @agegr/pi-web@latest
```

### Easier model management

- Models can now be enabled or disabled directly from **Settings → Models**, individually or by model service, without editing configuration files by hand. Existing selections, reasoning-level settings, and temporarily unavailable entries are preserved where possible; project-level overrides are clearly shown as read-only. ([#930](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/930))
- A new **Refresh catalog** action fetches recently released models that are not bundled with the current Pi Web version. There is no longer a need to wait for another Pi Web release or run the Pi CLI first; offline mode is reported clearly. ([#938](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/938))
- Model services added by extensions now appear in Models settings and authentication screens, including API-key management. ([#833](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/833))
- OpenCode Go usage and quota information is now available. Older usage snapshots show relative time so they are not mistaken for data from today. ([#844](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/844), [8b084d3](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/commit/8b084d338))

### Faster, more complete large sessions

- The session list can show known information first and fill in uncached details in the background. Search results no longer keep refreshing and reordering during agent activity. Returning to a recent session restores loaded content immediately and keeps any earlier history the user already requested. ([#940](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/940))
- Automatic session naming no longer sends the full history and every tool result to the model. In the 120-turn benchmark, model input dropped from about 74,000 tokens to 1,700 and elapsed time dropped from about 3.8 seconds to 1.3 seconds. ([#807](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/807))
- Long-session pagination now counts messages that are actually visible. In one real session with 15 user messages and 562 internal records, the old first page showed only one user message; this release no longer lets hidden tool data crowd the conversation out. ([#810](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/810))
- Each browser tab remembers its own open session. Reloading one tab no longer sends it to whichever session another tab opened most recently. ([#887](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/887))
- Content written to a session by the Pi CLI or another Pi process is now visible after reopening or refreshing that session. ([#796](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/796))

### Better chat and file workflows

- The session and file lists in the sidebar can be resized by dragging their divider. The file viewer can also expand to full width and return to the previous layout without reloading the preview. ([#825](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/825), [#790](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/790))
- A jump-to-latest button appears after scrolling away from the bottom. Chat scrollbars are now visible and easier to grab, and the conversation navigator shows the number of tool calls in each turn. ([#845](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/845), [#932](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/932), [#939](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/939))
- Image attachments can be previewed before sending. Screenshots and generated images remain visible when a tool card is collapsed, and Markdown images can be opened in the full-screen preview. ([#735](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/735), [#826](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/826))
- File changes made through `apply_patch` now show file names and side-by-side code differences instead of raw data. Tool cards opened by the user also remain open while the response continues. ([#744](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/744), [#743](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/743))
- Replies cut off by a model's output limit now show a clear warning instead of looking normally complete. The active reasoning level also remains visible while a turn is running. ([#830](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/830), [#777](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/777))
- The new `/auto-compact` command toggles automatic conversation compaction for the current session. ([#828](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/828))
- PDF links keep their requested page, so `report.pdf#page=12` opens directly on page 12. Uploads above 10 MB are no longer cut off by the proxy layer and can use Pi Web's existing 100 MB per-upload allowance. ([#841](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/841), [#846](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/846))
- Changed-file rows now have a shortcut for inserting the file path into the composer, and long paths preserve the full file name. ([#853](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/853))

### More controllable subagents

A subagent is a task delegated by the main conversation to work independently.

- Built-in subagents such as `general-purpose`, `explore`, and `plan` can be disabled individually without copying and maintaining their definitions. ([#934](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/934))
- Background results are delivered only once. If the parent agent already collected a result, the completion notification no longer starts another turn with the same result. ([#937](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/937))
- Background reports are no longer mistaken for new user instructions, preventing them from changing the user's recorded goals during conversation compaction. Completion notifications also no longer hide earlier replies from the current view. ([#935](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/935), [#891](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/891))
- Model-service errors now mark subagent runs as failed and preserve the reason, instead of reporting success with no output. Foreground completions also include the subagent session ID so the run can be resumed later. ([#886](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/886), [#847](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/847))

### Reliability, compatibility, and security

- New sessions now inherit Pi's configured default tools instead of silently replacing them with Pi Web's four-tool preset. A tool preset overrides that configuration only after the user explicitly selects one. ([#936](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/936))
- Fixed the first streamed text, reasoning, or tool-input chunk briefly appearing twice. In development mode, returning to a running session now resumes live output immediately instead of waiting for a page refresh. ([#835](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/835), [#933](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/933))
- An installed web app now waits at most eight seconds before showing its offline page when the server accepts a connection but never responds, instead of remaining blank indefinitely. ([#879](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/879))
- Fixed npm plugin update checks and path handling on Windows, preserved Windows network-share paths, and improved RISC-V startup compatibility. ([#837](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/837), [#827](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/827), [c04bab7](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/commit/c04bab75e), [#823](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/823))
- Git worktree creation allows more time for large repositories and starts from an existing remote-tracking branch when the target branch is not available locally. ([#732](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/732))
- Upgraded Next.js to 16.3.5 to patch two unauthenticated remote-code-execution vulnerabilities. Failed web-password attempts now receive increasing delays from one second up to 60 seconds, and returning from an external page no longer commonly signs users out. ([e5a2434](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/commit/e5a2434d5), [20ad98b](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/commit/20ad98bc9), [#818](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/818))
- Server shutdown now closes outstanding live-message connections so an old process does not linger and leave the proxy returning 502 errors after a restart. ([#809](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/809))

### Other improvements

- Plugin details now include the package description. Extension widgets keep their configured order and follow the chat font-size setting. ([#868](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/868), [#839](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/839), [#733](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/733))
- Updated the Pi core packages to 0.87.0. ([#931](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web/pull/931))

fix(auth): throttle web password failures with global backoff

429 with Retry-After while blocked and surface the wait on the login page.

Show the reasoning level of the running turn (#777)

* Show the reasoning level of the running turn

The reasoning control is hidden while a turn streams because the level
cannot be changed mid-turn. That also hides the level itself, exactly when
it decides how long the turn runs and how much budget it spends.

Render the active level as a read-only label in the same slot while
streaming. It is not a button: nothing can change until the turn ends, so
a clickable control would only invite clicks that do nothing. The label
reuses the existing display label, icon, padding, height, and mobile
collapse rule, so the control row keeps its spacing next to Stop.

* Address review: show the level the turn actually runs with

Choosing "Use pi default" sets the selector to "auto" without touching the
runtime, so the runtime can keep an earlier explicit level. Rendering the
selector state while streaming would then label a turn "auto" that is in
fact running at, say, "high".

When a turn starts, read the runtime's thinking level from the agent state
and adopt it, so the read-only label and the selector both reflect the
level in effect. The lookup is skipped if the turn has already ended.

fix: see sessions written by another pi process (#796)

* fix: see sessions written by another pi process

A live in-memory wrapper only reflects the appends pi-web itself made. When
another pi process (the TUI) writes the same session file, the wrapper's entries
silently diverge from disk, and GET /api/sessions/[id] kept serving that stale
snapshot. The refresh button cannot help, by construction: it re-requests the
same shadowed endpoint. The new output stayed invisible until the wrapper was
evicted by the 10-minute idle timeout.

Detect that the newest on-disk entry id is unknown to the wrapper, then drop the
wrapper so the request rebuilds from the file. Eviction is limited to idle
wrappers: mid-run the wrapper owns the write path, so an external write then is
the genuinely unsupported concurrent-write case rather than a stale read.

Rebuilding is safe because startRpcSession restores the persisted tool selection
from the file and the model from its model_change entries, so an evicted session
comes back on the same path as any cold start after idle eviction or restart.

The bounded tail probe skips the session header, which carries the session id
rather than an entry id (the SDK's entry index excludes it), and tolerates a torn
trailing line, since appendFileSync is not atomic from a reader's perspective.

Regression coverage:
- lib/session-reader-latest-entry.test.mjs covers the probe (newest id, header
  skip, torn trailing line, absent file, bounded read, CRLF).
- lib/session-reader-external-write.test.mjs covers the decision on a real
  SessionManager: an externally appended entry is unknown, while a manager's own
  append is always known (no self-eviction loop).
- e2e/run.mjs warms a real wrapper, appends as the TUI would, and asserts the new
  entry becomes visible and that repeated reads stay stable. Without the fix this
  fails with the exact symptom of the report (the appended entry is missing).

* fix: probe session files only on mount and reconnect SSE after eviction

Two processes writing one JSONL is unsupported, so post-turn reads should
keep the live snapshot. Only ?force=1 (session mount / page refresh) scans
the file tail. Destroy now closes attached SSE streams and rechecks
isRunning so an idle-looking wrapper cannot be disposed mid-prompt.

Name sessions from a bounded transcript (#807)

* Name sessions from a bounded transcript, on a model you can choose

Naming currently clones the session's agent state: the system prompt, the
tool definitions, and the whole message history, with the title request
appended to the trailing user message. The cost of naming therefore tracks
the size of the session, and depends on whether the session's prefix is
still cached.

Send a plain-text transcript instead. Every user turn is kept because it
carries the intent; replies are clipped to their opening line, and the
final reply keeps more because it usually holds the outcome. Tool calls and
results are dropped: they dominate the token count and say nothing about
what the session was for. The transcript has a total budget split between
the opening turns and the newest ones, so a 12-turn and a 1200-turn session
produce the same request.

Because the request no longer reuses the session's prefix, there is no
cache to lose by naming with a different model, so a title model can be
configured. It defaults to the session's own model, leaving current
behaviour unchanged, and thinking is set to the cheapest level the chosen
model actually supports.

Measured on 1, 8, 20, and 120-turn sessions with the same session model:
the request is flat at about 1.7k tokens and 1.3s instead of growing to
74k tokens and 3.8s, and a cold naming costs the same as a warm one.
Across five adversarial session shapes, over three runs, the titles still
name the real subject.

* Keep the bounded title transcript; drop the configurable title model

fix(streaming): stop duplicating the first streamed chunk (#835)

Pi's assistant `message_start` snapshot can already contain a block's first
delta: pi-ai documents `partial` as a shared live response-so-far helper, not
an event-time snapshot, so a snapshot read at `*_start` may carry the chunk
that the following `*_delta` delivers again.

The reducer kept that text when `text_start`/`thinking_start` arrived and then
appended the delta a second time, rendering the first word twice until the
authoritative `*_end` replaced the whole block. Streamed tool input had the
same problem.

matching pi-ai's documented semantics (empty at start, grown only by deltas,
`*_end` authoritative) and pi's own AssistantMessageEventProxy.

lib/streaming-message.test.mjs.

Markdown links such as `[report.pdf#page=12](/api/files/...?type=read#page=12)`

fix(pwa): bound the navigation and asset fetches so a dead upstream cannot hang (#879)

A reachable port with a dead upstream accepts the connection and then never
answers, so fetch() neither resolves nor rejects. The navigation therefore
never fell back to offline.html — it stayed blank until the browser gave up —
and a static asset cache miss left the page waiting on a request that would
never finish.

the timer is cleared as soon as the headers arrive, so a streamed SSR body is
never cut off mid-stream.

No shell or data caching is introduced here: the worker still keeps only
offline.html and the static assets in its cache.

fix(chat): reopen the session event stream under Strict Mode effect re-runs (#933)

Switching to another session and back while its agent was still running left
the chat frozen in the dev server: no streamed output appeared and the
finished reply only showed up after the 15-second reconcile poll or a page
refresh. Opening a running session directly had the same problem.

React Strict Mode (on by default in `next dev`) re-runs every effect after a
simulated unmount, in declaration order. The mount-only effect's cleanup
flips `sessionHookMountedRef` to false and only restores it when that effect
re-runs, which happens after the warm-session effect. `shouldMaintain()`
therefore refused the SSE connection and the selected session never opened
its event stream; only `handleSend` (which connects explicitly) worked.

Re-assert the ref in the warm-session effect before maintaining the stream.
Verified with a Playwright run against a slow fake model: before the fix the
switch-back never requested `/api/agent/[id]/events`; after it the stream
reconnects immediately and the streamed words render as they arrive.
`next start` was unaffected because it does not double-invoke effects.

fix(subagents): mark background results as non-user messages (#875) (#935)

pi's `convertToLlm` replays every `custom` message to the model as a
plain `user` turn with its content verbatim, and a background subagent's
completion is delivered through `sendCustomMessage`. Compaction then
summarizes from those converted messages under a prompt that asks what
*the user* is trying to accomplish and which constraints *the user*
mentioned, so the subagent's report is read as user intent and lands in
the summary's Goal / Constraints sections.

stating that it is a subagent report rather than a user message. Doing it
in code instead of in the subagent's prompt keeps the marker from being
dropped by the model. Foreground `Agent` and `get_subagent_result` results
are unchanged: they are already `toolResult` messages and need no marker.

fix(tools): stop overriding settings.json defaultTools on new sessions (#700) (#936)

Pi Web sent an explicit toolNames array on every session it created, so a new
session was always pinned to the hardcoded "default" preset (read, bash, edit,
write) even for users who had never opened the tool picker. That silently
narrowed the loadout configured in ~/.pi/agent/settings.json and made Pi Web
disagree with the `pi` CLI over the same agent directory.

Add a "configured" preset that stands for "send no override". Picking it omits
toolNames entirely, which the server already handles: startRpcSession leaves
the allow-list unset and falls back to the SDK's resolved active tools, and no
pi-web:tool-selection entry is written, so the session keeps following the
setting. It is also the fallback when no preference is stored, since only an
explicit pick from the dropdown is ever persisted - so "never chose" no longer
means "pinned to our four built-ins".

Returning an already pinned session to the configured defaults needs a way to
retract the pin, and the session log is append-only. Add a `cleared: true`
tool-selection entry for that; readSessionToolSelection treats it as "no
selection" while a later pin still wins. Clearing rebuilds the session, because
the loadout defaultTools resolves to is only known once pi builds it.

The picker labels an unpinned session "configured" rather than borrowing
whichever concrete preset its resolved tools happen to match, so the reverse
mapping is now typed to the concrete presets only.

fix(subagents): drop the completion notification for an already collected result (#889) (#937)

A background subagent unconditionally notified its parent when it finished,
even when the parent had already taken the same result through
`get_subagent_result`. The notification is sent with `triggerTurn: true`, so
the parent woke a new turn and processed the result a second time, pushing its
real final summary away from the bottom of the chat.

`get_subagent_result` now marks a finished background run as consumed, and
`notifyParent` takes that mark instead of sending. Checking it only when the
completion promise resolves would not help: at that moment the parent is
usually still inside its `get_subagent_result` poll (500ms interval), and
`deliverAs: "followUp"` would queue the duplicate until that turn ends. So the
notification is held while the parent `isRunning()` and the mark is re-checked
before sending. An idle parent is still notified immediately, and a result the
parent never collected is still delivered once the parent goes idle.

feat(models): add a manual "Refresh catalog" button to the Models panel (#914) (#938)

pi's built-in model lists are generated when the SDK is built and pi-web
pins one SDK version, so a model a provider ships after that release is
invisible until pi-web publishes a new version.

The SDK already carries the other half: each built-in provider is wrapped
in a pi.dev catalog overlay that ModelRuntime.refresh() fetches and
persists to ~/.pi/agent/models-store.json, and restoring that overlay
needs no network. Both of pi-web's refresh paths ask for the offline half
only (createAgentSessionServices() and lib/provider-usage.ts pass
allowNetwork: false), which is why running the pi CLI once was the known
workaround — the CLI refreshes with the network on and pi-web read what
it left behind.

The button next to Enable all / Disable all runs that pass for the
provider on screen, through POST /api/models/refresh. Nothing refreshes
catalogs on a timer or on another request's path: a pass fetches a
catalog per authenticated provider, and a save must not wait on a slow
one — the same reason the API-key route stores the credential itself
instead of calling ModelRuntime.login().

- refresh() is called with force: true, since pressing the button is
  exactly a request to skip the SDK's four-hour freshness window, but
  without allowNetwork, so the runtime keeps applying its own PI_OFFLINE
  rule instead of pi-web overriding it. PI_OFFLINE is reported as such
  rather than reported as a pass that ran.
- shareModelCatalogRefresh() joins concurrent presses for the same
  providers so two tabs cannot race over the store file.
- Change detection compares the model ids and names the runtime exposes,
  never the stored bytes: a successful revalidation rewrites checkedAt
  and etag on every pass. It only decides whether the caches are dropped
  and the panel reloads — the catalog itself reaches the UI through the
  ordinary /api/models and /api/models/enabled loads, so the route never
  returns a model list of its own.

The integration test stubs pi.dev and asserts that a model the pinned SDK
has never heard of reaches a separate runtime built with the network
untouched — the list GET /api/models serves.

file had been read.

header and stat alone, marking those rows detailsPending. The sidebar paints

remounted. Pending rows show an ellipsis instead of a message count.

sessions are now also capped by their summed on-disk size, and a session

can produce on disk.

}

    extract_policy=ExtractPolicy(),
    mapping_policy=mapping_policy
)

- Actual installed version was 0.10.2/0.11.0
- Root cause: version.py tried to read pyproject.toml which doesn't exist in installed packages

- Fall back to reading pyproject.toml only for development environments

Version detection priority:
1. importlib.metadata.version() - works for pip install, pip install -e, and production

3. Return "0.0.0-dev" - fallback for edge cases

## [0.16.0] - 2026-03-02

### Added

- **WebSocket infrastructure** (All SDKs): Persistent WebSocket connections for sessions (`wsUrl`), push notification callbacks (`registerCallback`/`unregisterCallback`), stream cancellation with `WsCancelledError`, and a true synchronous WS client for Python.
- **Session keep-alive & idle release timeout** (All SDKs): Prevent idle timeout disconnections; configurable `idle_release_timeout` in session creation.
- **New API models** (All SDKs): MQTT token, volume operations, skills metadata listing, and official skills sandbox APIs.
- **Java enhancements**: Auto release support, `executeCommand` stdout/stderr separation, browser agent interface unification.
- **Python enhancements**: Browser agent interface unification, page use login API.
- **Screenshot improvements**: Full-page screenshot support, type/mime_type fields, beta long screenshot with JPEG quality.
- **Context sync**: Optional ID filtering for context synchronization.
- **Cookbook**: LangChain DeepAgents skills sandbox; renamed Moltbot to OpenClaw.
- **Developer tools**: Tiered knowledge builder for AI context files; enhanced Config class with defaults.

### Changed

- **Removed 50s timeout cap on `execute_command`** (All SDKs): The SDK-side 50-second timeout limit has been removed. Custom `timeout_ms` values are now passed through to the backend without capping. Note: the backend gateway may still enforce its own timeout.
- Added managed proxy support, clear API, and removed legacy Java browser config.

### Fixed

- macOS SSL compatibility for WsClient (Python); drop malformed WS messages without invocationId.
- Browser: destroy not resetting params, `get_window` title null, browser.agent crash.
- Mobile: null `link_url` in screenshot, `get_installed_apps` error.
- Pause/Resume for both async and sync APIs; protobuf compatibility; dotenv loading guard.
- Unit test stability improvements across CI.

### Security

- Dependency updates: protobuf 3.20.3→5.29.6, setuptools, urllib3, lodash, axios, js-yaml, next 14.2.33→15.5.10.

## [0.17.0] - 2026-03-16

### Added

- **run_code WebSocket streaming** (All SDKs): Added WebSocket-based streaming for code execution, enabling real-time output delivery during `run_code` operations.
- **Browser autoLogin & callForUser** (All SDKs): Added `autoLogin` and `callForUser` options for browser sessions, with captcha-solving examples and call-for-user notification channel support.
- **Dynamic context binding** (All SDKs): Support for binding contexts to sessions dynamically at runtime.
- **BrowserSyncMode** (All SDKs): Added `MINIMAL`/`STANDARD` whitelist modes for browser synchronization.
- **Cookbook additions**: 4 new cookbooks (computer use, web scraping, streaming, multi-session), browser login persistence, mobile device simulation, OpenClaw Python/Java web service integration with DingTalk bot and FastAPI, Feishu one-click setup, DingTalk credential auto-apply.

### Changed

- **Removed client-side port range validation** (All SDKs): `getLink` no longer validates port ranges on the client side, deferring to backend enforcement.
- **Logger refactoring** (All SDKs): Replaced direct terminal `print`/`console.log`/`fmt.Print` calls with structured logger calls across Python, TypeScript, Golang, and Java.
- **SSE support for get_link HTTPS URLs**: Added documentation for Server-Sent Events over HTTPS link URLs.

### Fixed

- **watchDirectory race condition** (Python, Golang, TypeScript): Fixed a race condition where file operations performed before the filesystem baseline was established would be lost. Added a "ready" signal mechanism (`ready_event`/`readyCh`/`ready` Promise) so callers can wait for baseline establishment before performing file operations.
- **DirectoryWatcher asyncio event loop isolation** (Python): Fixed asyncio event loop isolation issue in `watch_directory`.
- **TypeScript fixes**: Missing `autoLogin`/`callForUser` params in tests, `toolList` type mismatch in POP SDK models.

### Security

- Dependency updates: Jackson 2.15.2→2.18.6 (Java), npm audit fixes for security vulnerabilities.

### Added

- **Skills feature (Beta)** (All SDKs): Skills metadata API (`get_metadata`) and session-level skill loading via `skill_ids` parameter in session creation.
- **Agent streaming output (Beta)** (All SDKs): WebSocket-based streaming for agent task execution with `TaskExecution` handle, delivering real-time reasoning and content events via typed callbacks (`on_reasoning`, `on_content`, `on_call_for_user`, `on_error`). Includes `MobileTaskOptions` and `StreamOptions` for structured configuration.

## [0.19.0] - 2026-04-16

### Added

- **Git module** (All SDKs): Clone, init, commit, status, log, branch management, diff, and remote operations. Dedicated error types (`GitAuthError`, `GitConflictError`, etc.).
- **Session `appInstanceId`** (All SDKs): Exposed on Session class for tracking cloud instance identity.
- **FileSystem `watch_directory` push mode** (Go, Java, Python): Real-time file monitoring via WebSocket push instead of polling.
- **BrowserOperator** (Go): Added Go BrowserOperator, aligned with other SDKs.

### Changed

- **Deprecated `getLinkUrl` / `getToken`** (All SDKs): Use `linkUrl` / `token` properties instead.
- **FileSystem read/write optimization**: Skip chunking for HTTP LinkUrl channel for better performance.
- **`sync()` exponential backoff** (All SDKs): Polling now uses exponential backoff for more efficient synchronization.

### Fixed

- **Java POP API**: Added automatic retry for transient failures.
- **Java ApiKey**: Fixed null value under concurrent multi-thread access.
- **Java call-for-user**: Fixed platform agent notification not working.
- **FileSystem binary read**: Fixed missing `size` field in `BinaryFileContentResult` for LinkUrl reads.

feat(filesystem): share session WsClient for watch_directory push mode

session's single WsClient instead of creating a dedicated one per
monitoring thread.  This fixes concurrent multi-path monitoring
(backend only allows one WS connection per session) and ensures
coexistence with other WS-based services like run_code.

Key changes:
- Two-phase startup: Phase 1 does a synchronous HTTP baseline poll
  to unblock the caller immediately; Phase 2 uses
  run_coroutine_threadsafe to obtain the shared WsClient, subscribe,
  and perform a catch-up poll.
- Add _monitor_polling_after_baseline() as fallback when WS subscribe
  fails after Phase 1 has already set ready_event.
- Reconnection handler uses asyncio.to_thread for catch-up polling
  to avoid blocking the main event loop.

fix(python): enable WS push mode for sync SDK watch_directory

The sync SDK's watch_directory was always falling back to HTTP polling
because the WS push prerequisite check required asyncio.get_running_loop(),
which is never available in sync context.

- Replace _run_async (run_coroutine_threadsafe bridge) with _call_ws
  which auto-detects coroutines vs direct values via asyncio.iscoroutine,
  enabling the same code path to work in both async and sync SDKs

  has its own internal event loop thread and exposes blocking methods
- Fix sync WsClient.on_connection_state_change to return unsubscribe
  callable (was discarding return value)

271605224.body:
Agentgateway is an open source project that is built on AI-native protocols to connect, secure, and observe agent-to-agent and agent-to-tool communication across any agent framework and environment.

This release is one of the largest Agentgateway releases to date, and includes significant new features and improvements.

## New Features

* Added support for Mutual TLS listeners
* LLM Prompt Guards now support multiple prompt guards, in an ordered list
* Added support for automatic LLM Prompt Caching
* Added support for LLM Embeddings
* Added support for OpenAI Responses API
* Added support for Anthropic Count Tokens API
* Added support for `Basic` authentication
* Added support for API Key authentication
* Support for stateful routing to MCP backends
* Added support for HTTP-based External Authorization servers (in addition to the existing gRPC support). Check out the examples using this to integrate with [Tailscale](./examples/tailscale-auth) and [Oauth2 Proxy](./examples/oauth2-proxy)!
* CIDR and IP support for CEL expressions. See the [example](./examples/http/config.yaml) for a sample IP authorization allowlist!
* Added support for the Azure OpenAI provider
* Policies can now be specified on `listeners`, allowing policies to run before routing occurs.
* A new concept of "Frontend Policies" has been added. These can be configured at the top level `frontendPolicies` field. Frontend policies define how to handle incoming traffic, and can be dynamically updated. This includes fields to customize TCP, TLS, and HTTP behavior, as well as logging and tracing.
* New fields have been exposed to CEL expressions: `response.headers`, `apiKey`, `basicAuth`, `llm.params.{dimensions,encoding_format}` (for Embeddings), and `source.{subjectAltNames,issuer,subject,subjectCn}` (for Mutual TLS).

## Kubernetes Controller (Kgateway)

When deploying Agentgateway, it is recommended to run with [Kgateway](https://agentgateway.dev/docs/kubernetes/) which provides a first class Kubernetes controller (with Gateway API support). In addition to the features above, this release paves the way for the upcoming Kgateway v2.2.0, which is a major leap forward in running Agentgateway on Kubernetes.

This release will further decoupled Agentgateway from Kgateway's Envoy-based components, including...

* A new set of APIs: `AgentgatewayPolicy`, `AgentgatewayBackend`, and `AgentgatewayParameters`.
* A new Helm chart for Agentgateway usage.
* A new controller image dedicated to Agentgateway.

These new changes will avoid confusion between the two dataplane modes of Kgateway, and enhance our ability to deliver features quickly.

Please note, these changes represent a breaking change in the v2.1.0 to v2.2.0 upgrade.
Please consult the [migration guide](https://github.com/kgateway-dev/kgateway/blob/main/docs/guides/agentgateway-migration.md), and stay tuned for the official v2.2.0 release!

## Breaking Changes

* When using the `promptGuard` policy type, guards (`regex`, `webhook`, `moderation`, etc) are now specified in an ordered list.
* When using the `extAuthz` policy type, a new field `protocol` is required. To retain the old behavior, set this to `grpc`.
* When using an `ai` backend type, the following fields have been moved: `backendAuth`, `backendTLS`, `promptGuard`, `prompts`, `overrides`, `defaults`, `modelAliases`. Instead, these are now under `policies.backendAuth`, and similar for the others. In addition, all backend policies may now be set on the new field, instead of just the subset that was previously allowed.
* The `config.listener` settings have been moved to `frontendPolicies`.

## What's Changed
* cleanup: remove unused funcs by @jenshu in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/592
* Implement new Xds API  by @howardjohn in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/588
* chore: remove deprecated github.com/golang/protobuf by @Juneezee in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/600
* Ensure JWT claims are available to route‑level CEL expressions by @webcodes-cz in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/599
* Fix inline backend policies ("filters") by @howardjohn in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/604
* feat: Support optional JWT audience validation by @heojay in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/606
* Add Basic Authentication and API Key authentication by @howardjohn in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/605
* backends: support inline policies by @howardjohn in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/610
* proto: support multiple jwt providers by @howardjohn in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/611
* fix stack overflow with large OpenAPI by @howardjohn in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/612
* ext authz: allow sending metadata like JWT by @howardjohn in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/613
* ui: AI backend fixes by @jenshu in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/607
* Automatically rewrite hostname by @howardjohn in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/522
* Fix accidental log line by @howardjohn in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/615
* JWT unit tests by @puertomontt in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/581
* local config: give useful errors on AI issues by @howardjohn in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/616
* Azure OpenAI support by @jenshu in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/589
* Add security policy by @howardjohn in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/624
* perf: do not generate an unused error on the dns hotpath by @howardjohn in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/622
* refactored backend forms to use full URLs for MCP and SSE targets, re… by @peterj in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/561
* feat: responses api and bedrock features by @apexlnc in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/603
* Bump deps by @howardjohn in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/623
* support for Anthropic models with Vertex by @puertomontt in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/643
* Support pseudo headers in HTTP route matching by @Copilot in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/626
* Add support for double-hbone by @ymesika in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/591
* feat: enable route and gateway targeting for backend policies by @apexlnc in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/629
* add 'timeout' to 'extAuthz' config for local input by @stoicflame in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/644

🎉 Welcome to the 1.0.0-alpha.3 release of the agentgateway project!

## Artifacts

**Binaries** are available below.

## Quick Start

Follow the [Kubernetes](https://agentgateway.dev/docs/kubernetes/latest/quickstart/) or [Standalone](https://agentgateway.dev/docs/standalone/latest/quickstart/) quick start guide to get started!


## What's Changed
* Fix version number in release by @howardjohn in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/1072
* Do not use a stale version in cargo by @howardjohn in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/1075
* release: properly tag images with 'v' prefix by @howardjohn in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/1074
* Revert "fix: Overlays can delete map elements with 'null'" by @chandler-solo in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/1079
* client: do not swallow logs from Body by @howardjohn in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/1076
* Copy tcp routes when inserting listener by @i11 in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/1085
* Provide Istio mesh config to XDS builder by @ymesika in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/1086
* Better support for policies when connecting to policy backends by @howardjohn in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/1091
* Improvements to tracing and logging config by @howardjohn in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/1093
* Fix overlapping keys with local LLM mode by @howardjohn in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/1097
* Gateway API v1.5.0 by @howardjohn in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/1068
* feat(llm): accept /v1/messages InputFormat for chat/completions backends by @apexlnc in https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/909


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/compare/v1.0.0-alpha.2...v1.0.0-alpha.3

commits.message: Fix version number in release (#1072)
Do not use a stale version in cargo (#1075)
release: properly tag images with 'v' prefix (#1074)

Revert "fix: Overlays can delete map elements with 'null'" (#1079)

Reverts agentgateway/agentgateway#1065 because the unittests didn't use
a real k8s API server. A real k8s rejects any CRD that attempts to use a
null map value, and you cannot easily change the CRD because
controller-tools is opinionated about that. I don't want to add new
'remove' APIs for this edge case or kustomize a CRD.

client: do not swallow logs from Body (#1076)

Have had 2 issues of 'error from body', this makes them visible.

Copy tcp routes when inserting listener (#1085)

This addresses the issue with tcp routes disappearing from the existing
listeners on every xDS reconnection, when used in congestion with
https://github.com/kgateway-dev/kgateway/ operator.

I'm not 100% sure why routes are copied here in the first place, since
in case of xDS `insert_route` and `insert_tcp_route` will be called as
well, but maybe there're other use-cases I'm not aware of. Overall this
seems racy, but I'm just going with the flow for now.

Provide Istio mesh config to XDS builder (#1086)

Workloads currently don't have a trust domain set. This results in the
data plane falling back to using `cluster.local` as the trust domain.
Setting Istio to use a different trust domain didn't affect the
Workloads.

The PR is basically replacing the dummy empty mesh config with the real
Istio one (if exists) and by that causing the builder to set the
workloads with the trust domain from the Istio Mesh Config.

This PR replaces https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/1064
following important
[comment](https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/1064#issuecomment-3967999405).

Better support for policies when connecting to policy backends (#1091)

Users can now specify (in standalone) policies to connect to backends
that are made in policies.

Remove deprecated extauthz explicit timeout which is obsolete by this.

Additionally, do not allow 'ai' policies where they don't make sense.

Improvements to tracing and logging config (#1093)

Part of https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/issues/1078

* Deprecate `config.logging` and `config.tracing` which has been
superseded by frontendPolicies
* Remove reading of those, instead convert to frontendPolicies in local
config processing
* Support path in tracing
* Move MCP to the unified tracing config (for frontendPolicies support)
* Add support to add headers on the backend request

Pulls in part of https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/765/
(the MCP part only; that PR has more)

Fix overlapping keys with local LLM mode (#1097)

Fixes https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/issues/1095

we did this for routes but not backends
Gateway API v1.5.0 (#1068)

feat(llm): accept /v1/messages InputFormat for chat/completions backends (#909)

- implement Anthropic /v1/messages <-> OpenAI-style /v1/chat/completions
translation across request, non-stream response, stream, and error paths
- extend role/content mapping in both directions, including tool calls,
tool results, system/developer handling, and multimodal user content
- improve streaming translation sequencing and finish behavior (tool
block lifecycle, done handling, and missing-finish edge cases)
- wire Messages InputFormat behavior consistently for OpenAI-compatible
providers (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Vertex non-Anthropic, Gemini)
- fix Bedrock tool-result mapping for completions/responses translations
to avoid forcing success status when source APIs do not carry explicit
status
- add/expand translation tests for request/response/stream/error parity,
roundtrip semantics, and edge-case regressions; refresh affected
fixtures/snapshots
- bump async-openai to 0.32.4

commits.message:
http2: better pool that avoids single connection limit (#1107)

Today, HTTP2 pool allows only a single connection per key. This is
problematic if we want more than ~100 concurrent streams.

This change attempts to fix this. Still a WIP

Fix auth policy guardrails  (#1485)

Fixes https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/issues/1225

---------

Signed-off-by: npolshakova <nina.polshakova@solo.io>

Normalize SSE headers and completion (#1505)

Fixes https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/issues/1490

e2e: faster tracing tests (#1508)

polling 15s means we took 45s per test. poll faster
gha: do not cancel postsubmit runs (#1509)

route attachments: support arbitrary parents (#1511)

gatewayRouteAttachmentCountCollection did not just build status, it
built the reference index we use to decide which gateways to send config
to; renamed it accordingly

also, do not limit based on the parentRef group kind, allowing plugin
parent resolution to set a specific gateway directly.

mcp: make stateless defer DELETE send (#1503)

Before, we send delete ~immediately. Some servers cut off the SSE stream
if the session is removed. instead, wait until the entire response is
complete.

Harden GHA (#1519)

`zizmor` and `pinact` were used
gha: cache windows and osx builds (#1520)
gha: really do not cancel postsubmit jobs (#1512)

ref(controller): Modernize remote JWKS handling (#1175)

Modernize remote JWKS handling in the controller

This PR refactors remote JWKS handling around fetch-semantic identity,
KRT-derived state, persistence, and lookup.

Relative to `main`, it does four things:
- key shared remote JWKS state by effective fetch semantics instead of
URL-only sharing
- derive shared JWKS requests and persisted keyset entries from KRT
collections and indexes
- consolidate persisted JWKS handling so lookup, startup hydration, and
ConfigMap reconciliation use one JWKS-owned persistence boundary
- simplify the JWT/JWKS surface to explicit `remote` and `inline` JWKS
inputs

The resulting split is:
- `remotehttp` stays the stateless transport-resolution layer
- `jwks` owns shared request aggregation, persisted keyset views,
last-known-good keysets, inline lookup for translation, and ConfigMap
writeback
- persisted JWKS ConfigMap writes remain in an imperative controller for
leader election, retries, and cleanup
- plugins and translation continue to consume `InlineJWKS` and do not
learn fetch or persistence details

A key intentional behavior change is that shared JWKS identity is now
derived from effective fetch semantics rather than raw URL alone. That
means URL, verification mode, SNI, CA bundle hash, and related transport
inputs no longer alias onto one shared request when they describe
materially different fetch behavior.

This also changes the internal persisted artifact identity and canonical
ConfigMap naming. The branch preserves upgrade compatibility for
existing persisted JWKS artifacts by continuing to read legacy ConfigMap
payloads and normalize them onto the current request-key model.

feat: expose source workload identity in CEL context (#1459)

Closes #1460

## Summary
- Resolves source IP → workload identity via the WDS store and exposes
it as `source.workload.name`, `source.workload.namespace`, and
`source.workload.serviceAccount` in CEL expressions
- Enables authorization, transformation, and access logging policies to
use source workload identity without requiring mTLS
- Populates the workload context in both HTTP (gateway) and TCP proxy
paths

## Motivation
When using AgentGateway as a proxy for inter-service traffic, the
gateway receives requests from source pods but has no way to expose the
resolved workload identity in policy expressions. The WDS store already
maps source IPs to workload metadata — this PR wires that lookup into
the CEL context.

The workload store is populated via WDS from the controller, which
watches Kubernetes pods directly. This works for any pod the controller
can see — it does not require the source pod to be enrolled in a service
mesh.

## Example: Authorization based on source service account

Only allow requests from pods running as specific service accounts:

```yaml
apiVersion: agentgateway.dev/v1alpha1
kind: AgentgatewayPolicy
metadata:
  name: restrict-by-source-sa
spec:
  targetRefs:
    - group: gateway.networking.k8s.io
      kind: HTTPRoute
      name: internal-api
  traffic:
    authorization:
      action: Allow
      policy:
        matchExpressions:
          - "source.workload.serviceAccount in ['agent-orchestrator', 'agent-scheduler']"
```

## Example: Source-aware routing with header injection

Inject source identity headers so the receiving service knows which
workload made the request:

```yaml
apiVersion: agentgateway.dev/v1alpha1
kind: AgentgatewayPolicy
metadata:
  name: inject-caller-identity
spec:
  targetRefs:
    - group: gateway.networking.k8s.io
      kind: Gateway
      name: agent-gateway
  traffic:
    transformation:
      request:
        set:
          - name: x-source-workload
            value: "source.workload.name"
          - name: x-source-namespace
            value: "source.workload.namespace"
          - name: x-source-service-account
            value: "source.workload.serviceAccount"
```

## Example: Per-caller access logging

Include source workload identity in access logs for audit:

```yaml
apiVersion: agentgateway.dev/v1alpha1
kind: AgentgatewayPolicy
metadata:
  name: audit-log-with-source
spec:
  targetRefs:
    - group: gateway.networking.k8s.io
      kind: Gateway
      name: agent-gateway
  frontend:
    accessLog:
      attributes:
        add:
          - name: "source.workload"
            expression: "source.workload.name"
          - name: "source.namespace"
            expression: "source.workload.namespace"
          - name: "source.sa"
            expression: "source.workload.serviceAccount"
```

## Test plan
- [x] Existing tests pass with `workload: None` added to all
`SourceContext` constructions
- [x] `cargo check` passes
- [x] Unit test for `source.workload.name`, `source.workload.namespace`,
`source.workload.serviceAccount` CEL evaluation
- [ ] Manual verification: deploy AgentGateway with WDS enabled, send
request from a known pod, verify `source.workload.name` resolves in CEL

Support multi-port InferencePool backends (#1445)

## Summary

This PR adds multi-port `InferencePool` support while keeping a single
logical backend for each pool.

The normal EPP-selected `ip:port` path stays unchanged. When the
endpoint picker actually fails open and does not return an explicit
destination, agentgateway now picks a random available target port from
the selected endpoint instead of always falling back to the canonical
port.

## What changed

- Allow multi-port `InferencePool`s in controller translation without
fanning one pool out into multiple backends.
- Keep `InferencePool` backends represented by a single canonical
backend port.
- On actual inference `fail_open`, choose a random available target port
from the selected endpoint when no explicit destination is returned.
- Add Go and Rust coverage for the controller translation, endpoint
selection, and fail-open fallback behavior.
- Drop the earlier per-port xDS and discovery modeling from this PR.
- Defer the observability and logging additions to a follow-up.

## Why

Previously, agentgateway only handled a single target port for an
`InferencePool`. That meant multi-port pools were either rejected or
effectively collapsed to one port, which did not match the intended
single-pool behavior from `kgateway-dev/kgateway#12238` and
`kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api-inference-extension#1519`.

Fixes: #601

## Follow-up

Ordered retry across an EPP-provided destination endpoint list is
tracked separately in #1444.

## Validation

- `go test ./controller/... -count=1`
- `cargo test -p agentgateway ext_proc --lib --no-fail-fast`
- `cargo test -p agentgateway httpproxy --lib --no-fail-fast`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`

improve stack usage when evaluating CEL (#1552)

Long arithmetic chains made it very easy to reproduce a stack overflow. 

Each commit contains a separate fix:

1. flatten associative chains of operators and walk them iteratively
rather than recursively
2. move the branches of the big match into separate functions set to
never inline, reducing the size of each stack frame

Without any of these fixes, it will crash at twenty  five. 

The stack frame fix alone makes it work at twenty five, but still fails
at fifty.
The iterative optimization fixes it up to hundreds of items in a chain. 
 

```
#   curl 127.0.0.1:3000/one
#   curl 127.0.0.1:3000/five
#   curl 127.0.0.1:3000/ten
#   curl 127.0.0.1:3000/twenty
#   curl 127.0.0.1:3000/fifty
#
# A crashing worker prints `thread 'agentgateway-N' has overflowed its stack`.
# Exact threshold depends on Tokio worker stack size and build profile
# (debug frames are fatter than release).
binds:
- port: 3000
  listeners:
  - protocol: HTTP
    routes:
    - name: one
      matches:
      - path: { pathPrefix: /one }
      policies:
        transformations:
          request:
            set:
              x-boom: '"a"'
        directResponse: { body: "ok\n", status: 200 }

    - name: five
      matches:
      - path: { pathPrefix: /five }
      policies:
        transformations:
          request:
            set:
              x-boom: '"a"+"b"+"c"+"d"+"e"'
        directResponse: { body: "ok\n", status: 200 }

    - name: ten
      matches:
      - path: { pathPrefix: /ten }

Add tunnel policy support jwks (#1543)

Added support for HTTP Proxy Support for JWKS Fetching via the tunnel
policy:
```
apiVersion: agentgateway.dev/v1alpha1
kind: AgentgatewayBackend
metadata:
  name: dummy-idp-proxied
  namespace: agentgateway-base
spec:
  static:
    host: dummy-idp.default.svc.cluster.local
    port: 8443
  policies:
    tls:
      insecureSkipVerify: All
    tunnel: # this now gets used by the fetcher 
      backendRef:
        group: agentgateway.dev
        kind: AgentgatewayBackend
        name: squid-proxy
        port: 3128

a proxy.
