#### 1.5.71 August 26th, 2026 #### Akka.NET v1.5.71 is a maintenance release that fixes a Cluster Sharding private-replicator recovery bug, hardens MultiNodeTestRunner conductor reliability, flushes graceful `Disassociate` PDUs before transport force-close on shutdown, and resolves a handful of TestKit, ClusterClientDiscovery, and DotNetty fixes. **Akka.Cluster.Sharding** * [Fix Cluster Sharding private replicator recovery](https://github.com/akkadotnet/akka.net/pull/8480): Fixes a bug where a Cluster Sharding private replicator could fail to recover its state, leaving shard state inconsistent after a coordinated shutdown / recovery cycle. Adds a `ClusterShardingReplicatorResiliencySpec` covering the recovery path. **Akka.Remote** * [Backport #8421 to v1.5: flush graceful `Disassociate` PDUs before transport force-close on shutdown](https://github.com/akkadotnet/akka.net/pull/8487): Ensures in-flight graceful `Disassociate` control messages are flushed to the wire before the transport force-closes the connection on shutdown, preventing an abrupt teardown from silently dropping them. * [Akka.Remote: stop, don't restart, failed throttler children](https://github.com/akkadotnet/akka.net/pull/8437) - Fixes [#8433](https://github.com/akkadotnet/akka.net/issues/8433) and [#8434](https://github.com/akkadotnet/akka.net/issues/8434): A failing outbound-throttler child is now stopped rather than restarted, avoiding an unbounded restart loop that could stall remote message throughput. * [Clarify DotNetty hostname validation direction](https://github.com/akkadotnet/akka.net/pull/8464): Clarifies the direction of the DotNetty hostname validation check so it validates the expected peer identity instead of the local endpoint. **Akka.Remote.TestKit (MultiNodeTestRunner)** * [Backport MNTR conductor reliability to v1.5](https://github.com/akkadotnet/akka.net/pull/8488) - Backports [#8431](https://github.com/akkadotnet/akka.net/issues/8431) and [#8485](https://github.com/akkadotnet/akka.net/issues/8485): Hardens the MNTR `BarrierCoordinator`, `Conductor`, `Controller`, `Player`, and `RemoteConnection` against conductor-side races and disconnect handling, reducing multi-node spec flakiness. **Akka.TestKit** * [Add AutoDilate metadata to TestKit timeouts](https://github.com/akkadotnet/akka.net/pull/8441): Adds AutoDilate dilation metadata to TestKit timeout expectations so dilated deadlines are correctly tracked and reported. * [Fix torn read in `PromiseActorRef.GetPath` that made `Path` return null](https://github.com/akkadotnet/akka.net/pull/8436): Fixes a torn read in `PromiseActorRef.GetPath` that could return `null` under concurrent access. * [Fix double-dilated timeout in `ExpectMsgAsync(Func, ...)`](https://github.com/akkadotnet/akka.net/pull/8430): Fixes a bug where the overload of `ExpectMsgAsync` that takes a predicate could apply its timeout dilation twice, causing spurious timeout failures. **Akka.Cluster.Tools** * [Fix ClusterClientDiscovery: preserve contact-point subscriptions across rediscovery](https://github.com/akkadotnet/akka.net/pull/8426): Ensures `ClusterClientDiscovery` keeps its contact-point subscriptions alive across rediscovery cycles instead of dropping them. **Tests** * [Make `ClusterShardingQueriesSpec` stats/region-state commits.message:
fix: make ClusterShardingQueriesSpec stats/region-state queries converge-then-assert (async) (#8311)

The stats (GetClusterShardingStats) and region-state (GetShardRegionState)
assertions in ClusterShardingQueriesSpec were one-shot reads with no retry,
racing sharding's internal 3s shard-region-query-timeout on the Second/Third
regions. Under CI load a Shard actor can momentarily miss that timeout and be
reported in Failed instead of Stats, transiently undercounting the Stats sum
(4 -> 3) and failing the assertion. The product is correct by design (partial
results are expected); the defect was purely the one-shot assertion.

Wrap the stats query + both sum assertions, and each GetShardRegionState block,
in AwaitAssertAsync (converge-then-assert) with a fresh TestProbe per attempt so
a late reply can't pollute the next expect. Mirrors ClusterShardingGetStatsSpec.
Also converts the spec to async TestKit (RunOnAsync/AwaitAssertAsync/
ExpectMsgAsync/EnterBarrierAsync). Busy's 0ms shard-region-query-timeout (the
feature under test) is intentionally kept.

Test-only; multi-node spec so compile-verified only (CI validates behavior).

(cherry picked from commit d5fe72f2e786038e868aa42174e3941d895f63ab)
Clarify DotNetty hostname validation direction (#8464)

Fix ClusterClientDiscovery: preserve contact-point subscriptions across rediscovery (#8426)

* Fix ClusterClientDiscovery: preserve contact-point subscriptions across rediscovery

ClusterClientDiscovery supervises the real ClusterClient as a child and recreates that child from
scratch on every rediscovery (when the current child exhausts its reconnect-timeout and stops). The
contact-point subscriber list lives on the child, so a SubscribeContactPoints subscriber silently
stopped receiving ContactPoints/ContactPointAdded/ContactPointRemoved once the client rediscovered —
the fresh child had no record of it.

Track contact-point subscribers at the supervisor level and re-subscribe them onto each newly-created
child (on the subscriber's behalf, so the child registers them and replies with the current snapshot).
DeathWatch each subscriber so a terminated subscriber is dropped from tracking (auto-unsubscribe).
Subscribe/Unsubscribe are still forwarded to the current child, so live behavior is unchanged; only the
across-rediscovery gap is closed.

* ClusterClientDiscoverySpec: verify contact points via subscription events

Replace the three GetContactPoints polling blocks (each with an orphaned, hand-tightened 1s inner
ExpectMsg that spuriously timed out on loaded CI agents) with a single event-driven helper: subscribe
via SubscribeContactPoints and wait on the client's own ContactPoints/ContactPointAdded/ContactPointRemoved
stream until the contact points settle to exactly the expected node. No per-attempt reply timeout to race.

This also covers the ClusterClientDiscovery subscription-survival fix: the second and third phases exercise
rediscovery after a graceful down and a hard shutdown, so the subscription must survive the child being
recreated for the helper to observe the new node. Verified locally, 4/4 across repeated runs.

Fix double-dilated timeout in ExpectMsgAsync<T>(Func<T, IActorRef, bool>, ...) (#8430)

This overload resolved its bound as RemainingOrDilated(RemainingOrDilated(timeout)), applying
akka.test.timefactor twice. Every sibling overload applies it once.

With timefactor = 3 an explicit 5s wait became 45s. The null case is worse: the inner call resolves
to RemainingOrDefault - the time actually left in the enclosing Within - and the outer call then
dilates that, producing a bound larger than the remaining budget it was derived from.

Apply RemainingOrDilated once, matching every other overload. No in-repo caller uses this overload,
so nothing here was relying on the inflated bound; Akka.TestKit.Tests (320) and
Akka.TestKit.Xunit2.Tests (4) pass.

Fix torn read in PromiseActorRef.GetPath that made Path return null (#8436)

* Fix torn read in PromiseActorRef.GetPath that made Path return null

`PromiseActorRef.GetPath()` matched on its `State` field and then re-read
that same field to build the return value:

    switch (State)                      // read #1 - matches ActorPath
    {
        ...
        case ActorPath _:
            return State as ActorPath;  // read #2 - re-reads the field

`State` is an `AtomicReference<object>` whose getter is a `Volatile.Read`, so
those are two genuinely separate loads of a field any thread can mutate. A
concurrent `Stop()` flipping the state from `ActorPath` to `StoppedWithPath`
between the two reads makes the `as` cast fail, and `Path` returns **null** -
violating the method's own contract ("Must always return the same ActorPath").
The sibling `case StoppedWithPath stoppedWithPath:` was already correct because
it binds the pattern variable instead of re-reading.

A null path then dereferences twice, unguarded, in `ActorRefBase.GetHashCode()`
and blows up. Observed in CI:

    System.NullReferenceException
       at Akka.Actor.ActorRefBase.GetHashCode()
       at System.Collections.Generic.HashSet`1.Remove(T item)
       at Akka.Actor.FullActorState.RemoveWatchedBy(IActorRef)
       at Akka.Actor.ActorCell.RemWatcher(...)
       at Akka.Actor.ActorCell.SysMsgInvokeAll(...)

The interleaving comes from `AskModeWithDeathCompletion` in
ThrottleTransportAdapter, which does Watch -> Tell -> SendSystemMessage(Unwatch)
while the promise completes and stops on another thread. Throwing out of
`SysMsgInvokeAll` kills an arbitrary actor mid-Unwatch; in the observed case it
restarted a transport throttler into a permanently broken state.

Fix, in two parts:

* `GetPath()` now snapshots `State` into a local at the top of each loop
  iteration and switches on the local, binding the pattern variable
  (`case ActorPath path: return path;`). The snapshot is per-iteration, not
  hoisted out of the loop, so the `Stopped`/`Registering`/`null` cases still
  re-read after the state transition they wait on. All other case semantics
  are unchanged.

* `ActorRefBase.ToString/GetHashCode/Equals/CompareTo` cache `Path` (and the
  other ref's `Path`) into locals instead of dereferencing the virtual property
  two to four times per call. No null guard is added: after the `GetPath()`
  fix, every return path is non-null - a failing `Provider.TempPath()` throws
  rather than returning null - so null is impossible at the source and
  swallowing it here would only hide the next such bug. The local cache is
  still correct practice: it removes the torn-read window for any `IActorRef`
  whose `Path` is computed from mutable state, and drops redundant virtual
  calls (`GetPath()` is a CAS loop, not a field read).

Regression test: `PromiseActorRefSpec` pins one `PromiseActorRef` between a
reader thread spinning on `GetHashCode`/`Path` and a stopper thread that waits
until the reader is demonstrably inside that spin before calling `Stop()`, so
the state flip always lands with a read in flight. Against the unfixed code it
reproduced 5/5 runs, 100-240 null paths and 90-290 NREs per 2,000 rounds, with
the failure stack matching the CI report. It passes 8/8 runs after the fix and
takes ~250ms.

Akka.Tests: 1306 passed, 0 failed, 23 skipped.
Akka.Remote.Tests: 645 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped.
Akka.API.Tests: 18 passed - no public API surface change.

* Narrow to the actual fix: drop the ActorRef caching and the race-repro spec

Two things did not earn their place in this change.

The ActorRef.cs Path caching was presented as protection against a torn read, but it protects against
nothing: PromiseActorRef.Stop() transitions ActorPath -> StoppedWithPath(p) carrying the SAME path
instance (Futures.cs:608), so two consecutive Path reads cannot disagree. Reverting Futures.cs while
keeping the caching also still reproduced the NRE, proving the caching was never the fix. What
remained was a micro-optimization with a misleading safety comment, widening a change that should be
trivially reviewable and backportable.

PromiseActorRefSpec reproduced the race by spinning thousands of rounds hoping to hit an
interleaving. It did its job proving the fix during development, but shipping a probabilistic,
CPU-heavy timing test into the permanent suite adds exactly the kind of flake this suite is being
cleaned of.

What is left is the one defect: GetPath() matched on State and then re-read the field, so a
concurrent Stop() made 'State as ActorPath' return null.

Akka.Remote: stop, don't restart, failed throttler children (#8433, #8434) (#8437)

ThrottlerManager never managed the lifecycle of its ThrottledAssociation
children, which produced two related failures.

1. No SupervisorStrategy was declared, so the default Restart applied. A
   restarted inbound ThrottledAssociation re-enters WaitExposedHandle, and the
   Handle message that leaves that state is only ever sent once - at creation.
   The association then sat there for the life of the process, logging
   "unhandled event InboundPayload" and dropping every inbound packet, with no
   disassociation and no quarantine to tell remoting anything was wrong.
   ThrottlerManager now stops failed children, matching AkkaProtocolManager.

2. _handleTable entries were only removed on the ForceDisassociate paths, so a
   throttler that died any other way left a stale entry behind. Later
   SetThrottle/PassThrough walks messaged dead refs - the throttle mode
   dead-lettered and the change silently did not apply. Children are now
   watched at their single creation site and purged from the table on
   Terminated.

Belt and braces: an InboundPayload arriving in WaitExposedHandle is impossible
during a healthy startup - the read handler is not registered until we leave
that state - so it now disassociates and stops instead of dropping packets
quietly.

Scope: the throttle adapter is only in the transport pipeline when
applied-adapters includes trttl/gremlin, i.e. multi-node test runs rather than
production deployments.
Add AutoDilate metadata to TestKit timeouts (#8441)
fix: add AutoDilate API approval updates for #8441 backport

Backport MNTR conductor reliability to v1.5 (#8431 + #8485) (#8488)

Barrier failures now actually fail the barrier: three Player.cs sites replied with the FSM-inherited Failure type, so the barrier ask completed successfully and the failure was silently swallowed - the asking node walked on unsynchronized and the breakage surfaced elsewhere as an unrelated-looking flake. All three now reply Status.Failure, plus the discarded-ask cleanup and the runner mislabeling fix.

Conductor keeps re-registered nodes: a restarting node's stale ClientDisconnected was matched by role name and evicted the fresh registration, then the barrier coordinator dropped the evicted node's arrivals with no reply, hanging it for the full ask timeout. Disconnects are now matched against the registered FSM identity, unregistered arrivals get an explicit BarrierResult(false), and ReleaseAll detaches the shared event-loop groups.

Validated locally with revert-proven tests and three consecutive green ReDeployment MNTR runs. With barrier failures now honest, latent v1.5 spec failures may surface attributed to the node that actually broke - the intended effect. Dev's node-hang kill backstop was deliberately not taken: it needs Process.Kill(entireProcessTree:), unavailable on netstandard2.0; needs a netstandard-safe follow-up.

Backport #8421 to v1.5: flush graceful Disassociate PDUs before transport force-close on shutdown (#8487)

Clean cherry-pick of #8421 onto v1.5, whose ActorTransportAdapter.Shutdown() was byte-identical to the pre-fix dev version. Sequences the adapter teardown - manager and its Disassociate-writing children first, wrapped transport after - so the graceful Disassociate PDU reaches the wire instead of being force-closed away, sparing peers the up-to-120s zombie-association window on every graceful shutdown. Validated by two fully-green dev gate runs and the transport suites on v1.5's own toolchain (14/14 adapter specs, 105/105 transport filter); v1.5 CI failures across three runs were five distinct pre-existing flakes in unrelated assemblies, all documented on the PR.

Fix Cluster Sharding private replicator recovery (#8480)

* Fix Cluster Sharding private replicator recovery

Watch role-scoped sharding DData replicators and recreate them at their stable actor paths when they terminate. Use actor selections so existing coordinators and remember-entities stores continue communicating with the replacement incarnation.

Add regression coverage for DData remember entities and the persistence compatibility configuration.

* Address sharding replicator recovery review

Keep IActorRef throughout the sharding DData consumers and publish a local replacement message when the guardian recreates a terminated replicator. Existing coordinators and remember-entities stores swap to the new ref and retry their active operation, while providers use the replacement for newly-created stores.

Use WatchWith role-aware termination messages, preserve the peer-visible actor path, suppress shutdown recreation, and simplify the regression test fixtures.

* Simplify remember entities provider tracking

* Simplify sharding replicator recovery

* Cover sharding replicator coordinated shutdown

Release Akka.NET v1.5.71 (#8493)

* Bump version to 1.5.71 and update release notes

* Correct XML escaping in release notes for v1.5.71

# Overview
<!-- A sentence or two capturing the release and any noteworthy details that anyone taking the release should be aware of -->
This release includes Algod API updates to make it easier for developers to access applications and assets along with several connection management improvements for the P2P network.

# What's New
* Paginated Applications endpoint
* Paginated Assets and Applications endpoints incorporate deltas in their results (providing a much more realtime view) and are no longer behind the experimental flag
* Users of /v2/accounts now have the ability to exclude app and assets parameters when querying

# Changelog
## Enhancements
* API: Incorporate deltas in presenting paginated view of assets or applications ([#6559](https://github.com/algorand/go-algorand/pull/6559))
* API: add OnlineCirculation to GetSupply ([#6322](https://github.com/algorand/go-algorand/pull/6322))
* API: New pagination endpoint for applications ([#6552](https://github.com/algorand/go-algorand/pull/6552))
* API: Enhance /v2/accounts to conditionally exclude app and asset parameters ([#6547](https://github.com/algorand/go-algorand/pull/6547))
* Agreement: implement TODO in broadcast/relay actions ([#6551](https://github.com/algorand/go-algorand/pull/6551))
* Build: add golangci-lint format into make fmt ([#6549](https://github.com/algorand/go-algorand/pull/6549))
* Eval: Prefetch better ([#6555](https://github.com/algorand/go-algorand/pull/6555))
* Network: adjust pubsub params ([#6569](https://github.com/algorand/go-algorand/pull/6569))
* Network: don't listen if IncomingConnectionsLimit == 0 ([#6568](https://github.com/algorand/go-algorand/pull/6568))
* Network: silently fall back if uncompressed vote received for stateless decoder ([#6495](https://github.com/algorand/go-algorand/pull/6495))
* Network: use specific error assertions in tests ([#6544](https://github.com/algorand/go-algorand/pull/6544))
* Node: collect goroutines stacks before SIGKILL ([#6557](https://github.com/algorand/go-algorand/pull/6557))
## Bugfixes
* Kmd: fix macOS HID failures caused by Go async preemption signals ([#6565](https://github.com/algorand/go-algorand/pull/6565))
* Ledger: fix lookupAssetResources/lookupApplicationResources delta-merge bugs ([#6577](https://github.com/algorand/go-algorand/pull/6577))
* Network: fix streamManager deadlock that causes goroutine leak on P2P hybrid relays ([#6576](https://github.com/algorand/go-algorand/pull/6576))
* Network: handle stream creation on existing conns ([#6572](https://github.com/algorand/go-algorand/pull/6572))
* P2p: ignore pubsub PX peers for all node modes ([#6554](https://github.com/algorand/go-algorand/pull/6554))

* Tools: fix DevNet genesis hash in algokey ([#6556](https://github.com/algorand/go-algorand/pull/6556))
## Protocol Upgrade
This release does not contain a protocol upgrade.

feat: add Update All to the Updates page

Adds an Update All capsule to the top bar on the Updates page that

fix: drop analytics signals when TelemetryDeck has no app ID

Builds without Configs/Secrets.xcconfig never initialize the SDK, whose
shared-instance getter asserts in Debug builds — the first analytics
signal (any sidebar click) crashed the app with SIGTRAP. Guard send()
so secret-less builds stay silent, matching the documented intent.

cards show a "Queued…" capsule instead of a tappable Update button —
which both signals queue membership and removes the race where tapping
Update on a queued cask spawned a second concurrent brew process.

perf: precompute per-cask search keys

Each search projection lowercased displayName, token, and desc for every
cask in the pass. A memoized token→searchKey dictionary now lowercases
the catalog once per revision; the filter does a single contains per

Merge pull request #132 from alielsokary/docs/code-of-conduct

perf: precompute localized name ranks for sorting

Name sorts ran localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare per comparison — ~44k
ICU collation walks per projection over the full catalog (the
_stringCompare hang). One locale-aware sort per catalog revision now
memoizes token→rank; projections order name sorts by Int rank with the
ICU comparator kept as fallback for casks outside the snapshot.
Ordering is unchanged, including diacritics. Ranks build lazily on the
first name-ordered sort.
ci: author back-merge prs with a pat so checks run without approval

perf: cap rendered catalog rows with scroll-triggered reveal

Browse list mode and Top Charts handed all ~3.7k casks to the lazy
containers, so every projection change forced SwiftUI to diff and lay
out the full array. The grid and list now render displayedCasks —
filteredCasks capped at 200 — with an invisible sentinel as the last
lazy item revealing the next 200 when scrolled to. filteredCasks stays
uncapped for the top-bar count and hero card. The cap resets on
sidebar, sort, and applied-search changes.

Merge branch 'develop' into perf/search-debounce

fix: scope reveal sentinel to the capped grid and gate browse layout on applied search

Review findings: caskGrid is shared with the 8-item browse shelves, so
their sentinels fired revealMore() against the global reveal state while
scrolling the landing page, inflating revealedCount and defeating the
render cap. The sentinel is now opt-in via showsReveal, enabled only at
the capped flat-grid call site. showsBrowseSections now reads the
debounced appliedSearchText so the layout swap and the filtered results
land in the same frame instead of flashing an unfiltered grid for the
debounce window.

fix: keep brew error lines through progress floods and stop duplicate 5xx reports

- BrewOutputCollector strips progress frames before its 2000-char tail
  cap, so a long extract can no longer evict the error line that failure
  classification depends on (the reason CASKHUB-C sits uncategorized)
- drop HomebrewOutputDiagnostics' important-lines branch: the collector
  caps output at 2000 chars, so the 8KB path was unreachable; make() is
  now strip + trim + tail safety cap
- disable Sentry's automatic failed-request capture: it duplicated our
  own HTTPError reporting and filed formulae.brew.sh 5xx outages as app
  errors with synthetic stacks (CASKHUB-6)
- retry catalog/analytics fetches once after 2s on 5xx so brief
  formulae.brew.sh outages don't surface at all

fix: refresh local state when brew rejects an action as not installed

Upgrading a cask brew no longer has a Caskroom record for (removed
externally, e.g. via terminal uninstall) failed with 'is not installed'
while the stale Update button stayed visible, inviting retries. Terminal
mutation failures whose failure class is not-installed now trigger a
snapshot refresh so the UI reconciles to the real install state.
revert: keep Sentry automatic failed-request capture enabled

fix: align installed detection with brew's timestamped caskfile check

Brew only counts a cask as installed when a caskfile exists under
.metadata/<version>/<timestamp>/Casks/ (Cask#installed?). Our scanner
accepted any version directory with an INSTALL_RECEIPT.json, so
leftovers from interrupted uninstalls read as installed with updates
available and every upgrade attempt earned 'is not installed'. Entries
without the timestamped caskfile are now zombies, which the resolver
already excludes from update offers.

test: wire projection input call sites explicitly and add reveal boundary test

AGENTS.md compliance pass: CatalogFilteredProjectionInput's searchKeys
and nameRanks lose their defaults — every call site wires them
explicitly — and caskGrid's showsReveal is now explicit at both call
sites. New production-boundary test hosts the real ContentView on the
browse landing page in a tall window and asserts the shelves cannot
consume the reveal budget; verified red against the pre-fix sentinel
wiring.
feat: enhance settings experience

Merge pull request #140 from alielsokary/feature/settings-enhancements

feat: Enhance settings experience
Merge branch 'develop' into fix/sentry-reporting-signal

fix: match brew's newest-timestamp caskfile check exactly

Brew's Caskroom.cask_installed_caskfile consults only the single newest
timestamp directory across all versions and requires Casks/<token>.rb or
.json by token name there. The scanner previously accepted any caskfile
in any timestamp, so a stale newer timestamp without the matching
caskfile still read as installed. Regression test covers a valid older
caskfile shadowed by an invalid newer timestamp.

fix: share ranks between collation-equal names and slim ContentView

Unique ranks broke ties the stable sort used to preserve, silently
reversing collation-equal names in descending sorts. Names comparing
orderedSame now share a rank, so ties stay ties in both directions —
ordering is genuinely identical to the ICU comparator again. Regression
test covers the Foo/foo descending case. RevealSentinel and
ResetScrollOnChange move to Views/Shared/CatalogScrollSupport.swift,
returning ContentView under the file-length limit.

perf: isolate per-cask operation observation and cut hot-path allocations

Audit findings (SwiftUI + Swift performance pass):

- CaskOperationStore kept every token's state in one @Observable
  dictionary, so each brew progress tick invalidated every visible row
  and card (each reads state(for:) several times per body). States now
  live in per-token CaskOperationBox instances — a tick touches only its
  own row, matching the isolation ObservedStatusBarView already used.
- App.init decoded ~920KB of bundled JSON (categories + added dates) on
  the MainActor before the first frame; both now decode @concurrent
  after launch, guarded so they never overwrite fresher remote data.
- CaskFlowReleases.fetch inherited MainActor, putting the ~1MB remote
  asset decodes on the main thread every foreground refresh — now
  @concurrent.
- formattedDownloads built a Locale + FormatStyle per visible cell per
  pass; the style is now a static let.
- categoryPresentation allocated an uncached presentation per cell per
  pass; now memoized per catalog/category revision like the other
  projections.
- CatalogProjector allocated a Set per cask per pass for category
  fan-out; replaced with an allocation-free unique-category walk.
- BrewOutputCollector recompiled the ANSI regex on every output chunk;
  compiled once.

fix: never capture task cancellation errors

Cancellation during the 5xx retry sleep surfaces as CancellationError,
which the URLError code filter never matched — a cancelled catalog fetch
would have reported as a fresh error class. Cancellation of any shape is
now dropped in capture. Also compacts the collector flood test to keep
the integration file under the length limit.
Merge branch 'develop' into fix/not-installed-resync

perf: parse brew output off the main thread

A Time Profiler trace of scrolling during an active download showed the
chunk pipeline — buffer tail copies, ANSI stripping, progress-bar regex
parsing, byte formatting — eating ~10% of main-thread samples in bursty
spikes, since every pty chunk ran the full parse on the MainActor.

BrewOutputAggregator now buffers, throttles, and parses on a serial
utility queue (including the cached-download file stat); the MainActor
receives only the finished update at ~10/s. Throttle semantics match
the old coordinator: marker lines parse immediately and never delay the
byte line after them. Tests sequence deliveries deterministically via
awaitPendingOutput().

commits.message:
fix: SQLite connection leak causing unbounded memory growth

SaveStats returned tx.Create().Error directly without assigning to the
local err variable, so the deferred closure always saw err==nil and
called Commit() on a failed transaction. This left the underlying
go-sqlite3 connection unreturned to the pool. With StatsJob firing
every 10s, leaked connections accumulated ~150 KB each, reaching
400+ MB after ~33 hours.

Fixes:

* fix(clash): inject default Proxy/Auto only when a custom group references them

Refines the proxy-group injection logic so default Proxy/Auto groups
are only injected when needed, rather than skipping injection entirely
when custom groups exist (#1110) or always injecting unconditionally
(#1066).

Two-part condition:
1. No group named Proxy already exists (user-defined Proxy is respected)
2. At least one existing group references Proxy in its proxies list

When injection is needed, defaults are prepended before custom groups.
Also avoids injecting a duplicate Auto group when the user already
defines one.

Added hasGroupNamed helper and comprehensive tests (15 cases) covering
nil/empty/custom/no-ref/duplicate-Auto scenarios.

Sing-Box v1.14.0-rc.2: compile-level upgrade

Re-sync core/protocol/* from upstream (they were verbatim copies), re-fork
core/box.go onto the new upstream box.go, and adapt to changed APIs:

- adapter.ConnectionTracker gained RoutedFlow; add no-op impls to both trackers
- log.ObservableFactory gained AttachPlatformWriter; add no-op impl
- box.Context now takes a CertificateProviderRegistry; wire one up with
  the origin_ca provider
- box.go now depends on debug*.go; copy them from upstream
- hysteria inbound moved QUIC option building into quic.go; copy it

Deps: sing v0.9.0-beta.4, sing-quic v0.7.0-beta.4, sing-tun v0.9.0-beta.2.

Runtime behaviour is not yet validated and config migration for options
deprecated in 1.14 is not done, so this is not ready for main.

core: add config compatibility test for the 1.14 upgrade

Starts a real box for each config in testdata/configs and logs the
deprecation notes it triggers. Covers the eight re-copied protocol inbounds
plus the option shapes s-ui's UI can emit that 1.14 deprecates.

Confirms no config s-ui produces fails to start under 1.14; the deprecated
ones warn and keep working.

core: register ACME and Tailscale certificate providers

The 1.14 upgrade wired up a certificate provider registry with only
origin_ca, so `tls.certificate_provider: {"type": "acme"}` failed to parse
with "unknown certificate provider type". Register ACME and Tailscale too,
behind the same build tags upstream uses, with stubs that report a helpful
error when the tag is absent.

This is what `tls.acme` migrates to in 1.14: the same fields move under
certificate_provider with `type: "acme"`, which parses clean with no
deprecation warning.

database: migrate options deprecated in sing-box 1.14

One-shot migration over the stored config and TLS rows, guarded by a setting
so it runs once:

- dns.independent_cache is dropped (1.14 reads it only to warn; the value is
  never passed to the DNS client)
- experimental.cache_file.store_rdrc becomes store_dns
- route.rule_set[].download_detour becomes the http_client 1.14 builds for it
- inline tls.acme becomes tls.certificate_provider with type "acme"

Legacy DNS address filters and the `strategy` DNS rule action are NOT migrated
automatically. Converting them means inserting evaluate rules and reordering,
which changes how names resolve, so they are logged with the upstream
migration link for the operator to handle.

Tests cover each rewrite, that unrelated options survive, that a config with
nothing to migrate is left byte-identical, and that the migrated shapes build
a box with no deprecation warning.

frontend: bump to the 1.14 option shapes

Points the submodule at s-ui-frontend singbox-1.14, which stops emitting
tls.acme, rule-set download_detour and dns.independent_cache.

core: register the protocols added in sing-box 1.14

Adds every new 1.14 type to the registries, following upstream's include
package: the build-tagged ones get the same stub pair s-ui already uses for
naive and tailscale, so a build without the tag reports which tag is missing
instead of failing to parse.

- inbound: snell, cloudflared
- outbound: snell, bridge
- endpoint: openconnect, openvpn (client and server)
- dns transport: mdns, resolved, openconnect, openvpn
- service: api, oom-killer, usbip (server and client)

with_cloudflared, with_openconnect, with_openvpn and with_usbip are added to
build.sh, the Dockerfile and both release workflows. Verified the linux
amd64/arm64 and windows amd64 cross-builds CI ships.

Registry tests now assert the full expected type set rather than just
certificate providers, and the box tests write their cache file to a temp
directory instead of leaving core/cache.db behind.

core: cover the new 1.14 protocols with config tests

Starts snell v5 and v6 inbounds, a snell outbound and an oom-killer service;
bridge gets construct-only coverage since creating its tun needs privileges.

Also bumps the frontend submodule to the UI for these protocols.

- hash(B256) and hash_canonical(B256) for block hashes

commits.message:
fix(transport): eagerly format itertools to prevent double-format panic (#3668)

`.format()` from itertools returns a `Format` struct that panics if
displayed more than once. The `#[instrument]` macro may format span
fields multiple times, causing a panic at runtime.

Fixes #3666

398409995.body:
## Highlights

### Throttled auto-updates of `var`s, `lazy val`s, and `Future`s

When using Scala 2, the output of a cell defining a top-level `var` is updated when the `var` changes later on,
the output of a `lazy val` is updated when it's computed, and the output of a `Future` is updated when it completes.
When a `var` changed many times in a short time, like in a loop, each change sent an update to the front-end, which
could flood it. Updates are now coalesced: only the latest value is sent, at most every 100 ms or so, and pending
values are flushed when the cell that changes them completes.

These automatic updates can now be turned off with two new kernel options,
`--auto-update-vars=false` and `--auto-update-lazy-vals=false`.
See [Auto-updated variables](https://almond.sh/docs/api-jupyter#auto-updated-variables) in the docs.

by @alexarchambault in https://github.com/almond-sh/almond/pull/1757

### Fix kernel crashes when inspecting code while a cell runs (Scala 2)

Hovering over code (`inspect_request`) while another cell was running could kill the whole kernel, and the
`SparkContext` along with it in Spark notebooks. Inspections read compiler symbol information from the wrong
thread, which triggered an `AssertionError` in scalac, and since that error isn't caught, it brought the JVM down.
With 0.14.5, this happened after about two dozen inspections of a cell with an import, while another cell was running.
Inspections now do all their compiler work on the presentation compiler thread. A failed docstring lookup now costs
only that inspection and not the kernel, and a `NullPointerException` hit while a background compilation was in
progress has been fixed too.

by @alexarchambault in https://github.com/almond-sh/almond/pull/1712

### Load and reload Ammonite scripts

Notebooks can now load Ammonite scripts, with the same syntax as in Ammonite:
```scala
import $file.path.to.script // compiles and runs path/to/script.sc
script.foo()
```
Paths are relative to the working directory of the kernel, which is usually the directory of the notebook,
and `^` stands for the parent directory. Scripts can also be loaded with a directive, which accepts any path:
```scala
//> using script path/to/script.sc
//> using scripts path/to/script.sc, /absolute/path/to/other.sc
```
A script is compiled and run only once per session, unless its content changed since it was last loaded.
In that case, loading it again re-compiles and re-runs it, and cells run after that see its new definitions,
so you can edit a script next to your notebook and pick up the changes without restarting the kernel.

by @alexarchambault in https://github.com/almond-sh/almond/pull/1762

### `--last-value-only` option

A new kernel option, `--last-value-only`, makes the kernel display only the last value defined or computed in each cell,
rather than one line per `val` (#256). For example, this cell only displays `second: Int = 2`:
```scala
val first = 1
val second = first + 1
```
All statements still run, and both values can still be used in later cells. Imports and class, method,
and type definitions aren't echoed, and explicit output (`println`, `display(…)`) is still shown.
Enable it when installing the kernel:
```bash
cs launch --use-bootstrap almond:0.15.0 --scala 2.13.18 -- --install --last-value-only
```

by @alexarchambault in https://github.com/almond-sh/almond/pull/1764

### Completions while a cell is running

Completion requests are now answered while a cell executes, instead of waiting in line until it finishes.
They run asynchronously, with access to the compiler synchronized with the running cell, and the kernel
still reports itself as busy while the cell runs.

by @alexarchambault in https://github.com/almond-sh/almond/pull/1755

### Better support for VS Code

- `kernel_info_request` messages sent on the control channel (protocol 5.5, which the VS Code Jupyter extension uses)
  are now answered. They were ignored before. They're answered even while a cell is running.
- Inspection replies now include a `text/plain` alternative next to the HTML one. The VS Code Jupyter PowerToys
  Contextual Help panel needs it, and showed "No response from kernel" without it.

by @alexarchambault in https://github.com/almond-sh/almond/pull/1713

## Breaking changes / packaging

### Supported Scala versions

For Scala 3, only the latest version and the LTS are now supported. For Scala 2, on the other hand,
many more versions are supported than in 0.14.x. Almond 0.15.0 supports:
- Scala **3.9.0** and **3.3.8** (LTS)
- Scala **2.13.3** to **2.13.18**
- Scala **2.12.8** to **2.12.21**

Scala 3.4.x, 3.5.x, 3.6.x, 3.7.x, 3.8.x, and older 3.3.x versions aren't supported anymore. For those versions,
use earlier Almond versions (0.14.2 or 0.14.5 depending on the version).

Newly supported Scala 2 versions older than 2.12.18 and 2.13.11 need a JDK 17 or older to run.

by @alexarchambault in https://github.com/almond-sh/almond/pull/1700, https://github.com/almond-sh/almond/pull/1754, https://github.com/almond-sh/almond/pull/1689, https://github.com/almond-sh/almond/pull/1722

### Almond now uses its own Ammonite fork

Almond now depends on an Ammonite fork published under the `sh.almond.ammonite` organization, instead of
`com.lihaoyi`. If your library depends on the Ammonite API to interact with the kernel (`ammonite.interp.api.InterpApi`,
`ammonite.repl.api.ReplAPI`), update its coordinates. For example with sbt:
```scala
("sh.almond.ammonite" % "ammonite-interp" % "…" % Provided).cross(CrossVersion.full)
("sh.almond.ammonite" % "ammonite-repl" % "…" % Provided).cross(CrossVersion.full)
```

by @alexarchambault in https://github.com/almond-sh/almond/pull/1715

### Fewer published modules

Almond publishes far fewer modules. This matters if you depend on Almond modules directly, for example to write
libraries that interact with the kernel:
- `scala-kernel-api`, `scala-interpreter`, and `scala-kernel` are now published once per binary Scala version
  (`_2.12`, `_2.13`, `_3`) rather than once per full Scala version (`_2.13.18`, …). Use `%%` / `::` rather than
  `CrossVersion.full` / `:::` to depend on them.
- `interpreter-api` and `jupyter-api` were merged into a new `api` module
- `logger`, `logger-scala2-macros`, `channels`, `protocol`, and `interpreter` were folded into `kernel`
- `coursier-logger` and `shared-directives` were folded into `scala-interpreter` (and the launcher)
- `toree-hooks` was folded into `scala-kernel-api`
- `almond-rx` and `shared-test` aren't published anymore

by @alexarchambault in https://github.com/almond-sh/almond/pull/1721, https://github.com/almond-sh/almond/pull/1723, https://github.com/almond-sh/almond/pull/1768

### No more dependency on the main coursier module

Almond now uses only the lower-level coursier modules, and no longer depends on `io.get-coursier::coursier`.
The main coursier module is due to drop Scala 2.12 support, so this change lets Almond keep supporting Scala 2.12.

by @alexarchambault in https://github.com/almond-sh/almond/pull/1728, https://github.com/almond-sh/almond/pull/1726

## Other fixes and enhancements

Fix PC thread issues (#1712)

* Don't read symbol infos off the presentation compiler thread in inspect

ScalaInterpreterInspections.inspect runs on the message-handler thread and
reads scalac symbol infos from there in three places. Each trips
Global.assertCorrectThread, and because the resulting AssertionError is not
NonFatal it escapes inspect and terminates the kernel JVM (taking the
SparkContext with it, in a Spark notebook). typeOfTree already does this
correctly via askForResponse; the other reads now follow it.

- tree.toString, the fallback when typeOfTree yields nothing, goes through
  symName -> isErroneous -> Symbol.info. Produce that fallback inside
  typeOfTree's own askForResponse block instead. This is the path that
  reproduces on demand: a cell containing an import, hovered while another
  cell executes, kills 0.14.5 after ~24 inspect_requests.
- Docstrings.documentation invokes the parents thunk later, from
  parentDocumentation, so symbol.allOverriddenSymbols ran off-thread.
  Compute it, and sym, on the PC thread and pass a thunk over the result.
- Widen the catch around the docstring lookup from InvalidSymbolException to
  Throwable: a failed docstring lookup should cost an inspection, not the
  kernel.

Also null-check tree.tpe in typeOfTree. askTypeAt can hand back an untyped
tree while a background compile is in flight, and tree.tpe.widen then NPEs.

Verified against 2.12.18 with a client that fires inspect_request while cells
execute: 144 requests at one per 300ms and 7060 at full rate both complete with
no assertions and no kernel exit, where 0.14.5 dies after 24 and ~2000
respectively.

Answer kernel info on Control, and inspect with a text alternative (#1713)

* Answer kernel_info_request on Control, and inspect with a text/plain alternative

Two independent fixes for VS Code clients of the kernel.

Protocol 5.5 added kernel_info_request on the control channel, where it is "the
same kernel info message as that received on the Shell channel", and the VS Code
Jupyter extension sends it there. Only the shell channel was handled, so those
requests were logged as "Ignoring unhandled message on Control" and never
answered. The new handler skips the `blocking` helper, so it publishes no
busy/idle status and answers while a cell is executing.

Separately, the Scala 2 inspect implementation replied with text/html only. The
VS Code Jupyter PowerToys Contextual Help panel requires text/plain to be
present in the reply data and otherwise shows the user "No response from
kernel"; JupyterLab renders the HTML, which is why this only showed up in VS
Code. The plain-text alternative is built from the same type string and
docstring the HTML uses.

fix(morph): close dialogs properly when removing `open` attribute (#4739)

Morphing a `<dialog>` opened via `showModal()` would call `removeAttribute('open')` directly, leaving the dialog in the browser's top layer and making the page permanently inert. Now calls `dialog.close()` instead, which properly exits the top layer.

Fix x-ref crash during child-element morph (#4748)

Wrap x-ref's inline handler with skipDuringClone() to prevent TypeError
when morph runs on a child element (not the x-data root). During morph,
cloneNode() runs directives on detached elements where closestRoot()
returns undefined. Refs re-register on live DOM via MutationObserver.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix $watch oldValue for objects being identical to new value (#4749)

When deep-watching objects, oldValue and value were the same reference,
so by callback time oldValue reflected the already-mutated state.

Fix: reuse the JSON.stringify result already computed for deep tracking,
store it, and JSON.parse it back as oldValue when the callback fires.
Zero additional stringify calls — only a JSON.parse when the callback
actually fires.

Closes #3293
Related: #4406, #3046, #3617

Fix `x-model.blur` crash when input is removed from a form (#4783)

The cleanup callback for `x-model.blur`'s pending model update registration
accessed `el.form` without guarding against null. When an input is removed
from the DOM (e.g. during Livewire morph), `el.form` becomes null because
the element is no longer associated with a form, causing a TypeError.

Capture the form reference at registration time and add a null guard in the
cleanup callback.

310735644.body:
## What's Changed
* Add stale workflow for inactive issues and PRs by @amalshaji in https://github.com/amalshaji/portr/pull/235
* Redesign client dashboard v2 with terminal-inspired UI by @amalshaji in https://github.com/amalshaji/portr/pull/239


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/amalshaji/portr/compare/v1.0.5...v1.0.8

commits.message: chore: add stale issue workflow (#235)

Redesign client dashboard v2 with terminal-inspired UI (#239)

* Redesign client dashboard v2 with terminal-inspired UI

- Full terminal aesthetic: Fragment Mono, off-white #fafaf7, electric-green accent, grid backdrop
- Home page: stats row, connections table with live/idle/closed status, scrollable list (page no longer scrolls)
- Tunnel page: split-pane inspector with sidebar request list and 6-tab detail pane (Headers, Query, Request body, Response body, Cookies, Raw)
- Edit & replay dialog restyled with method chips, terminal inputs and buttons
- Server unavailable banner restyled to match terminal palette
- No-content empty state improved with icon and contextual label
- Cmd/Ctrl+K focuses sidebar search input
- Backend: capture DurationMs, BytesIn, BytesOut, Protocol on each proxied request (GORM AutoMigrate handles schema)
- Frontend types updated with optional duration/bytes/protocol fields

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix server unavailable banner spacing on detail page

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix goreleaser dirty state from rebuilt client dashboard assets

Bump config to version 2 and add dirty_ignore for the dist directory —
CI rebuilds the dashboard before release, producing new content-hash
filenames that differ from the committed ones.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix goreleaser dirty state check for CI dashboard build

The release workflow builds the dashboard before goreleaser runs,
which produces new content-hash asset filenames and leaves the tree
dirty. Use --skip=validate (goreleaser's documented fix for this) and
remove the invalid git.dirty_ignore field added in the previous commit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
